````markdown
# kaggle-code-agent Milestones

Status: M0–M9 done; M9.2 ✓ done (/save-log operator-tooling skill); M10 in planning (notebook-submission regression — Petals to the Metal)  
Created: 2026-05-16  
Scope: hybrid human + AI code competition platform

## Product thesis

`kaggle-code-agent` is a platform for human users to collaborate with AI code agents on code competitions and authorized challenge environments.

Initial focus: Kaggle competitions.  
Later extensions: authorized CTF/lab challenges, Devpost, hackathons, benchmark competitions, and other policy-scoped coding contests.

The platform should help a human user:

- discuss ideas and strategies;
- research competition rules, data, notebooks, papers, discussions, and baseline approaches;
- create, modify, test, and iterate code;
- track experiments, artifacts, results, submissions, and analysis;
- require human approval for external side effects such as Kaggle submissions or remote kernel pushes;
- summarize learnings and produce final writeups.

## Source of truth

**GitHub repo + Claude Code + CI + Supabase migrations.**

All product source code, migrations, tests, architecture decisions, and task specs live in this repository. AI tools do not share hidden memory reliably across sessions or products. Claude Code is the primary development environment for all layers: CLI, backend, UI shell, and worker.

Lovable may be used for visual prototyping or landing-page mockups only. It is not the source of truth for schema, migrations, agent runners, or any backend logic.

## Terminology: two meanings of "code agent"

This project uses two related but distinct agent concepts.

### 1. Platform-development coding agents

These are external AI tools used to build this repository.

Examples:

- Claude Code CLI / VS Code / Desktop / Web (primary);
- ChatGPT Pro / Cursor (supplementary);
- GitHub Actions / Claude Code Web / Routines for cloud automation.

Role:

- write and review this product's source code;
- update docs, tasks, tests, and architecture decisions;
- run local tests and CI repair loops;
- open branches/PRs under human supervision.

Important rule: these tools do not share hidden memory reliably. GitHub repository files are the durable source of truth.

### 2. Runtime competition code agents

These are agents launched by the finished platform to help a human user compete.

Initial runtime direction:

- Claude Agent SDK as the first core worker/harness;
- isolated workspace/container per job;
- Python/notebook-first for Kaggle;
- TypeScript/Python service boundary depending on platform vs worker needs;
- future model router for Claude, GPT-style models, local vLLM/Ollama models, and specialized tools.

Runtime agents must operate under competition-specific policy, sandboxing, budget limits, approval gates, and audit logging.

## Architecture north star

```text
Human user / future UI
        ↓
TypeScript-first platform/control plane
  - project/session/job/task queue
  - policy and approval gates
  - discussion/research/analysis records
  - experiment/run/submission/artifact records
  - model router configuration
        ↓
Worker layer
  - Python-first Kaggle workers
  - Claude Agent SDK runtime sessions
  - notebooks/scripts/tools/kca wrappers
  - Playwright/browser/research tools
  - sandboxed execution and evaluation
        ↓
External systems
  - GitHub repo / branches / PRs
  - Supabase DB/storage/edge functions later
  - Kaggle API/CLI, only with approval for remote side effects
  - authorized CTF/lab/hackathon platforms under explicit policy
```

## Cross-cutting rules

- GitHub repo files are the project memory and source of truth.
- Each agent task gets a branch/worktree/PR when it modifies code.
- Main branch remains stable and protected.
- Do not allow multiple AI sessions to edit the same branch/files at the same time.
- No secrets in repo, prompts, logs, artifacts, or screenshots.
- Kaggle submissions, kernel pushes, dataset uploads, and other remote side effects require explicit human approval.
- CTF/lab work must be local/sandboxed or explicitly authorized.
- Every task prompt should include acceptance criteria and a stop condition.
- Every worker loop should have budget, turn, time, and side-effect limits.
- Tests and local validation should run before external submission.

## Milestone final-review protocol

After every milestone final review, before marking done:

1. Update `PROJECT_STATE.md` — set current milestone, summarize open decisions, and record any new known blockers.
2. Update `README.md` current milestone section to name the new active milestone and goal.
3. Update `docs/milestones.md` — mark the finished milestone `✓ done`, add a one-line summary of what landed, and note any follow-ups carried forward.
4. Write `docs/handoffs/m{x}-handoff.md` — a per-milestone, ready-to-paste context prompt for the next AI tool / session that will start M{x+1}. Use `docs/handoff-prompt.md` as the canonical template; populate the "State at handoff", "Read these files first", and "Current task" sections from the M{x} final review and the M{x+1} entry in this file. The generic `docs/handoff-prompt.md` stays as the template; the per-milestone instances live under `docs/handoffs/`.

## M6: multi-agent review + OTEL telemetry + local-model layer ✓ done

Goal: harden the M3–M5 worker with an independent reviewer agent, end-to-end
OpenTelemetry tracing, and a local-model layer that routes log-triage /
summarisation jobs to user-owned GPU hosts before paying for cloud tokens.

Planned capabilities:

- Reviewer agent (sync mode) fires before high-stakes ops
  (`kaggle_submit`, `supabase_migrate`, `git_force_push`, `dataset_upload`,
  `delete_artifact`). Verdict `approve | reject | abstain` lands in a new
  `agent_reviews` table; `approve` satisfies the matching approval gate
  without human intervention, `reject` escalates (default) or fails the
  job, `abstain` falls through to the existing human-decisions flow.
- Local-model layer (`src/worker/local_model.py`) talks to vLLM / Ollama
  endpoints on the user's GPU hosts (`snorlax` RTX 4090, `may` RTX 3090)
  via OpenAI-compatible HTTP. Numbered-slot env config
  (`KCA_LOCAL_ENDPOINT_<n>_*`), priority ordering, a TTL-cached probe, and
  a `KCA_LOCAL_FALLBACK_MODEL` cloud fallback.
- New job types `log_triage` and `summarise` route to the local layer by
  default; `kca local probe / pick / triage` surfaces endpoint state.
- OTEL instrumentation per ADR-0007 with three exporters: stderr (dev),
  SQLite (`.agent/telemetry.sqlite`), and Supabase
  (`agent_telemetry_spans`). Spans cover job / turn / tool / reviewer /
  local-probe.
- TC-3 Spaceship Titanic exercises the reviewer-gate path end-to-end on a
  binary-classification submission flow.

Exit criteria: all met. See `docs/m6-final-review.md`.

## M7: KCA CLI architecture — command / skill / tool / job / permission policy ✓ done

_Shipped 2026-05-21: four-layer CLI scaffold (command/skill/tool/job), skill loader, tool registry (16 tools), three permission profiles, `kca skill list/show/run` + `kca tool list/audit/doctor`, four seed skills, audit JSONL, 15 smoke tests, and `docs/architecture/kca-cli-architecture.md`. 28/28 exit checks PASS — see `docs/m7-final-review.md`._

Goal: implement the full KCA command/skill/tool/job architecture so the platform
has a stable, inspectable CLI that can drive agent workflows, replace ad-hoc
`python tools/kca/kca.py` calls, and enforce structured permission decisions.

This is distinct from the product UI shell (M8): M7 is operator/developer-facing
and headless. The UI in M8 will call into the same CLI/API surface.

See `docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-21-r1.md` §1–3 for full design rationale.

### Four-layer model

| Layer | Description |
|---|---|
| **Command** | Deterministic CLI/API entry points for operators (`kca job run`, `kca decision approve`). |
| **Skill** | Agent-facing workflow recipes stored under `.kca/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter. Callable via `kca skill run <name>` or slash-style invocation. |
| **Tool** | Executable actions with input/output schema, timeout, permission label, sandbox metadata, and audit logging. |
| **Job** | Durable records that run a skill through the agent loop with budget, turn, cost, runtime limits, and decision gates. |

### M7 task sequence

| Task | Description | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| M7-T000 | Audit + repair `.github/workflows/` — fix failing CI checks, add no-db + lint jobs | — |
| M7-T001 | Skill loader: read `.kca/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter; argument substitution | — |
| M7-T002 | Command registry: register KCA CLI subcommands declaratively | T001 |
| M7-T003 | Tool registry: tool metadata, approval policy labels, sandbox metadata | T001 |
| M7-T004 | Permission policy layer: allow/ask/deny resolution with structured JSON policy records | T003 |
| M7-T005 | Slash-style invocation: `kca skill run <name> [args] [--dry-run]` shows permissions + rendered prompt | T001, T004 |
| M7-T006 | Audit logging: record every tool execution in `agent_job_events` with policy decision | T004 |
| M7-T007 | Seed `.kca/skills/` with `run-milestone`, `triage-log`, `prepare-submission`, `review-pr` | T001 |
| M7-T008 | `tests/test_m7_smoke.py`: skill parsing, arg substitution, permission resolution, command registry, decision gates | T001–T006 |
| M7-T009 | Documentation: `docs/architecture/kca-cli-architecture.md` explaining Commands vs Skills vs Tools vs Jobs | all |
| M7-T010 | M7 exit criteria validation + `docs/m7-final-review.md` | all |

### Permission policy design

Runtime agent permissions are data, not ad-hoc prompts:

```json
{
  "operation": "kaggle.submit",
  "default_decision": "ask",
  "reason": "External competition submission",
  "allowed_in_modes": ["human-approved", "competition-finalization"],
  "audit_required": true
}
```

Allow by default: edit workspace files, run tests/benchmark, create artifacts,
summarize logs, call LiteLLM/local models, create branch, commit, create PR.

Decision gate: submit to Kaggle, merge PR, publish dataset/kernel, apply
remote Supabase migration, spend above budget threshold, change model tier,
change competition direction/objective.

Deny: read secrets, write outside workspace, sudo/root, rm outside workspace,
drop database/schema, force push, network exfiltration.

### Recommended directory layout

```text
.kca/
  skills/
    run-milestone/SKILL.md
    triage-log/SKILL.md
    prepare-submission/SKILL.md
    review-pr/SKILL.md
  tools/tools.yaml
  permissions/
    default.yaml
    permissive-dev.yaml
    competition-runner.yaml

tools/kca/
  kca.py
  commands/
    job.py  skill.py  tool.py  decision.py
    workspace.py  kaggle.py  supabase.py
  agent/
    runner.py  skill_loader.py  tool_executor.py
    permission_policy.py  audit.py
```

Exit criteria:

- `kca skill list` shows available skills from `.kca/skills/`.
- `kca skill show <name>` prints parsed metadata and body.
- `kca skill run <name> ... --dry-run` prints planned tool permissions and rendered prompt without executing.
- Permission policy resolves allow/ask/deny for any (operation, mode) pair.
- Audit log records every tool execution with policy decision.
- `.github/workflows/` CI passes on main branch (no-db + lint at minimum).
- `tests/test_m7_smoke.py` passes without API keys or DB.
- Documentation explains Commands vs Skills vs Tools vs Jobs.
````

````markdown
# M10 — Loop Prompts

_Live end-to-end Kaggle regression test on
[Petals to the Metal — Flower Classification on TPU](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/tpu-getting-started)._
_For sequential, partly autonomous execution on Arch Linux._
_Prerequisite: M9 exit confirmed (live LB recorded, dry-run e2e green; see `docs/m9-final-review.md`)._
_Shared rules: every Loop Prompt below MUST follow `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` (sequencing, no real Kaggle/Anthropic outside designated approval paths, DB DSN + sandbox bypass, **per-milestone worktree by default**, secret denylist)._

---

## M10 at a glance

M10 is the **second end-to-end live Kaggle regression** for this platform, and
the first to exercise the **notebook-submission / kernel-push** path.
M9 validated the CSV-submission path (`kca kaggle submit` →
`kaggle competitions submit`) on Spaceship Titanic. M10 validates the
notebook-submission path (`kca kaggle push` → `kaggle kernels push` →
kernel run → public LB) on Petals to the Metal — Flower Classification on TPU
(`tpu-getting-started`).

Petals to the Metal is "Getting Started" tier: multi-class image
classification over 104 flower species, public leaderboard, no cash prize,
safe for repeated dry-run iteration and a single real kernel push under
explicit human approval. TPU is optional — Kaggle accepts GPU-backed
notebooks for this competition too — so the baseline can run locally
and only the kernel runner needs Kaggle's hardware.

M10 is **not** a leaderboard-chasing milestone. The acceptance criterion is
that the kernel-push loop *runs end-to-end correctly under the approval
gates*, not that the LB score is high. The CV / holdout thresholds in
`docs/milestones.md` §M10 are sanity guards, not targets.

Direct entry into M10 is blocked until **all** are true:

- M9 is merged on main (`docs/m9-final-review.md` exists and reports PASS).
- Issue #11 (dotenv-leak / Kaggle leaderboard pollution) is merged on main —
  hard pre-req for **M10-T007** so the new dry-run e2e test cannot leak
  into the `tpu-getting-started` leaderboard the same way M9 leaked into
  Spaceship Titanic. M10-T000 through M10-T006 may proceed in parallel
  with #11 work; only T007 is gated on it.
- The local Supabase container is running and the M9 DB rows (M9-T002 /
  M9-T004 / M9-T005) are reachable (M10-T006 references the M9 baseline
  for cross-milestone regression sanity).

### What's in scope

| Capability | Owned by | M10 touches |
|---|---|---|
| Kaggle credentials handling | `env.example`, `.env`, `KAGGLE_USERNAME`/`KAGGLE_KEY` | T000 — verifies env without printing secrets; gates push on presence |
| Competition register + workspace | `tools/kca/competition.py` (`register`, `clone`, `list`, `info`) | T000 / T001 |
| Data discovery for non-CSV competitions | `tools/kca/kg.py` (existing `cmd_download` / `cmd_verify` if extended) + a new manifest shape | T001 — notebook competitions read TFRecord-style data from Kaggle-hosted GCS at kernel runtime; the local manifest records `kaggle competitions files` output, not file checksums |
| Notebook authoring + percent-format round-trip | `kg-nb` skill (`tools/kca/notebook.py` or equivalent) | T002 / T007 |
| Worker loop (research → baseline → local CV → notebook artifact) | `src/worker/` + `tools/kca/run.py` + skills | T002 |
| Reviewer gate before kernel push | `src/worker/reviewer.py` + `services/decision_api/` + UI Approval Inbox (under `target_op="kernel_push"`) | T003 |
| Real Kaggle kernel push (under approval) | `tools/kca/kg.py::cmd_push` + `kaggle kernels push` + kernel-run polling | T004 — single real call |
| Second experiment (alt backbone / augmentation) | same worker, second run | T005 |
| Regression assertions | `tests/test_m10_e2e.py` + `runs` table + `submissions` table | T006 / T007 |

- Running Kaggle submit / kernel push / dataset upload / model upload outside
  T004's single approved kernel-push call.

  don't expand scope. Issue #11 is the only hard pre-req (see entry gates).

  uses the existing `kca` surface (`competition`, `kaggle`, `run`,
  `research`, `review`, `decisions`, `skill`) without inventing new ones.
  Internal helpers (e.g. kernel-run polling) may be added under
  `tools/kca/kg.py` as private functions if `cmd_push` doesn't already
  cover them, but no new top-level subcommand surface.

## GitHub issue / label workflow for M10

Each M10 task is filed as a GitHub issue using the `feature-work.yml` form,
labelled per task type. Issue #12 is the canonical M10 proposal /
decision-confirmation record; individual task issues link back to it.

| Task | Issue labels at file time | Labels added by triage | Labels at merge |
|---|---|---|---|
| M10-T000 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:kaggle`, `area:config`, `area:security` | `ai:ready` (after AC + owner) | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M10-T001 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:kaggle` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M10-T002 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:worker`, `area:kaggle` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M10-T003 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:worker`, `area:supabase`, `area:ui` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M10-T004 | `type:feature`, `ai:blocked`, `policy:approval-required`, `decision:needed`, `area:kaggle`, `priority:P0` | `decision:confirmed` + `ai:ready` only after human comment "approved to push" | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M10-T005 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:worker`, `area:kaggle` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M10-T006 | `type:test-gap`, `ai:triage`, `area:testing` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M10-T007 | `type:test-gap`, `ai:triage`, `area:testing`, `area:ci` | `ai:ready` only after issue #11 is closed | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M10-T008 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:release`, `area:docs` | `ai:ready` after T000–T007 closed | `ai:implementing` → close |

T004 is the only task that starts `ai:blocked` and requires a
`decision:confirmed` comment with an explicit "approved to push" record
before triage may promote it to `ai:ready`. This is enforced by the
`github-issue-triage` agent rules in `.claude/skills/github-issue-triage/`.

T007 is the only task gated on closing a separate issue (#11). The
triage agent should refuse to promote T007 to `ai:ready` while
`gh issue view 11 --json state` returns `"OPEN"`.

The PR for each task uses `.github/pull_request_template.md`. The
"Remote side effects" section is load-bearing: T004's PR is the ONLY
M10 PR that may check the "Live Kaggle call" box, and must link the
approval comment from the closing issue.

## Approval gates (summary)

| Gate | When it fires | Where the approval is recorded | Who can approve |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kernel_push` | Worker stages a notebook + kernel-metadata.json and calls into `tools/kca/kg.py::cmd_push` | `human_decisions` row + comment on the closing GitHub issue | Project owner / reviewer named on the issue |
| `kaggle_submit` | Not used in M10 (would be a second-submission path; out of scope) | n/a | n/a |
| `dataset_upload` | Not used in M10 | n/a | n/a |
| `model_upload` | Not used in M10 | n/a | n/a |

The Kaggle approval flow inside M10 is:

```
worker stages notebook + kernel-metadata.json
  → reviewer-gate writes agent_reviews row + agent_job_events
    (target_op="kernel_push")
  → decision_api surfaces pending decision (POST /decisions queued; UI
    reads via supabase-js until issue #15 lands GET /decisions)
  → UI Approval Inbox renders pending decision
  → human approves via UI (POST /decisions/<id>/approve) OR
    `kca decisions approve --id <id>`
  → human comments "approved to push" on the closing issue
  → triage agent promotes issue to `decision:confirmed` + `ai:ready`
  → M10-T004 Loop Prompt runs ONE `kca kaggle push`
  → poll kaggle kernels status until non-running
  → LB score recorded; submissions row written with kernel-run linkage
  → PR opens with the approval comment linked
```

A second real Kaggle push inside M10 is **out of scope**. If a
follow-up experiment in M10-T005 turns out to need its own LB score,
file it as a new M11+ issue and gate it the same way.

## Rollback / stop criteria

Stop the milestone — do **not** advance to the next Loop Prompt — if any of
these is true:

- A real Kaggle kernel push returns an error from Kaggle (rate limit,
  bad notebook metadata, rules violation). The fix path is local:
  regenerate the notebook + kernel metadata and re-request approval;
  do NOT silently retry.
- The reviewer gate (M10-T003) fails to fire when it should, or fires
  when it shouldn't.
- Any `policy:approval-required` issue advances without the corresponding
  `decision:confirmed` label and comment.
- Any test in the validation suite regresses from green to red.
- The DSN, credentials, or `.env*` are accidentally printed in any log,
  audit row, or PR. Stop and rotate the credential immediately.
- Local CV / holdout scores diverge from the M10-T006 thresholds in a
  way that suggests a leakage bug (e.g. holdout near 1.0). Investigate
  before pushing.
- Issue #11 is reopened mid-milestone with evidence that the leak
  re-emerged. Halt T007 work until #11 is green again.

If M10 needs a new architectural decision (e.g. submission-format
auto-selection, a new artifact-storage shape for notebook payloads, a
TPU-specific resource model), **pause and ask** — those are M11+ /
issue #7 / issue #8 decisions, not M10 expansion. Open an ADR draft in
`docs/adr/` and stop the milestone there.
````

````markdown
# Milestone Loop Protocol

_Shared rules that apply to every milestone Loop Prompt (M0+) unless a
milestone explicitly overrides one._

Each `docs/m*-loop-prompts.md` should reference this file once at the top
rather than duplicating the rules per prompt.

---

## 1. Sequencing

- Loop Prompts within a milestone MUST execute in order.
- Each prompt's **acceptance checks MUST pass** before moving to the next.
- On failure: fix the specific issue and **retry that prompt only**; do
  not skip ahead and do not redo prompts that already passed.

## 2. External systems and side effects

- Do NOT call the **real Anthropic API or Kaggle API** outside of paths
  the milestone explicitly designates as live; default to `--dry-run`.
- Do NOT run real **Kaggle submit / kernel push / dataset upload /
  model upload** unless the milestone explicitly requests it AND a
  human-approval record exists.
- Do NOT change **production Supabase**.

## 3. Database validation

- Use `SUPABASE_DB_URL=postgresql://postgres:s3cr3t@172.21.0.4:5432/postgres`
  — the `supabase-db` container on the local Docker network.
- Container IPs change on `docker compose down/up`; refresh with:
  ```bash
  docker inspect supabase-db \
    --format '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}'
  ```
- DB calls and LAN-host calls require `dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true`.
  Cloud LLM calls stay **inside** the sandbox.

## 4. Reporting

- Report **PASS / FAIL / SKIP** inline for each prompt's verification
  step.
- At milestone end, write the milestone's defined **Closeout format**
  (see each milestone's last Loop Prompt for the exact fields).

## 5. Git / GitHub — worktree mode

This project executes each milestone inside a dedicated **git worktree**
branched off `main`.

- **Mid-milestone, mid-prompt:** do not `git commit` or `git push`
  unless the individual task spec explicitly says so. Stage with
  `git add` and surface diffs in the inline report.
- **At milestone end** — once every Loop Prompt has PASSed and the
  milestone's Closeout has been written — Claude Code SHOULD:
  1. `git add` only the files listed in the Closeout's "files changed"
     section (or its equivalent).
  2. `git commit` using either:
     - one squash commit per milestone, OR
     - one commit per Loop Prompt,
     depending on the milestone's preference. The default is **one
     commit per Loop Prompt**, with the milestone's final review as the
     last commit.
  3. `git push` the worktree's branch to the remote.
  4. `gh pr create` against `main` using the milestone's
     `docs/m{N}-final-review.md` as the PR body.

- The following **still require explicit human approval** at any time:
  - `git push --force` (any branch)
  - `gh pr merge` (any PR)
  - any push to `main` directly
  - any `gh label create/edit/delete`, `gh issue edit/comment`,
    `gh pr edit/comment` against issues or PRs **not** owned by this
    milestone

- If the milestone's task spec or scope says
  "do not commit / push / open PRs", that override **wins** — typically
  used for planning-only or evidence-only milestones.

## 6. Secrets and forbidden reads

These are always denied, regardless of milestone:

- `.env*`
- `**/kaggle.json`, `~/.kaggle/kaggle.json`
- `~/.ssh/id_rsa`, `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`, any private key contents
- `~/.aws/**`, `~/.config/gcloud/**`
- `secrets/**`

Shell commands that would surface the above (`cat`, `grep`, `head`,
`tail`, `less`, `more`, file uploads) over these paths are blocked at
the hook layer.

---

## How a milestone references this file

In each Loop Prompt block, instead of repeating the rules above, include
one line near the top:

```
Follow: docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md
```

A milestone's `docs/m{N}-loop-prompts.md` should still spell out:

- the milestone's own scope, non-goals, and task list;
- per-Loop-Prompt read lists, scope, acceptance criteria;
- any **override** of a default in this file (e.g. a planning-only
  milestone overriding the worktree commit/push behavior).

---

## 7. Discovery / Debate Gate

_Added by M9.4. Additive only — §1–§6 above are unchanged._

Some tasks are large enough that "implement first, debate later"
loses load-bearing requirements (the canonical failure: `tools/legacy/kkr.py`
migration missing multi-Kaggle-account / owner / env semantics; see
`docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-24-r3.md` §6). The Discovery / Debate Gate
runs three role-isolated subagents — `legacy-archaeologist`,
`requirements-skeptic`, `design-red-team` — **before** any
implementation work begins.

The gate is **mandatory** for any task whose spec is tagged `arch:`
(introduces / revises an architectural primitive) or
`legacy-migration:` (migrates / rewrites / replaces a legacy artefact).
Routine tasks (bug fixes, doc edits, dependency bumps, small
refactors) do not trigger the gate.

When the gate fires, the executing session MUST:

1. Invoke `legacy-archaeologist` first if the task touches any
   legacy artefact (skip allowed only for greenfield `arch:` tasks,
   with explicit note in the closeout).
2. Invoke `requirements-skeptic` next.
3. Invoke `design-red-team` last.
4. Attach all three reports to the task closeout under
   `docs/evidence/<milestone>/<task>/discovery/`.
5. Verify all three canonical acceptance lines (defined in
   `docs/architecture/discovery-debate-gate.md`) byte-for-byte
   against the reports. A missing acceptance line is a task FAIL.

Full template, tag-placement options, and the verbatim acceptance
lines live in `docs/architecture/discovery-debate-gate.md`. The
orchestration skill `.claude/skills/design-archaeology/SKILL.md`
(owned by M9.3) is the inline alternative when the task is small
enough not to warrant separate subagents; the agent path and the
skill path emit compatible output shapes by design.

M9.4 enforces the gate via task-spec acceptance criteria and this
section's wording, **not** via hook-level denials. Hook-based
enforcement is a deferred follow-up; file a separate issue if you
want it built.
````

```markdown
# Kaggle Code Agent — Project State

_Last updated: 2026-05-26 (M9.4 close)_

## Product intent
Build a hybrid human + AI competition engineering workbench. The first target is Kaggle-style competitions, with future support for authorized CTF/lab challenges. The system should research, discuss ideas with humans, edit code, run tests/evaluations, analyze results, iterate, and prepare submissions under human-approved guardrails.

## Chosen architecture direction
- Hybrid architecture.
- Claude Code Desktop/CLI for interactive project development and dogfooding (primary development tool for all layers).
- Claude Agent SDK for the production coding worker.
- Python-first worker for Kaggle/ML/CTF execution.
- TypeScript/Supabase control plane and UI shell (developed in Claude Code, not Lovable).
- GitHub + Claude Code + CI + Supabase migrations are the source of truth. All decisions, architecture, task specs, and safety rules live in repo files.
- Supabase is the control plane and audit database, not the primary code execution environment.

## Current MVP boundary
1. Local-first repository workflow with `CLAUDE.md`, skills, hooks, subagents, and GitHub.
2. Supabase schema for projects, sessions, jobs, messages, research notes, experiments, runs, submissions, artifacts, approvals, and `agent_tool_audit` (M8).
3. Kaggle baseline loop: understand competition, create validation, run baseline, record metrics, iterate, prepare submission.
4. Browser/research loop: fetch pages, summarize sources, track trust and citations.
5. Multi-agent reviewer gate + OTEL telemetry + local GPU model layer.
6. Authorized CTF sandbox loop only for explicit challenge environments.
7. Operator-facing UI: Dashboard, Run Timeline (OTEL swim-lane), Experiments, Research, Approval Inbox + Decision Gate, Artifact Browser.

## Human approval gates
Require approval for:
- Kaggle competition submissions.
- Kaggle kernel/notebook pushes.
- Any remote write operation.
- Any operation touching credentials, secrets, or account settings.
- Any CTF action outside a declared sandbox/challenge scope.
- PR merges (create is allowed, merge requires approval).

Mutations from the UI flow through `services/decision_api/` (FastAPI) →
`tools/kca/decisions.py` → DB. The browser bundle never holds a
Supabase service-role key. The M7 permission policy resolution stays
authoritative.
```

````markdown
# M9 — Loop Prompts

_Live end-to-end Kaggle regression test on
[Spaceship Titanic](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/spaceship-titanic/overview)._
_For sequential, partly autonomous execution on Arch Linux._
_Prerequisite: M8.5 exit confirmed (CI green + GitHub Issues/PR/labels interface in place; see `docs/m8_5-final-review.md`)._
_Shared rules: every Loop Prompt below MUST follow `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` (sequencing, no real Kaggle/Anthropic outside designated approval paths, DB DSN + sandbox bypass, worktree commit/push/PR at milestone end, secret denylist)._

---

## M9 at a glance

M9 is the **first end-to-end live Kaggle regression** for this platform. It
exercises the M3 worker, M5 research path, M6 reviewer + telemetry, the M7
permission policy, and the M8 decision_api + UI shell against a real Kaggle
competition. The competition is Spaceship Titanic — binary classification,
public leaderboard, no cash prize, safe for repeated dry-run iteration and a
single real submission under an explicit human-approval gate.

M9 is **not** a leaderboard-chasing milestone. The acceptance criterion is
that the loop *runs end-to-end correctly under the approval gates*, not that
the LB score is high. The CV thresholds in `docs/milestones.md` §M9 are
sanity guards, not targets.

Direct entry into M9 is blocked until **all** are true:

- M8.5-T001 (CI repair) is merged on main.
- M8.5-T002 (engineering practice + GitHub interface) is merged on main and
  `.github/labels.yml` has been synced to `origin` (33 labels visible via
  `gh label list`).
- `scripts/sync_labels.py --dry-run` reports `0 update`.
- `docs/m8_5-final-review.md` exists and reports PASS.

### What's in scope

| Capability | Owned by | M9 touches |
|---|---|---|
| Kaggle credentials handling | `env.example`, `.env`, `KAGGLE_USERNAME`/`KAGGLE_KEY` | T000 — verifies env without printing secrets; gates submit on presence |
| Competition register + workspace | `tools/kca/competition.py` (`register`, `clone`, `list`, `info`) | T000 / T001 |
| Data download + checksum | `tools/kca/kg.py::cmd_download`, `cmd_verify` (sha256 manifest already implemented in M5) | T001 |
| Worker loop (research → baseline → CV → submission file) | `src/worker/` + `tools/kca/run.py` + skills | T002 |
| Reviewer gate before submit | `src/worker/reviewer.py` + `services/decision_api/` + UI Approval Inbox | T003 |
| Real Kaggle submit (under approval) | `tools/kca/kg.py::cmd_submit` + `kaggle competitions submit` | T004 — single real call |
| Second experiment (HGB / feature engineering) | same worker, second run | T005 |
| Regression assertions | `tests/test_m9_e2e.py` + `runs` table | T006 / T007 |
| GitHub issue / label workflow | `.github/labels.yml`, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`, `.github/pull_request_template.md`, `policy:approval-required` | every task — work order issue per task |
| Final review | `milestone-final-review` skill + `worktree-milestone-pr` skill | T008 |

### What's NOT in scope

- Running Kaggle submit / kernel push / dataset upload / model upload outside
  T004's single approved call.
- Changing production Supabase.
- Implementing M9 follow-ups from M8 (multi-user auth, artifact preview via
  signed URLs, live-DB CI on fork PRs, OTEL collector wiring). Those are
  separate milestones; if M9 surfaces blockers for them, file follow-up
  issues — don't expand scope.
- Adding new CLI subcommands. M9 uses the existing `kca` surface
  (`competition`, `kaggle`, `run`, `research`, `review`, `decisions`,
  `skill`) without inventing new ones.
- Runtime submission-format detection. KCA's `kca kaggle submit` is
  format-agnostic: it passes `--file` straight to `kaggle competitions
  submit`, and Kaggle validates server-side. **M9 assumes
  `submission.csv` because Spaceship Titanic is a CSV competition.** Other
  competition shapes (code-competition notebooks → `kca kaggle push`;
  `submission.zip`; JSON; etc.) need different paths that KCA does not
  yet auto-select. Tracked as a separate `area:kaggle` / `type:feature`
  follow-up — see M9-T002's "Submission-format note" for context.

DB / sandbox details: see `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` §3 — the local
`supabase-db` container (`postgresql://postgres:s3cr3t@172.21.0.4:5432/postgres`)
needs `dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true`.
````

```markdown
# M10-T000: Kaggle credentials + competition registration (`tpu-getting-started`)

## Milestone
M10: live end-to-end regression test — Petals to the Metal (notebook-submission / kernel-push path).

## Goal
Confirm the agent can read Kaggle credentials without exposing them, run
READ_ONLY Kaggle calls against the kernel-runner path, and register
`tpu-getting-started` (Petals to the Metal) in the local control plane.
No real push, no submission, no dataset / model upload.

This task assumes **M9 is merged on main** (`docs/m9-final-review.md`
reports PASS) and that the M9-T000 deviation (AC #1 satisfied via
`kaggle.api.config_values` rather than the literal python-dotenv check)
is honoured here too.

## Read first

1. `PROJECT_STATE.md`
2. `AGENTS.md`
3. `CLAUDE.md`
4. `docs/milestones.md` §M10
5. `docs/engineering-practice.md`
6. `docs/m9-final-review.md` (M9-T000 deviation)
7. `docs/handoffs/m9-handoff.md`
8. `env.example`
9. `tools/kca/competition.py`
10. `tools/kca/kg.py` — `cmd_list`, `cmd_watch`, `cmd_fetch`, `cmd_push` (header / args only — do NOT call), `add_parsers`
11. `.claude/settings.json` — verify Kaggle `submit/push/upload/datasets`
    are on `ask`
12. `.claude/hooks/guard_tool.py` — verify `kaggle.json` / `.env` reads
    are denied

## Scope

1. Verify Kaggle credentials are reachable WITHOUT printing them. Two
   accepted paths:
   - Preferred: `python -c "from dotenv import load_dotenv; import os; load_dotenv(); print(bool(os.environ.get('KAGGLE_USERNAME')), bool(os.environ.get('KAGGLE_KEY')))"` prints `True True`.
   - Equivalent (per M9-T000 deviation): `python -c "from kaggle import api; api.authenticate(); cv = api.config_values; print(bool(cv.get('username')), bool(cv.get('key')))"` prints `True True`.
   Either is acceptable; the deviation exists because in some sandboxed
   views `.env` is bind-mounted to `/dev/null`. Booleans only — never
   the values.
2. Run `kca kaggle list --json` (READ_ONLY) to confirm credentials work.
   Capture only the count or slug presence, never the raw response.
3. Run `kaggle competitions files -c tpu-getting-started` (READ_ONLY) to
```

````markdown
# M10-T007: `tests/test_m10_e2e.py` dry-run end-to-end smoke

## Milestone
M10: live end-to-end regression test — Petals to the Metal.

## Goal
Add `tests/test_m10_e2e.py` that exercises the M10 pipeline in
dry-run mode — research → baseline notebook → kg-nb round-trip →
reviewer-gate (`kernel_push`) → decision approve → `kca kaggle push`
credentials-gate refusal — all WITHOUT real Kaggle credentials and
WITHOUT any real Kaggle network call. CI must collect it in both the
`no-db` and `live-db` jobs.

**HARD PRE-REQ: issue #11 (dotenv-leak) must be CLOSED on `main`
before this Loop Prompt may run.** The reason: the equivalent M9
test (`tests/test_m9_e2e.py::test_kca_kaggle_submit_refuses_without_credentials`)
inadvertently posted 3 ERROR submissions to the Spaceship Titanic
leaderboard because `tools/kca/db.py` re-injects `.env` credentials
into the subprocess regardless of `cwd`. If we run this Loop Prompt
without #11 closed, the equivalent M10 test will pollute the
`tpu-getting-started` leaderboard with null-score ERROR kernel
pushes — the same failure mode at higher cost (kernel pushes count
against a daily limit).

This task assumes **M10-T006 closeout is PASS** AND **issue #11 is
CLOSED**.

## Read first

1. `tests/test_m9_e2e.py` (the closest pattern; learn from its leak)

   `KAGGLE_KEY`)
6. Issue #11 (the leak this test must NOT repeat)
7. `docs/tasks/M9-T007-e2e-dryrun-test.md` (the precedent)

## Scope

Before writing the test, verify issue #11 is closed:

```
gh issue view 11 --json state
```

Must report `"CLOSED"`. If not, HALT and ask.

Then add `tests/test_m10_e2e.py` with tests covering:

1. **Baseline notebook smoke** — author a tiny notebook against
   fixture data under `tests/fixtures/tpu-getting-started/` (a 2-class,
   ~80-image stub — not the real 104-class dataset). Verify the
   notebook executes top-to-bottom locally in < 60s.

2. **kg-nb round-trip** — convert the notebook to percent-format `.py`,
   convert back, assert the cell sequence and outputs are equivalent
   (modulo execution timestamps).

3. **Reviewer-gate + decision_api round-trip** — drive a stub worker
   that abstains at `kernel_push`; assert the `agent_reviews` +
   `human_decisions` rows land; approve via the decision_api (POST or

   appropriately so `no-db` SKIPs cleanly).

4. **`kca kaggle push` credentials-gate refusal** — the most
   important and most fragile test. Mirror the M9 pattern with
   M9-T007's tightening + the #11 fix:
   ```python
   env = {
       "PATH": os.environ.get("PATH", ""),
       "HOME": str(tmp_path),  # so kaggle library can't find ~/.kaggle/kaggle.json
       "PYTHONPATH": str(REPO_ROOT),
       "KCA_SKIP_DOTENV": "1",  # honoured by tools/kca/db.py after #11
   }
   proc = subprocess.run(
       [sys.executable, str(REPO_ROOT / "tools" / "kca" / "kca.py"),
        "kaggle", "push",
        "--competition", "tpu-getting-started",
        "--notebook", "/dev/null",
        "--message", "m10-e2e dry-run — must refuse",
        "--json"],
````

````markdown
# M13 — Loop Prompts

_Evaluation, reliability, and regression suite — measures whether the
platform improves over time._
_For sequential, partly autonomous execution on Arch Linux._
_Prerequisite: M10 exit confirmed (notebook-submission path validated;
see `docs/m10-final-review.md`). M11 (CTF) and M12 (Devpost) are NOT
prerequisites — their eval cases are deferred to follow-ups._
_Shared rules: every Loop Prompt below MUST follow
`docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` (sequencing, no real Kaggle /
Anthropic outside designated paths, DB DSN + sandbox bypass,
per-milestone worktree by default, secret denylist, Discovery / Debate
Gate on `arch:` tasks)._

---

## M13 at a glance

M13 is the first **internal regression milestone** — it does not chase
a leaderboard or ship a user-visible feature. Its job is to make every
later platform change measurable. After M13, an arbitrary code change
on `main` can be evaluated against a fixed set of suites (tool-smoke,
Kaggle replay, notebook/kernel dry-run, reasoning, model-route
comparison) and produce a metrics snapshot that future PRs can be
graded against.

This is also the first milestone whose entry task (`M13-T000`) is
tagged `arch:` and therefore triggers the **Discovery / Debate Gate**
(M9.4): `legacy-archaeologist` (skippable — greenfield), then
`requirements-skeptic`, then `design-red-team`. ADR-0016 must cite all
three transcripts under `docs/evidence/m13/T000/discovery/` before any
implementation begins.

M13 is **not** a leaderboard-chasing milestone and **not** an
LLM-quality milestone. Pass/fail is structural: did the suite run,
did it record the expected metrics, did the report writer produce a
diffable snapshot. The metric *values* are baselined here, not
gated.

Direct entry into M13 is blocked until **all** are true:

- M10 is merged on `main` (`docs/m10-final-review.md` exists and
  reports PASS). The notebook/kernel fixtures from M10-T007 are the
  seed for `M13-T004`.
- M9 dry-run leak (issue #11) remains CLOSED on `main` — the eval
  harness inherits the same secrets posture; if #11 reopens, halt T008.
- Local Supabase container is running; M0–M10 migrations are applied;
  the existing `competitions` / `experiment_runs` / `submissions` /
  `agent_reviews` / `agent_tool_audit` rows from M9 / M10 are
  reachable. M13's new tables sit alongside them.

### What's in scope

| Capability | Owned by | M13 touches |
|---|---|---|
| Regression-suite framework + metrics schema | `docs/adr/0016-eval-regression-suite.md` + `docs/architecture/eval-regression-suite.md` | T000 |
| `eval_suites` / `eval_runs` / `eval_results` tables | `supabase/migrations/0008_m13_eval.sql` + `tools/kca/db.py` | T001 |
| `kca eval` CLI surface (`list`, `run`, `show`, `report`) | `tools/kca/eval.py` + `tools/kca/kca.py` registration | T001 — scaffold; T002–T007 — fill |
| Tool-smoke suite (deterministic, no LLM) | `tools/kca/eval/suites/tool_smoke/` + fixtures | T002 |
| Kaggle classic-practice replay (Titanic / Spaceship Titanic / House Prices) | `tools/kca/eval/suites/kaggle_replay/` + fixtures | T003 |
| Notebook/kernel dry-run regression | `tools/kca/eval/suites/kernel_dryrun/` (reuses M10 fixtures) | T004 |
| Reasoning-heavy benchmark | `tools/kca/eval/suites/reasoning/` + 5–10 fixed prompts + deterministic + rubric judges | T005 |
| Model-route comparison harness | `src/worker/routing.py` reuse + `tools/kca/eval/router.py` + cost budget | T006 |
| Metrics aggregator + Markdown / JSON report | `tools/kca/eval/report.py` + `kca eval report` | T007 |
| CI nightly cron + smoke / e2e tests | `.github/workflows/eval.yml` + `tests/test_m13_smoke.py` + `tests/test_m13_e2e.py` | T008 |
| Final review | `milestone-final-review` skill + `worktree-milestone-pr` skill | T009 |

### What's NOT in scope

- **CTF/lab eval cases.** Deferred to M13.1 (or whatever sub-milestone
  M11 produces). M11 has not landed; its solver-script / writeup
  artefacts are not yet stable enough to baseline against.
- **Hackathon / Devpost eval cases.** Deferred to M13.2 — see M12.
- **Real Kaggle network calls.** None. The whole point of replay is
  that the suites run offline against checked-in fixtures. T006's
  model-route comparison may call real LLM APIs under explicit budget
  cap and `--route` flag; Kaggle remains offline in every suite.
- **Production Supabase.** Local only.
- **New leaderboard chases.** M13 does not push a new Kaggle
  submission, kernel, dataset, or model. M9-T004 and M10-T004 are the
  only "real Kaggle write" rows in the system; M13 reads them but
  does not extend them.
- **Pass/fail thresholds on LLM quality.** M13 baselines values; future
  milestones (M14+) decide whether to gate PRs on score-deltas.
- **New top-level CLI subcommands beyond `kca eval`.** Internal
  helpers and per-suite drivers may live under `tools/kca/eval/`, but
  the CLI surface stays at one new top-level subcommand.

DB / sandbox details: see `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` §3 — the
local `supabase-db` container (`postgresql://postgres:s3cr3t@172.21.0.4:5432/postgres`)
needs `dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true`. T006's optional live-LLM
route also needs sandbox bypass; default is the local-vllm route or
`--dry-run` (mocked LLM via `litellm.mock_completion`).

## GitHub issue / label workflow for M13

Each M13 task is filed as a GitHub issue using the `feature-work.yml`
form (or `test-gap.yml` for T008), labelled per task type. A
canonical M13 proposal issue is filed at planning close and is the
target of `decision:confirmed` for the milestone.

| Task | Issue labels at file time | Labels added by triage | Labels at merge |
|---|---|---|---|
| M13-T000 | `arch:`, `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:eval`, `area:docs`, `decision:needed` | `decision:confirmed` + `ai:ready` after Discovery / Debate Gate transcripts attached | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M13-T001 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:supabase`, `area:eval`, `area:cli` | `ai:ready` (after AC + owner) | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M13-T002 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:eval`, `area:worker` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M13-T003 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:eval`, `area:kaggle` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M13-T004 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:eval`, `area:kaggle`, `area:testing` | `ai:ready` after M10-T007 fixture confirmed present | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M13-T005 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:eval`, `area:worker` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M13-T006 | `type:feature`, `ai:blocked`, `policy:approval-required`, `area:eval`, `area:routing`, `decision:needed` | `decision:confirmed` + `ai:ready` only after live-LLM budget cap confirmed on the M13 proposal issue | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M13-T007 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:eval`, `area:docs` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M13-T008 | `type:test-gap`, `ai:triage`, `area:testing`, `area:ci`, `area:eval` | `ai:ready` only after issue #11 confirmed CLOSED | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M13-T009 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:release`, `area:docs` | `ai:ready` after T000–T008 closed | `ai:implementing` → close |

T000 and T006 are the only tasks that start with `decision:needed`.
T000 because it's `arch:` and the Discovery / Debate Gate verdict
is part of the decision record. T006 because it is the only Loop
Prompt that may make non-mocked, paid LLM calls and needs an
explicit budget cap recorded on the proposal issue.

T008 is gated on issue #11 being CLOSED — same posture as M10-T007.

The PR for each task uses `.github/pull_request_template.md`. T006's
PR is the ONLY M13 PR that may check the "External LLM call" box,
and must link the budget-cap comment from the proposal issue.

## Approval gates (summary)

| Gate | When it fires | Where the approval is recorded | Who can approve |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kaggle_submit` | Not used in M13 (out of scope) | n/a | n/a |
| `kernel_push` | Not used in M13 (out of scope) | n/a | n/a |
| `external_llm` (T006 only) | `kca eval run --route claude_* \| gpt_*` (any non-`local_vllm` / non-`mocked` route) | `human_decisions` row + comment on the M13 proposal issue | Project owner |
| `external_fetch` | Not used in M13 (cached pages only) | n/a | n/a |

T006's `external_llm` gate fires once per `eval run` invocation; the
M13 proposal issue carries the approved budget cap. If the budget
cap is exceeded mid-run, the harness aborts the remaining cases and
records `aborted_on_budget` in the run row.

## Rollback / stop criteria

Stop the milestone — do **not** advance to the next Loop Prompt —
if any of these is true:

- T006 exceeds the approved live-LLM budget cap. The harness should
  abort cleanly; if it does not, the leak is a P0 bug.
- Any test in the validation suite regresses from green to red.
- The DSN, credentials, or `.env*` are accidentally printed in any
  log, audit row, eval report, or PR. Stop and rotate the credential.
- Any suite mistakenly calls real Kaggle or real-LLM endpoints when
  it should not. The audit-grep sentinel from M10-T007 must apply
  to every M13 suite: 0 lines for `kaggle competitions submit`,
  `kaggle kernels push`, `kaggle datasets create`, `kaggle datasets
  version` reach the kaggle CLI from any test or eval process.
- Issue #11 (dotenv leak) is reopened mid-milestone. Halt T008 work
  until #11 is green again.
- The Discovery / Debate Gate at T000 does not surface a load-bearing
  unknown (eval framework lock-in, schema decision, route comparison
  shape). Pause, request a human review of the three transcripts,
  do not advance to T001.

If M13 needs a new architectural decision mid-flight (e.g.
"reasoning benchmark needs its own DB table", "model-route harness
needs a new run-artefact shape"), pause and update ADR-0016 in a
new revision; do not advance to the next Loop Prompt with hidden
schema drift.
````

````markdown
# M13-T000: `arch:` Regression-suite architecture + ADR-0016 (Discovery / Debate Gate)

## Milestone
M13: evaluation, reliability, and regression suite.

## Tag
`arch:` — introduces a new architectural primitive (the eval
regression-suite framework). Triggers the **Discovery / Debate Gate**
per `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` §7.

## Goal
Write the canonical M13 design docs — `docs/adr/0016-eval-regression-suite.md`
(decision record) and `docs/architecture/eval-regression-suite.md`
(architecture and data-flow). Run the Discovery / Debate Gate
(`legacy-archaeologist` optional / skippable for greenfield;
`requirements-skeptic` mandatory; `design-red-team` mandatory) and
attach all three transcripts under `docs/evidence/m13/T000/discovery/`.

No code, no migration, no CLI changes in this Loop Prompt. Design
and discovery only.

## Read first

1. `docs/milestones.md` §M13
2. `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` §7 (Discovery / Debate Gate)
3. `docs/architecture/discovery-debate-gate.md` (canonical acceptance
   lines for the three agents)
4. `.claude/agents/requirements-skeptic.md`
5. `.claude/agents/legacy-archaeologist.md` (you will likely skip
   this one — document the skip in the closeout)
6. `.claude/agents/design-red-team.md`
7. `docs/adr/0010-model-routing.md` (route-routing precedent)
8. `docs/adr/0013-otel-console-sqlite-supabase.md` (multi-exporter
   precedent — eval reports may borrow this shape)
9. `docs/architecture/kca-cli-architecture.md` (existing four-layer
   CLI shape; `kca eval` will be a new top-level command)
10. `docs/adr/0006-approval-gate-policy.md` (approval gate posture
    for the new `external_llm` gate at T006)
11. `src/worker/routing.py` (per-job-type routing this milestone
    will reuse for T006's `--route` selector)
12. `tools/kca/run.py` (existing run-artifact layout — `runs/<comp>/<id>/`)
13. `tests/test_m9_e2e.py`, `tests/test_m10_e2e.py` (the closest
    "offline replay" precedents)

## Scope

1. **Run the Discovery / Debate Gate.**
   - Decide whether `legacy-archaeologist` applies. Greenfield is the
     default here: M13 introduces a new subsystem with no direct
     legacy artefact. The skip is acceptable IF you document it
     explicitly in the closeout AND the M13 proposal issue has a
     `decision:confirmed` comment naming the skip.
   - Invoke `requirements-skeptic` against the M13 description in
     `docs/milestones.md`. Expect ≥5 questions across ≥3 categories
     (scope, schema, routing, secrets, replay-stability, …) plus a
     non-empty `explicit_unknowns` list. Save the transcript under
     `docs/evidence/m13/T000/discovery/requirements-skeptic.md`.
   - Invoke `design-red-team` against a strawman draft of ADR-0016
     (write the strawman first, then red-team it). Expect ≥3
     alternatives, ≥1 dropped capability with file:line evidence
     from the current repo, 4 cost axes, actionable
     `open_disagreements`. Save under
     `docs/evidence/m13/T000/discovery/design-red-team.md`.
   - Verify all canonical acceptance lines byte-for-byte against
     `docs/architecture/discovery-debate-gate.md`. A missing
     acceptance line is a task FAIL.

2. **Write `docs/adr/0016-eval-regression-suite.md`.** Decisions
   covered (non-exhaustive):
   - Schema choice: three new tables (`eval_suites`, `eval_runs`,
     `eval_results`) vs single wide table. Argue for three.
   - Driver shape: per-suite Python module under
     `tools/kca/eval/suites/<name>/` exposing a `register()` +
     `run(case, route) -> EvalResult` contract. Argue why.
   - Route selector: reuse `src/worker/routing.py`'s job-type
     routing as the source of truth for `--route` values, plus a
     `mocked` route that returns `litellm.mock_completion`.
   - Cost gate: `external_llm` gate fires per route invocation
     (not per case) to avoid N×cost runaway; hard cap honoured by
     the harness, not by `litellm`.
   - Fixture posture: every Kaggle replay reads frozen sub-samples
     under `tests/fixtures/<comp>/` (≤ ~5 MB total per fixture);
     real Kaggle network is never reachable from any suite.
   - Replay determinism: every suite seeds `random.seed(0)` +
     `numpy.random.seed(0)` and pins the route-emitted text via
     `litellm.mock_completion`'s fixture string when `--route
     mocked` is selected.

3. **Write `docs/architecture/eval-regression-suite.md`.**
   Include:
   - ASCII data-flow: `kca eval run` → suite driver → cases →
     `eval_results` row → `kca eval report` → JSON + Markdown.
   - Table layout for each of the three new tables (column,
     type, nullable, FK).
   - Per-suite metric definitions (which suite emits which
     metric key into `eval_results.metrics_jsonb`).
   - Where each route's secrets are read (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`,
     `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `KCA_LOCAL_ENDPOINT_*` env vars) and
     which routes need `KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1`.
   - The "audit-grep sentinel" — every M13 suite must inherit
     the M10-T007 guard (0 lines for `kaggle competitions submit`
     / `kaggle kernels push` / `kaggle datasets create` etc.
     reach the kaggle CLI from any suite process).

4. **File the M13 proposal issue** using
   `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature-work.yml`. Body links ADR-0016,
   the architecture doc, and the three discovery transcripts.
   Labels at file: `arch:`, `type:feature`, `area:eval`,
   `area:docs`, `decision:needed`, `ai:triage`. Promote to
   `decision:confirmed` + `ai:ready` only after a human confirms
   the gate skip (if any) and the live-LLM budget cap for T006.
````

````markdown
# M13-T001: Migration 0008 + `kca eval` CLI scaffold

## Milestone
M13: evaluation, reliability, and regression suite.

## Goal
Land the three new tables (`eval_suites`, `eval_runs`,
`eval_results`) via `supabase/migrations/0008_m13_eval.sql`, the
matching helper functions in `tools/kca/db.py`, and the `kca eval`
top-level subcommand surface with four placeholder verbs (`list`,
`run`, `show`, `report`). No suites yet; the scaffold must exit-0
on `--help` for every verb, and `run` must refuse with
`NO_SUITES_REGISTERED` until T002+ register their suites.

This task assumes **M13-T000 closeout is PASS** and the M13 proposal
issue has reached `decision:confirmed` + `ai:ready`.

## Read first

1. M13-T000 closeout (ADR-0016 + architecture doc).

   implements).

   migration; idempotency posture).
5. `supabase/migrations/0006_m6_reviews_spans.sql` (the M6 two-table
   pattern is close to what `eval_runs` + `eval_results` need).
6. `tools/kca/db.py` (existing helper functions — the new ones
   follow the M6 / M8 naming convention).
7. `tools/kca/kca.py` (top-level subcommand registration).
8. `tools/kca/run.py` (LOCAL_WRITE pattern; gating; JSON-output
   convention).
9. `docs/architecture/kca-cli-architecture.md` (where the new
   subcommand sits in the four-layer model).
10. `tests/test_m4_smoke.py` and `tests/test_m5_smoke.py` (migration
    test patterns — extending one of these for T008's smoke is
    out of scope here, just understand the shape).

## Scope

1. **Migration `supabase/migrations/0008_m13_eval.sql`** —
   idempotent (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS …`):

   - `eval_suites` — `id uuid pk`, `name text unique not null`,
     `description text`, `version text not null`, `category text
     check (category in ('tool_smoke','kaggle_replay','kernel_dryrun','reasoning','model_route_compare'))`,
     `metadata jsonb default '{}'::jsonb`, `created_at timestamptz
     default now()`.
   - `eval_runs` — `id uuid pk`, `started_at timestamptz default
     now()`, `finished_at timestamptz`, `route text not null`,
     `dry_run bool not null default true`, `total_cases int not null
     default 0`, `total_pass int`, `total_fail int`, `total_skip
     int`, `aborted_on_budget bool default false`, `budget_usd
     numeric(10,4)`, `cost_usd numeric(10,4)`, `metadata jsonb
     default '{}'::jsonb`.
   - `eval_results` — `id uuid pk`, `run_id uuid not null references
     eval_runs(id) on delete cascade`, `suite_id uuid not null
     references eval_suites(id)`, `case_name text not null`,
     `route text not null`, `status text not null check (status in
     ('pass','fail','skip','error'))`, `metrics jsonb default
     '{}'::jsonb`, `latency_ms int`, `cost_usd numeric(10,4)`,
     `error_text text`, `created_at timestamptz default now()`.
   - Indexes: `(run_id)` on results; `(suite_id, route)` on
     results; `(started_at desc)` on runs; `(category)` on suites.

2. **DB helpers in `tools/kca/db.py`** — pure-Python, no business
   logic:
   - `register_eval_suite(name, description, version, category,
     metadata) -> str` (returns suite uuid; idempotent on `name`).
   - `start_eval_run(route, dry_run, budget_usd, metadata) -> str`.
   - `finish_eval_run(run_id, totals_dict, cost_usd,
     aborted_on_budget)` .
   - `record_eval_result(run_id, suite_id, case_name, route,
     status, metrics, latency_ms, cost_usd, error_text) -> str`.
   - `list_eval_suites(category=None) -> list[dict]`.
   - `list_eval_runs(limit=20) -> list[dict]`.
   - `fetch_eval_results(run_id) -> list[dict]`.

3. **`kca eval` CLI scaffold** —
   `tools/kca/eval.py` exports `add_parsers(subparsers)` registered
   from `tools/kca/kca.py`. Verbs:
   - `kca eval list [--json]` — lists registered suites (empty until
     T002+).
   - `kca eval run [--suite NAME ...] [--all] [--route ROUTE]
     [--dry-run] [--budget USD] [--json]` — at this point refuses
     with `{"ok": false, "error": "NO_SUITES_REGISTERED"}` if no
     suites are registered. When suites land in T002+ this becomes
     the entry point for the harness.
   - `kca eval show <run_id> [--json]` — prints the rolled-up rows
     for a given run.
   - `kca eval report <run_id> [--json | --md] [--out PATH]` — at
     this point a thin shim that defers to T007's aggregator;
     prints `{"ok": false, "error": "REPORT_AGGREGATOR_NOT_YET_IMPLEMENTED"}`.

4. **Suite-registration entry point.** Define a `register_all()`
   hook in `tools/kca/eval/__init__.py` that auto-discovers
   `tools/kca/eval/suites/*/__init__.py` modules and calls each
   module's `register(db)` function. T001 ships the discovery
   plumbing but no suites; T002+ add the suite modules.

5. **Smoke evidence** (not the formal test suite — that lands in
   T008):
   - `python -m tools.kca.kca eval --help` prints the four verbs.
   - `python -m tools.kca.kca eval list --json` prints `{"suites":
     [], "count": 0}`.
   - `python -m tools.kca.kca eval run --all --dry-run --json`
     prints `{"ok": false, "error": "NO_SUITES_REGISTERED"}`.
   - Connecting to the local Supabase DB with

     verify the three new tables exist via `psql -c "\\d eval_suites"`
     etc.

## Non-goals

- Do not implement the report aggregator. T007 owns it.
- Do not modify existing migrations.
````

````markdown
# M13-T002: Tool-smoke suite (deterministic; no LLM; ≥10 cases)

## Milestone
M13: evaluation, reliability, and regression suite.

## Goal
Author the first concrete eval suite — a deterministic tool-smoke
suite that exercises the existing tool registry (`src/worker/tools.py`
+ `.kca/tools/tools.yaml`) with fixed inputs and expected outputs.
No LLM, no Kaggle network, no Anthropic/OpenAI calls. Coverage
target: every tool flagged `category=read_only` in `tools.yaml`,
plus the four most-used `local_write` tools.

This task assumes **M13-T001 closeout is PASS** — the scaffold,
helpers, and migration are in place.

## Read first

1. M13-T000, M13-T001 closeouts.
2. `src/worker/tools.py` — the tool registry the suite evaluates.
3. `.kca/tools/tools.yaml` — tool metadata (category, side-effect
   level, schema).
4. `src/worker/tool_executor.py` — the executor the suite calls
   into.
5. `tests/test_m7_smoke.py` — already exercises some tools;
   reuse the fixture-input shape where possible.
6. `tools/kca/eval/__init__.py` (the T001 scaffold).
7. `docs/architecture/eval-regression-suite.md` (per-suite metric
   contract).

## Scope

1. **Author suite module** `tools/kca/eval/suites/tool_smoke/`:
   - `__init__.py` exports `register(db)` (calls
     `db.register_eval_suite(name="tool-smoke", category="tool_smoke",
     version="0.1.0", …)`) and a `cases()` generator.
   - `cases.yaml` (or `cases.py` if richer) declares each case:
     `{name, tool, input_json, expected_output_subset, expected_status}`.
   - The runner module reads each case, calls `tool_executor.run(tool,
     input_json)`, compares against `expected_output_subset`
     (subset-match, not full equality), records latency + status into
     `eval_results` via the T001 helpers.

2. **Coverage target** — ≥10 cases:
   - Every `category=read_only` tool in `tools.yaml` exercised by
     at least one case (today: `read_file`, `list_dir`, `kca_run_list`,
     `kca_competition_info`, `kca_kaggle_list`, etc. — verify against
     current `tools.yaml`).
   - At least four `category=local_write` cases, one each for:
     `kca_run_init`, `kca_run_record_metric`, `kca_research_add`,
     and one `write_file` case scoped to a tmpdir.
   - Zero `category=remote_write` cases — those are out of scope
     for tool-smoke (see T004 / T006 for indirect coverage).

3. **Determinism guard.** Every case must run in < 5 s wall and emit
   the same `metrics` JSON on repeated runs against a clean tmpdir.
   The suite seeds `random.seed(0)` and uses tmpdir fixtures from
   `tests/fixtures/tool_smoke/`.

4. **Metric contract.** Per case, the suite emits the following
   keys into `eval_results.metrics`:
   - `latency_ms` (int)
   - `output_match` (bool) — subset-match against expected
   - `output_keys` (list[str]) — sorted keys actually emitted
   - `status` ∈ `{pass, fail, skip, error}` (also the row's `status`
     column)

5. **Audit-grep guard.** Inherit the M10-T007 sentinel: 0 lines
   matching `kaggle competitions submit`, `kaggle kernels push`,
   `kaggle datasets create`, `kaggle datasets version` reach the
   kaggle CLI from any suite process. Verify by intercepting the
   audit log under `.agent/audit/` after the suite runs.

6. **Wire into `kca eval run`.** After T002, `kca eval run --suite
   tool-smoke --route mocked --dry-run --json` should:
   - Create an `eval_runs` row (`dry_run=true`, `route="mocked"`).
   - Insert ≥10 `eval_results` rows.
   - Finish with `total_pass + total_skip + total_fail == total_cases`.

## Non-goals

- No LLM calls — `mocked` route only.
- No Kaggle network. No real submission anything.
- No new tools added — this task evaluates the existing registry.
- No coverage of `remote_write` tools — kept for T004 (notebook /
  kernel dry-run) and T006 (model-route comparison).
- No report aggregator — that lands in T007.

## Acceptance criteria

- `tools/kca/eval/suites/tool_smoke/` exists with ≥10 cases.
- `kca eval list --json` shows `tool-smoke` as a registered suite.
- `kca eval run --suite tool-smoke --route mocked --dry-run --json`
  exits 0, creates one `eval_runs` row and ≥10 `eval_results` rows.
- Two consecutive runs produce identical `metrics` JSON per case
  (modulo `latency_ms` which is bounded but not byte-equal).
- Audit-grep guard PASSes: 0 lines for the four forbidden Kaggle
  CLI invocations from the suite process.
- `ruff check .` + `ruff format --check .` clean.
- `pytest tests/ services/decision_api/tests` — 0 regressions vs
  T001 baseline.

## Permissions

- `git add` / `git commit` deferred to milestone closeout.
- LOCAL_WRITE Supabase — ALLOWED.
- No Kaggle / LLM calls.

## Closeout format

```
M13-T002 closeout
  Suite: tools/kca/eval/suites/tool_smoke/ (registered as `tool-smoke` v0.1.0)
  Cases: <N> (read_only: <r>, local_write: <l>; total wall <s>s)
  eval_runs row id: <uuid>
  eval_results rows: <N> (pass: <p>, skip: <s>, fail: <f>, error: <e>)
  Determinism check: 2 consecutive runs — same metrics JSON: YES
  Audit-grep guard: 0 lines matching forbidden Kaggle CLI commands
  pytest: <X> passed / <Y> skipped (was <X> / <Y>; 0 regressions)
  ruff check + ruff format --check: clean
  Acceptance: PASS — first concrete suite landed
  Next: M13-T003 (Kaggle classic-practice replay)
```

## Related issues

- M13 proposal issue.

## Stop condition

Stop after 80 turns. HALT and ask if:
- A tool flagged `read_only` produces non-deterministic output for
  identical input (would be a tool-registry bug; file as a follow-up).
- The audit-grep guard FAILs — that is exactly the leak this suite
  is supposed to detect. Investigate which tool reached the kaggle
  CLI and surface as a P0 issue.
- The `mocked` route's behaviour drifts from T001's scaffold. Loop
  back to T001 if the drift is structural.
````

````markdown
# M13-T003: Kaggle classic-practice replay suite (offline fixtures)

## Milestone
M13: evaluation, reliability, and regression suite.

## Goal
Add three offline Kaggle replays — Titanic, Spaceship Titanic,
House Prices — each reading a frozen sub-sample of the training
CSV and executing a deterministic baseline (LR or LR-equivalent),
recording local CV / RMSLE into `eval_results`. No real Kaggle
network. No real Anthropic call by default (the optional `--route`
flag defers to T006).

This task assumes **M13-T002 closeout is PASS**.

## Read first

1. M13-T000, M13-T001, M13-T002 closeouts.
2. `docs/tasks/M4-T008-titanic-end-to-end.md` (Titanic precedent).
3. `docs/tasks/M5-T008-house-prices.md` (House Prices RMSLE
   precedent).
4. `docs/tasks/M9-T002-baseline-loop.md` (Spaceship Titanic LR
   baseline precedent — CV 0.79144 ±0.0086 in M9 final review).
5. `tests/test_m9_e2e.py` (closest dry-run replay pattern).
6. `runs/spaceship-titanic/` (existing M9 run artefacts — the
   replay should match their shape, not re-create them).
7. `tools/kca/eval/suites/tool_smoke/` (the T002 driver shape).
8. `docs/architecture/eval-regression-suite.md` (per-suite metric
   contract).

## Scope

1. **Fixtures under `tests/fixtures/`** — frozen sub-samples (≤ ~5 MB
   each), checked into git:
   - `tests/fixtures/titanic/train.csv` — first ~200 rows of the
     real Titanic train.csv, same columns.
   - `tests/fixtures/spaceship-titanic/train.csv` — first ~200 rows
     of the real Spaceship Titanic train.csv. Reuse the existing
     M9 fixture if present.
   - `tests/fixtures/house-prices/train.csv` — first ~200 rows
     (note: this is enough rows for a CV harness to run; not enough
     for realistic scores — that's by design, M13 baselines values
     and is not chasing leaderboard quality).

2. **Three suite modules** under `tools/kca/eval/suites/`:
   - `kaggle_replay_titanic/` — logistic regression on a fixed
     feature set; records `cv_accuracy_mean`, `cv_accuracy_std`,
     `holdout_accuracy`, `fit_time_ms`.
   - `kaggle_replay_spaceship_titanic/` — LR mirror of M9-T002's
     baseline; records same keys.
   - `kaggle_replay_house_prices/` — LR / Ridge mirror of M5-T008;
````

````markdown
merged on `main`** (the fixture and the gating code must already

7. `tools/kca/eval/suites/tool_smoke/` (T002 driver shape).

## Scope

1. **Suite module** `tools/kca/eval/suites/kernel_dryrun/`:
````

````markdown
# M13-T005: Reasoning-heavy benchmark (5–10 fixed prompts; deterministic + rubric)

## Milestone
M13: evaluation, reliability, and regression suite.

## Goal
Author a reasoning-heavy benchmark suite covering 5–10 fixed
prompts that exercise the worker / skill stack on tasks where
deterministic ground truth is checkable: research-brief from
cached pages, debug-a-worker-trace from a canned event slice,
CV-result analysis from a frozen `experiment_runs` row,
"should we submit?" decision-gate rationale.

Two judges per prompt:
- a **deterministic check** (regex / JSON shape / required-keys
  match) that pass/fails the case without an LLM call.
- an **optional rubric-LLM judge** gated behind `--route` (cheap
  route only — default `claude_haiku_4_5`); hard $0.05/prompt cap.

This task assumes **M13-T002 closeout is PASS**. T006 (route
comparison) consumes this suite later.

## Read first

1. M13-T000, M13-T001, M13-T002 closeouts.
2. `src/worker/worker.py` (the agent loop the benchmark drives).
3. `src/worker/routing.py` (per-job-type routing).
4. `tools/kca/research_fetch.py` (cached pages are the input to
   one of the prompts).
5. `docs/tasks/M5-T002-research-fetch.md` (research-brief precedent).
6. `.claude/skills/research-brief/SKILL.md` (the skill one prompt
   evaluates against).
7. `docs/architecture/eval-regression-suite.md` (metric contract).
8. `tools/kca/eval/suites/tool_smoke/` (T002 driver shape).

## Scope

1. **Suite module** `tools/kca/eval/suites/reasoning/`:
   - Registers as `reasoning` v0.1.0, category `reasoning`.
   - 5–10 cases under `cases.yaml`. Each declares:
     `{name, prompt_file, input_files, deterministic_check,
     rubric_prompt, expected_keys, max_cost_usd}`.

2. **Five canonical prompts** (the recommended seed set; more is
   fine):
   - `research_brief_from_cached_pages` — three cached HTML pages
     under `tests/fixtures/research/`; expected output: a brief
     with citations, trust labels, and an `explicit_unknowns`
     list. Deterministic check: required keys + citation count
     ≥ 3 + trust label ∈ enum.
   - `debug_worker_trace` — a frozen `agent_job_events` slice
     (JSONL) under `tests/fixtures/reasoning/worker_trace.jsonl`;
     expected output: a JSON diagnosis with `root_cause`,
     `evidence_event_ids` (≥1), `proposed_fix`. Deterministic
     check: required keys + at least one valid event id.
   - `cv_result_analysis` — a frozen `experiment_runs` row
     (JSON) under `tests/fixtures/reasoning/cv_row.json`;
     expected output: `{is_overfit, recommendation, next_experiment}`
     with `recommendation` ∈ enum. Deterministic check: enum
     match.
   - `submit_decision_rationale` — input: M9-style `submissions`
     candidate row + current best LB; expected output:
     `{should_submit, confidence, rationale}` matching the
     four-scenario decision table in `CLAUDE.md` §KCA autonomous
     submission strategy. Deterministic check: scenario tag in
     `{1,2,3,4}` + boolean shape.
   - `tool_choice_rationale` — input: a stubbed agent step where
     the model must pick between two `kca` subcommands; expected
     output: `{chosen_tool, justification}`. Deterministic check:
     `chosen_tool` ∈ the legal subcommand list.

3. **Deterministic vs rubric.** Each case records both:
   - `deterministic_pass` (bool) — from the regex / shape check.
   - `rubric_score` (float [0,1] or null) — from the optional
     rubric-LLM call. Null when `--route mocked` (the default).

4. **Cost cap.** When a non-mocked route is selected, the suite
   enforces `max_cost_usd` per case (default $0.05) AND a per-run
   budget (passed via `--budget`). If a case would exceed, mark it
   `status="skip"` with `error_text="BUDGET_EXCEEDED"`.

5. **Determinism.** `--route mocked` runs are byte-deterministic
   (the mocked LLM returns a fixture string per prompt; see
   `tests/fixtures/reasoning/mocked_responses.json`). Non-mocked
   runs are not byte-deterministic but must be value-bounded
   (`rubric_score ∈ [0,1]`).

6. **Wire into `kca eval run`.** After T005:
   - `kca eval list --json` shows `reasoning` as a registered
     suite.
   - `kca eval run --suite reasoning --route mocked --dry-run
     --json` exits 0 and creates one `eval_runs` row + 5–10
     `eval_results` rows.

## Non-goals

- No real LLM calls in this task (T006 wires up real routes
  across suites — the budget cap and `--route` flag are
  scaffolded here but not exercised live).
- No new benchmark prompts beyond the five canonical seeds — keep
  the suite small and surgical.
- No new tables — emit metrics into `eval_results.metrics_jsonb`.

## Acceptance criteria

- `tools/kca/eval/suites/reasoning/` registers as `reasoning`;
  `kca eval list` shows it.
- 5–10 cases under `cases.yaml`; each carries
  `deterministic_check` and (optional) `rubric_prompt`.
- `kca eval run --suite reasoning --route mocked --dry-run --json`
  exits 0, produces 5–10 `eval_results` rows.
- For every case, `deterministic_pass` is set; `rubric_score` is
  null in `--route mocked` mode.
- Two consecutive `--route mocked` runs produce byte-identical
  `metrics` JSON per case.
- Audit-grep guard PASSes: 0 lines for the four forbidden Kaggle
  CLI commands.
- `ruff check .` + `ruff format --check .` clean.
- `pytest tests/ services/decision_api/tests` — 0 regressions.

## Permissions

- `git add` / `git commit` deferred to milestone closeout.
- LOCAL_WRITE Supabase — ALLOWED.
- No real Kaggle calls.
- No real LLM calls in T005 — wiring only.

## Closeout format

```
M13-T005 closeout
  Suite: tools/kca/eval/suites/reasoning/ (registered as `reasoning` v0.1.0)
  Cases: <N> (research_brief_from_cached_pages, debug_worker_trace, cv_result_analysis, submit_decision_rationale, tool_choice_rationale, [optional extras])
  Fixtures: tests/fixtures/reasoning/* + tests/fixtures/research/* (total <s> KB)
  Deterministic checks pass rate (--route mocked): <p>/<N>
  Rubric judge: null (route=mocked, by design)
  Determinism check: 2 consecutive runs — byte-identical metrics: YES
  Audit-grep guard: 0 lines matching forbidden Kaggle CLI commands
  pytest: <X> passed / <Y> skipped (0 regressions)
  ruff check + ruff format --check: clean
  Acceptance: PASS
  Next: M13-T006 (model-route comparison harness)
```

## Related issues

- M13 proposal issue.

## Stop condition

Stop after 80 turns. HALT and ask if:
- A canonical prompt's deterministic check is brittle (e.g. fails
  on benign formatting differences). Re-design the check before
  expanding the prompt count.
- A fixture under `tests/fixtures/reasoning/` exceeds ~1 MB.
  Sub-sample more aggressively.
- The mocked-response fixture cannot satisfy every case's
  deterministic check. Surface — a prompt that can't pass even on
  the mocked response is mis-designed.
````
