````markdown
# M13 — Loop Prompts

_Evaluation, reliability, and regression suite — measures whether the
platform improves over time._
_For sequential, partly autonomous execution on Arch Linux._
_Prerequisite: M10 exit confirmed (notebook-submission path validated;
see `docs/m10-final-review.md`). M11 (CTF) and M12 (Devpost) are NOT
prerequisites — their eval cases are deferred to follow-ups._
_Shared rules: every Loop Prompt below MUST follow
`docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` (sequencing, no real Kaggle /
Anthropic outside designated paths, DB DSN + sandbox bypass,
per-milestone worktree by default, secret denylist, Discovery / Debate
Gate on `arch:` tasks)._

---

## M13 at a glance

M13 is the first **internal regression milestone** — it does not chase
a leaderboard or ship a user-visible feature. Its job is to make every
later platform change measurable. After M13, an arbitrary code change
on `main` can be evaluated against a fixed set of suites (tool-smoke,
Kaggle replay, notebook/kernel dry-run, reasoning, model-route
comparison) and produce a metrics snapshot that future PRs can be
graded against.

This is also the first milestone whose entry task (`M13-T000`) is
tagged `arch:` and therefore triggers the **Discovery / Debate Gate**
(M9.4): `legacy-archaeologist` (skippable — greenfield), then
`requirements-skeptic`, then `design-red-team`. ADR-0016 must cite all
three transcripts under `docs/evidence/m13/T000/discovery/` before any
implementation begins.

M13 is **not** a leaderboard-chasing milestone and **not** an
LLM-quality milestone. Pass/fail is structural: did the suite run,
did it record the expected metrics, did the report writer produce a
diffable snapshot. The metric *values* are baselined here, not
gated.

Direct entry into M13 is blocked until **all** are true:

- M10 is merged on `main` (`docs/m10-final-review.md` exists and
  reports PASS). The notebook/kernel fixtures from M10-T007 are the
  seed for `M13-T004`.
- M9 dry-run leak (issue #11) remains CLOSED on `main` — the eval
  harness inherits the same secrets posture; if #11 reopens, halt T008.
- Local Supabase container is running; M0–M10 migrations are applied;
  the existing `competitions` / `experiment_runs` / `submissions` /
  `agent_reviews` / `agent_tool_audit` rows from M9 / M10 are
  reachable. M13's new tables sit alongside them.

### What's in scope

| Capability | Owned by | M13 touches |
|---|---|---|
| Regression-suite framework + metrics schema | `docs/adr/0016-eval-regression-suite.md` + `docs/architecture/eval-regression-suite.md` | T000 |
| `eval_suites` / `eval_runs` / `eval_results` tables | `supabase/migrations/0008_m13_eval.sql` + `tools/kca/db.py` | T001 |
| `kca eval` CLI surface (`list`, `run`, `show`, `report`) | `tools/kca/eval.py` + `tools/kca/kca.py` registration | T001 — scaffold; T002–T007 — fill |
| Tool-smoke suite (deterministic, no LLM) | `tools/kca/eval/suites/tool_smoke/` + fixtures | T002 |
| Kaggle classic-practice replay (Titanic / Spaceship Titanic / House Prices) | `tools/kca/eval/suites/kaggle_replay/` + fixtures | T003 |
| Notebook/kernel dry-run regression | `tools/kca/eval/suites/kernel_dryrun/` (reuses M10 fixtures) | T004 |
| Reasoning-heavy benchmark | `tools/kca/eval/suites/reasoning/` + 5–10 fixed prompts + deterministic + rubric judges | T005 |
| Model-route comparison harness | `src/worker/routing.py` reuse + `tools/kca/eval/router.py` + cost budget | T006 |
| Metrics aggregator + Markdown / JSON report | `tools/kca/eval/report.py` + `kca eval report` | T007 |
| CI nightly cron + smoke / e2e tests | `.github/workflows/eval.yml` + `tests/test_m13_smoke.py` + `tests/test_m13_e2e.py` | T008 |
| Final review | `milestone-final-review` skill + `worktree-milestone-pr` skill | T009 |

### What's NOT in scope

- **CTF/lab eval cases.** Deferred to M13.1 (or whatever sub-milestone
  M11 produces). M11 has not landed; its solver-script / writeup
  artefacts are not yet stable enough to baseline against.
- **Hackathon / Devpost eval cases.** Deferred to M13.2 — see M12.
- **Real Kaggle network calls.** None. The whole point of replay is
  that the suites run offline against checked-in fixtures. T006's
  model-route comparison may call real LLM APIs under explicit budget
  cap and `--route` flag; Kaggle remains offline in every suite.
- **Production Supabase.** Local only.
- **New leaderboard chases.** M13 does not push a new Kaggle
  submission, kernel, dataset, or model. M9-T004 and M10-T004 are the
  only "real Kaggle write" rows in the system; M13 reads them but
  does not extend them.
- **Pass/fail thresholds on LLM quality.** M13 baselines values; future
  milestones (M14+) decide whether to gate PRs on score-deltas.
- **New top-level CLI subcommands beyond `kca eval`.** Internal
  helpers and per-suite drivers may live under `tools/kca/eval/`, but
  the CLI surface stays at one new top-level subcommand.

DB / sandbox details: see `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` §3 — the
local `supabase-db` container (`postgresql://postgres:s3cr3t@172.21.0.4:5432/postgres`)
needs `dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true`. T006's optional live-LLM
route also needs sandbox bypass; default is the local-vllm route or
`--dry-run` (mocked LLM via `litellm.mock_completion`).

## GitHub issue / label workflow for M13

Each M13 task is filed as a GitHub issue using the `feature-work.yml`
form (or `test-gap.yml` for T008), labelled per task type. A
canonical M13 proposal issue is filed at planning close and is the
target of `decision:confirmed` for the milestone.

| Task | Issue labels at file time | Labels added by triage | Labels at merge |
|---|---|---|---|
| M13-T000 | `arch:`, `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:eval`, `area:docs`, `decision:needed` | `decision:confirmed` + `ai:ready` after Discovery / Debate Gate transcripts attached | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M13-T001 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:supabase`, `area:eval`, `area:cli` | `ai:ready` (after AC + owner) | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M13-T002 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:eval`, `area:worker` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M13-T003 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:eval`, `area:kaggle` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M13-T004 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:eval`, `area:kaggle`, `area:testing` | `ai:ready` after M10-T007 fixture confirmed present | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M13-T005 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:eval`, `area:worker` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M13-T006 | `type:feature`, `ai:blocked`, `policy:approval-required`, `area:eval`, `area:routing`, `decision:needed` | `decision:confirmed` + `ai:ready` only after live-LLM budget cap confirmed on the M13 proposal issue | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M13-T007 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:eval`, `area:docs` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M13-T008 | `type:test-gap`, `ai:triage`, `area:testing`, `area:ci`, `area:eval` | `ai:ready` only after issue #11 confirmed CLOSED | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M13-T009 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:release`, `area:docs` | `ai:ready` after T000–T008 closed | `ai:implementing` → close |

T000 and T006 are the only tasks that start with `decision:needed`.
T000 because it's `arch:` and the Discovery / Debate Gate verdict
is part of the decision record. T006 because it is the only Loop
Prompt that may make non-mocked, paid LLM calls and needs an
explicit budget cap recorded on the proposal issue.

T008 is gated on issue #11 being CLOSED — same posture as M10-T007.

The PR for each task uses `.github/pull_request_template.md`. T006's
PR is the ONLY M13 PR that may check the "External LLM call" box,
and must link the budget-cap comment from the proposal issue.

## Rollback / stop criteria

Stop the milestone — do **not** advance to the next Loop Prompt —
if any of these is true:

- T006 exceeds the approved live-LLM budget cap. The harness should
  abort cleanly; if it does not, the leak is a P0 bug.
- Any test in the validation suite regresses from green to red.
- The DSN, credentials, or `.env*` are accidentally printed in any
  log, audit row, eval report, or PR. Stop and rotate the credential.
- Any suite mistakenly calls real Kaggle or real-LLM endpoints when
  it should not. The audit-grep sentinel from M10-T007 must apply
  to every M13 suite: 0 lines for `kaggle competitions submit`,
  `kaggle kernels push`, `kaggle datasets create`, `kaggle datasets
  version` reach the kaggle CLI from any test or eval process.
- Issue #11 (dotenv leak) is reopened mid-milestone. Halt T008 work
  until #11 is green again.
- The Discovery / Debate Gate at T000 does not surface a load-bearing
  unknown (eval framework lock-in, schema decision, route comparison
  shape). Pause, request a human review of the three transcripts,
  do not advance to T001.

If M13 needs a new architectural decision mid-flight (e.g.
"reasoning benchmark needs its own DB table", "model-route harness
needs a new run-artefact shape"), pause and update ADR-0016 in a
new revision; do not advance to the next Loop Prompt with hidden
schema drift.
````

````markdown
# M13-T002: Tool-smoke suite (deterministic; no LLM; ≥10 cases)

## Milestone
M13: evaluation, reliability, and regression suite.

## Goal
Author the first concrete eval suite — a deterministic tool-smoke
suite that exercises the existing tool registry (`src/worker/tools.py`
+ `.kca/tools/tools.yaml`) with fixed inputs and expected outputs.
No LLM, no Kaggle network, no Anthropic/OpenAI calls. Coverage
target: every tool flagged `category=read_only` in `tools.yaml`,
plus the four most-used `local_write` tools.

This task assumes **M13-T001 closeout is PASS** — the scaffold,
helpers, and migration are in place.

## Read first

1. M13-T000, M13-T001 closeouts.
2. `src/worker/tools.py` — the tool registry the suite evaluates.
3. `.kca/tools/tools.yaml` — tool metadata (category, side-effect
   level, schema).
4. `src/worker/tool_executor.py` — the executor the suite calls
   into.
5. `tests/test_m7_smoke.py` — already exercises some tools;
   reuse the fixture-input shape where possible.
6. `tools/kca/eval/__init__.py` (the T001 scaffold).
7. `docs/architecture/eval-regression-suite.md` (per-suite metric
   contract).

## Scope

1. **Author suite module** `tools/kca/eval/suites/tool_smoke/`:
   - `__init__.py` exports `register(db)` (calls
     `db.register_eval_suite(name="tool-smoke", category="tool_smoke",
     version="0.1.0", …)`) and a `cases()` generator.
   - `cases.yaml` (or `cases.py` if richer) declares each case:
     `{name, tool, input_json, expected_output_subset, expected_status}`.
   - The runner module reads each case, calls `tool_executor.run(tool,
     input_json)`, compares against `expected_output_subset`
     (subset-match, not full equality), records latency + status into
     `eval_results` via the T001 helpers.

2. **Coverage target** — ≥10 cases:
   - Every `category=read_only` tool in `tools.yaml` exercised by
     at least one case (today: `read_file`, `list_dir`, `kca_run_list`,
     `kca_competition_info`, `kca_kaggle_list`, etc. — verify against
     current `tools.yaml`).
   - At least four `category=local_write` cases, one each for:
     `kca_run_init`, `kca_run_record_metric`, `kca_research_add`,
     and one `write_file` case scoped to a tmpdir.
   - Zero `category=remote_write` cases — those are out of scope
     for tool-smoke (see T004 / T006 for indirect coverage).

3. **Determinism guard.** Every case must run in < 5 s wall and emit
   the same `metrics` JSON on repeated runs against a clean tmpdir.
   The suite seeds `random.seed(0)` and uses tmpdir fixtures from
   `tests/fixtures/tool_smoke/`.

4. **Metric contract.** Per case, the suite emits the following
   keys into `eval_results.metrics`:
   - `latency_ms` (int)
   - `output_match` (bool) — subset-match against expected
   - `output_keys` (list[str]) — sorted keys actually emitted
   - `status` ∈ `{pass, fail, skip, error}` (also the row's `status`
     column)

5. **Audit-grep guard.** Inherit the M10-T007 sentinel: 0 lines
   matching `kaggle competitions submit`, `kaggle kernels push`,
   `kaggle datasets create`, `kaggle datasets version` reach the
   kaggle CLI from any suite process. Verify by intercepting the
   audit log under `.agent/audit/` after the suite runs.

6. **Wire into `kca eval run`.** After T002, `kca eval run --suite
   tool-smoke --route mocked --dry-run --json` should:
   - Create an `eval_runs` row (`dry_run=true`, `route="mocked"`).
   - Insert ≥10 `eval_results` rows.
   - Finish with `total_pass + total_skip + total_fail == total_cases`.

## Non-goals

- No LLM calls — `mocked` route only.
- No Kaggle network. No real submission anything.
- No new tools added — this task evaluates the existing registry.
- No coverage of `remote_write` tools — kept for T004 (notebook /
  kernel dry-run) and T006 (model-route comparison).
- No report aggregator — that lands in T007.

## Acceptance criteria

- `tools/kca/eval/suites/tool_smoke/` exists with ≥10 cases.
- `kca eval list --json` shows `tool-smoke` as a registered suite.
- `kca eval run --suite tool-smoke --route mocked --dry-run --json`
  exits 0, creates one `eval_runs` row and ≥10 `eval_results` rows.
- Two consecutive runs produce identical `metrics` JSON per case
  (modulo `latency_ms` which is bounded but not byte-equal).
- Audit-grep guard PASSes: 0 lines for the four forbidden Kaggle
  CLI invocations from the suite process.
- `ruff check .` + `ruff format --check .` clean.
- `pytest tests/ services/decision_api/tests` — 0 regressions vs
  T001 baseline.

## Permissions

- `git add` / `git commit` deferred to milestone closeout.
- LOCAL_WRITE Supabase — ALLOWED.
- No Kaggle / LLM calls.

## Closeout format

```
M13-T002 closeout
  Suite: tools/kca/eval/suites/tool_smoke/ (registered as `tool-smoke` v0.1.0)
  Cases: <N> (read_only: <r>, local_write: <l>; total wall <s>s)
  eval_runs row id: <uuid>
  eval_results rows: <N> (pass: <p>, skip: <s>, fail: <f>, error: <e>)
  Determinism check: 2 consecutive runs — same metrics JSON: YES
  Audit-grep guard: 0 lines matching forbidden Kaggle CLI commands
  pytest: <X> passed / <Y> skipped (was <X> / <Y>; 0 regressions)
  ruff check + ruff format --check: clean
  Acceptance: PASS — first concrete suite landed
  Next: M13-T003 (Kaggle classic-practice replay)
```

## Related issues

- M13 proposal issue.

## Stop condition

Stop after 80 turns. HALT and ask if:
- A tool flagged `read_only` produces non-deterministic output for
  identical input (would be a tool-registry bug; file as a follow-up).
- The audit-grep guard FAILs — that is exactly the leak this suite
  is supposed to detect. Investigate which tool reached the kaggle
  CLI and surface as a P0 issue.
- The `mocked` route's behaviour drifts from T001's scaffold. Loop
  back to T001 if the drift is structural.
````

```python
"""Worker tool definitions and executor.

TOOL_SCHEMAS uses OpenAI tool schema format (LiteLLM-compatible for all providers).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import fnmatch
import json
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

from src.worker._types import JobPolicy

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tool schemas (OpenAI format)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

TOOL_SCHEMAS: list[dict] = [
    {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
            "name": "read_file",
            "description": "Read a file relative to the workspace root.",
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "path": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "Path relative to workspace root",
                    }
                },
                "required": ["path"],
            },
        },
    },
    {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
            "name": "write_file",
            "description": "Write content to a file in the workspace.",
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "path": {"type": "string"},
                    "content": {"type": "string"},
                },
                "required": ["path", "content"],
            },
        },
    },
    {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
            "name": "edit_file",
            "description": "Replace the first occurrence of old_string with new_string in a file.",
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "path": {"type": "string"},
                    "old_string": {"type": "string"},
                    "new_string": {"type": "string"},
                },
                "required": ["path", "old_string", "new_string"],
            },
        },
    },
    {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
            "name": "run_bash",
            "description": "Run a shell command in the workspace directory.",
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "command": {"type": "string"},
                    "timeout_s": {"type": "integer", "default": 60},
                },
                "required": ["command"],
            },
        },
    },
    {
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
            "name": "grep_workspace",
            "description": "Search for a pattern in the workspace files.",
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "pattern": {"type": "string"},
                    "path": {"type": "string", "default": "."},
                },
                "required": ["pattern"],
            },
        },
    },
]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Side-effect classification helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

_SIDE_EFFECT_ORDER = ["READ_ONLY", "LOCAL_WRITE", "REMOTE_WRITE", "SUBMISSION"]

# Hard-deny patterns for run_bash (regardless of policy).
_HARD_DENY_PATTERNS = [
    "sudo *",
    "rm -rf*",
    "git push*",
    "kaggle submit*",
]
_HARD_DENY_SUBSTRINGS = [".."]


def _side_effect_ge(a: str, b: str) -> bool:
    """Return True if side-effect a >= b in severity."""
    try:
        return _SIDE_EFFECT_ORDER.index(a) >= _SIDE_EFFECT_ORDER.index(b)
    except ValueError:
        return False


def _bash_side_effect(command: str) -> str:
    """Classify the side-effect level of a bash command."""
    cmd = command.strip()
    if any(
        fnmatch.fnmatch(cmd, pat)
        for pat in ["kca kaggle submit*", "kca kaggle push*", "kca kaggle upload*"]
    ):
        return "SUBMISSION"
    if any(
        fnmatch.fnmatch(cmd, pat)
        for pat in ["kca kaggle *", "kca run *", "python *", "pytest *"]
    ):
        return "LOCAL_WRITE"
    return "LOCAL_WRITE"


def _is_bash_allowed(command: str, policy: JobPolicy) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    """Return (allowed, reason). Hard-deny takes priority over policy."""
    cmd = command.strip()
    for sub in _HARD_DENY_SUBSTRINGS:
        if sub in cmd:
            return False, "command not in allowed_tool_patterns"
    for pat in _HARD_DENY_PATTERNS:
        if fnmatch.fnmatch(cmd, pat):
            return False, "command not in allowed_tool_patterns"
    for pat in policy.allowed_tool_patterns:
        if fnmatch.fnmatch(cmd, pat):
            return True, ""
    return False, "command not in allowed_tool_patterns"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ApprovalRequired exception
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class ApprovalRequired(Exception):
    """Raised when a tool call exceeds policy.max_side_effect."""

    def __init__(self, tool_name: str, tool_input: dict, side_effect: str):
        self.tool_name = tool_name
        self.tool_input = tool_input
        self.side_effect = side_effect
        super().__init__(f"{tool_name} requires approval (side_effect={side_effect})")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ToolExecutor
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class ToolExecutor:
    def __init__(self, workspace: Path, policy: JobPolicy):
        self.workspace = workspace.resolve()
        self.policy = policy

    def _guard_path(self, path: str) -> tuple[Path | None, str | None]:
        """Resolve path within workspace. Return (resolved, None) or (None, error)."""
        target = (self.workspace / path).resolve()
        if not str(target).startswith(str(self.workspace)):
            return None, f"path traversal rejected: {path}"
        return target, None

    def execute(self, tool_name: str, tool_input: dict) -> str:
        # Determine side effect and check approval gate.
        se = self._classify_side_effect(tool_name, tool_input)
        if (
            _side_effect_ge(se, self.policy.max_side_effect)
            and se != self.policy.max_side_effect
        ):
            raise ApprovalRequired(tool_name, tool_input, se)

        if tool_name == "read_file":
            return self._read_file(tool_input)
        elif tool_name == "write_file":
            return self._write_file(tool_input)
        elif tool_name == "edit_file":
            return self._edit_file(tool_input)
        elif tool_name == "run_bash":
            return self._run_bash(tool_input)
        elif tool_name == "grep_workspace":
            return self._grep_workspace(tool_input)
        else:
            return f"unknown tool: {tool_name}"

    def _classify_side_effect(self, tool_name: str, tool_input: dict) -> str:
        if tool_name in ("read_file", "grep_workspace"):
            return "READ_ONLY"
        if tool_name in ("write_file", "edit_file"):
            return "LOCAL_WRITE"
        if tool_name == "run_bash":
            return _bash_side_effect(tool_input.get("command", ""))
        return "LOCAL_WRITE"

    def _read_file(self, inp: dict) -> str:
        target, err = self._guard_path(inp["path"])
        if err:
            return err
        try:
            return target.read_text(errors="replace")
        except Exception as e:
            return f"read_file error: {e}"

    def _write_file(self, inp: dict) -> str:
        target, err = self._guard_path(inp["path"])
        if err:
            return err
        try:
            target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            target.write_text(inp["content"])
            return "ok"
        except Exception as e:
            return f"write_file error: {e}"

    def _edit_file(self, inp: dict) -> str:
        target, err = self._guard_path(inp["path"])
        if err:
            return err
        try:
            text = target.read_text(errors="replace")
            old = inp["old_string"]
            new = inp["new_string"]
            if old not in text:
                return f"edit_file error: old_string not found in {inp['path']}"
            target.write_text(text.replace(old, new, 1))
            return "ok"
        except Exception as e:
            return f"edit_file error: {e}"

    def _run_bash(self, inp: dict) -> str:
        command = inp.get("command", "")
        timeout_s = int(inp.get("timeout_s", 60))
        allowed, reason = _is_bash_allowed(command, self.policy)
        if not allowed:
            return json.dumps({"stdout": "", "stderr": reason, "exit_code": 126})
        try:
            proc = subprocess.run(
                command,
                shell=True,
                capture_output=True,
                text=True,
                timeout=timeout_s,
                cwd=str(self.workspace),
            )
            return json.dumps(
                {
                    "stdout": proc.stdout,
                    "stderr": proc.stderr,
                    "exit_code": proc.returncode,
                }
            )
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            return json.dumps({"stdout": "", "stderr": "timeout", "exit_code": 124})
        except Exception as e:
            return json.dumps({"stdout": "", "stderr": str(e), "exit_code": 1})

    def _grep_workspace(self, inp: dict) -> str:
        pattern = inp.get("pattern", "")
        search_path = inp.get("path", ".")
        target, err = self._guard_path(search_path)
        if err:
            return err
        results = []
        try:
            for p in sorted(target.rglob("*")):
                if not p.is_file():
                    continue
                try:
                    for i, line in enumerate(
                        p.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines(), 1
                    ):
                        if pattern.lower() in line.lower():
                            results.append(
                                {
                                    "file": str(p.relative_to(self.workspace)),
                                    "line_number": i,
                                    "line": line,
                                }
                            )
                except Exception:
                    continue
        except Exception as e:
            return f"grep_workspace error: {e}"
        return json.dumps(results)
```

```python
"""``kca eval`` subcommand implementation (M13-T001 scaffold).

Four verbs:

- ``kca eval list`` — list suites registered via ``register_all()``.
- ``kca eval run`` — run one or more suites. Until T002+ land their
  per-suite drivers, every invocation refuses with
  ``{"ok": false, "error": "NO_SUITES_REGISTERED"}``.
- ``kca eval show <run_id>`` — print roll-up rows for one ``eval_runs``
  id. Returns ``{"ok": false, "error": "NOT_FOUND"}`` on miss.
- ``kca eval report <run_id>`` — defers to T007's aggregator;
  refuses with ``REPORT_AGGREGATOR_NOT_YET_IMPLEMENTED`` until then.

The scaffold writes nothing to the DB unless ``run`` actually dispatches
suites (which it cannot do until T002+). It is therefore safe to invoke
in any environment, including CI without a DB.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import importlib
import json
import os
import pkgutil
import sys
from typing import Any

from _types import EXIT_OK, EXIT_RUNTIME, SideEffect


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Suite registry (in-process; populated by register_all()).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Each entry is the dict the suite module's register(db) function returned.
# Minimum keys (per ADR-0016): "name", "category", "version".
_REGISTRY: list[dict[str, Any]] = []


def _emit(payload: dict, side_effect: SideEffect = SideEffect.READ_ONLY) -> None:
    out = {"side_effect": side_effect.value, **payload}
    print(json.dumps(out, ensure_ascii=False))


def register_all(db_module: object | None = None) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Discover and register every suite under ``tools/kca/eval/suites/``.

    Each suite module is expected to expose a ``register(db)`` callable
    returning a dict with at least ``name`` / ``category`` / ``version``.
    Suites that raise on import are skipped with a stderr warning so a
    single broken suite does not break the whole CLI.

    T001 ships this hook with zero suites; T002+ populate the suites
    directory.
    """
    _REGISTRY.clear()
    # Re-import via __package__ so this works under both `python -m
    # tools.kca.kca` (where the parent is `tools.kca.eval`) and a flat
    # sys.path layout where the parent is just `eval`.
    parent = __package__ or "tools.kca.eval"
    suites_pkg = importlib.import_module(f"{parent}.suites")

    for mod_info in pkgutil.iter_modules(suites_pkg.__path__):
        if mod_info.name.startswith("_"):
            continue
        full_name = f"{suites_pkg.__name__}.{mod_info.name}"
        try:
            mod = importlib.import_module(full_name)
        except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
            print(
                f"[kca eval] suite '{mod_info.name}' import failed: {exc}",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            continue
        register_fn = getattr(mod, "register", None)
        if register_fn is None:
            print(
                f"[kca eval] suite '{mod_info.name}' missing register(db); skipped",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            continue
        try:
            spec = register_fn(db_module)
        except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
            print(
                f"[kca eval] suite '{mod_info.name}' register() raised: {exc}",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            continue
        if not isinstance(spec, dict):
            print(
                f"[kca eval] suite '{mod_info.name}' register() returned "
                f"{type(spec).__name__}; expected dict",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            continue
        _REGISTRY.append(spec)
    return list(_REGISTRY)


def _ensure_registered(db_module: object | None = None) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Lazy re-registration — populates _REGISTRY on first verb call."""
    if not _REGISTRY:
        register_all(db_module)
    return _REGISTRY


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Verb implementations.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def cmd_list(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    suites = _ensure_registered()
    payload = {
        "ok": True,
        "suites": [
            {
                "name": s.get("name"),
                "category": s.get("category"),
                "version": s.get("version"),
                "description": s.get("description"),
            }
            for s in suites
        ],
        "count": len(suites),
    }
    if getattr(args, "json", False):
        _emit(payload)
    else:
        if not suites:
            print("(no suites registered)")
        else:
            for s in suites:
                print(f"{s.get('name'):<32} {s.get('category'):<20} {s.get('version')}")
        # Always emit a JSON line at the end so callers can pipe.
        _emit(payload)
    return EXIT_OK


def cmd_run(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    suites = _ensure_registered()
    if not suites:
        _emit({"ok": False, "error": "NO_SUITES_REGISTERED"})
        return EXIT_RUNTIME
    # T002+ owns the harness loop. Until then, suites discovered via
    # register_all() are listed but not executed — fall through with a
    # 'not yet implemented' marker so a misconfigured T002 stub never
    # silently passes.
    _emit({"ok": False, "error": "EVAL_HARNESS_NOT_YET_IMPLEMENTED"})
    return EXIT_RUNTIME


def cmd_show(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    run_id = (getattr(args, "run_id", None) or "").strip()
    if not run_id:
        _emit({"ok": False, "error": "RUN_ID_REQUIRED"})
        return EXIT_RUNTIME
    # DB optional: if SUPABASE_DB_URL is unset we cannot resolve the run,
    # so surface NOT_FOUND consistently with a missing row.
    if not os.environ.get("SUPABASE_DB_URL"):
        _emit({"ok": False, "error": "NOT_FOUND", "reason": "DB_NOT_CONFIGURED"})
        return EXIT_RUNTIME
    import db as db_mod  # local import; module is at tools/kca/db.py

    try:
        rows = db_mod.fetch_eval_results(run_id)
    except Exception as exc:
        _emit(
            {
                "ok": False,
                "error": "DB_ERROR",
                "error_type": type(exc).__name__,
                "message": str(exc),
            }
        )
        return EXIT_RUNTIME
    if not rows:
        _emit({"ok": False, "error": "NOT_FOUND", "run_id": run_id})
        return EXIT_RUNTIME
    payload = {
        "ok": True,
        "run_id": run_id,
        "count": len(rows),
        "results": [_json_safe(r) for r in rows],
    }
    _emit(payload, SideEffect.READ_ONLY)
    return EXIT_OK


def cmd_report(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    # T007 owns the report aggregator. T001 is a thin shim.
    _emit({"ok": False, "error": "REPORT_AGGREGATOR_NOT_YET_IMPLEMENTED"})
    return EXIT_RUNTIME


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Argparse wiring.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def add_parsers(sub: argparse._SubParsersAction) -> None:
    ev = sub.add_parser(
        "eval",
        help="Evaluation regression-suite harness (M13).",
        description=(
            "M13 regression-suite framework. Four verbs: list, run, show, "
            "report. T001 scaffolds the surface; T002+ land per-suite "
            "drivers."
        ),
    )
    ev_sub = ev.add_subparsers(dest="eval_cmd", required=True)

    # list ------------------------------------------------------------------
    p_list = ev_sub.add_parser("list", help="List registered eval suites.")
    p_list.add_argument(
        "--category",
        help="Filter by suite category (tool_smoke / kaggle_replay / ...).",
    )
    p_list.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    p_list.set_defaults(func=cmd_list)

    # run -------------------------------------------------------------------
    p_run = ev_sub.add_parser(
        "run",
        help="Run one or more suites. Refuses if no suites are registered.",
    )
    p_run.add_argument(
        "--suite",
        action="append",
        default=[],
        help="Suite name to run; repeat for multiple.",
    )
    p_run.add_argument(
        "--all",
        action="store_true",
        help="Run every registered suite.",
    )
    p_run.add_argument(
        "--route",
        default="mocked",
        help="Route key (mocked / local_vllm / claude_* / gpt_*). Default: mocked.",
    )
    p_run.add_argument(
        "--dry-run",
        action="store_true",
        help="Walk through the suite without persisting eval_results rows.",
    )
    p_run.add_argument(
        "--budget",
        type=float,
        default=None,
        help="Hard cost cap in USD; required for any non-mocked / non-local route.",
    )
    p_run.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    p_run.set_defaults(func=cmd_run)

    # show ------------------------------------------------------------------
    p_show = ev_sub.add_parser(
        "show",
        help="Print eval_results rows for a given run id.",
    )
    p_show.add_argument("run_id", help="UUID of the eval_runs row.")
    p_show.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    p_show.set_defaults(func=cmd_show)

    # report ----------------------------------------------------------------
    p_report = ev_sub.add_parser(
        "report",
        help="Roll up eval_results into JSON + Markdown (T007).",
    )
    p_report.add_argument("run_id", help="UUID of the eval_runs row.")
    grp = p_report.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    grp.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    grp.add_argument("--md", action="store_true")
    p_report.add_argument("--out", help="Output path (default: stdout).")
    p_report.set_defaults(func=cmd_report)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _json_safe(d: dict) -> dict:
    """Coerce psycopg row values to JSON-serialisable types."""
    out: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for k, v in d.items():
        if hasattr(v, "isoformat"):  # datetime / date / time
            out[k] = v.isoformat()
        elif hasattr(v, "hex") and not isinstance(v, (bytes, bytearray, str)):
            # UUID
            out[k] = str(v)
        else:
            try:
                json.dumps(v)
                out[k] = v
            except TypeError:
                out[k] = str(v)
    return out
```

```python
"""kca DB access layer (psycopg3, sync).

Side-effect classification:
  - Operations against a local Supabase stack are LOCAL_WRITE.
  - Operations against a remote Postgres are REMOTE_WRITE and require
    both KCA_DB_TARGET=remote and KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1.

Env contract (set in .env, loaded automatically via python-dotenv if installed):
  - SUPABASE_DB_URL         : libpq conninfo string (preferred).
  - KCA_DB_TARGET           : "local" (default) or "remote".
```

```python
_EVAL_VALID_STATUSES = {"pass", "fail", "skip", "error"}


def register_eval_suite(
    name: str,
    description: str | None,
    version: str,
    category: str,
    metadata: dict | None = None,
    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,
) -> str:
    """Upsert an eval_suites row keyed by name. Returns the suite id (uuid str).

    Idempotent on ``name``: a second call with the same ``name`` updates
    description / version / category / metadata in place and returns the
    same suite id. This is the registration entry point invoked by
    ``tools/kca/eval/__init__.register_all()``.
    """
    if category not in _EVAL_VALID_CATEGORIES:
        raise ValueError(
            f"category must be one of {sorted(_EVAL_VALID_CATEGORIES)}, "
            f"got {category!r}"
        )
    return _with_conn(
        conn,
        _register_eval_suite,
        name,
        description,
        version,
        category,
        metadata or {},
    )


def _register_eval_suite(
    conn: "psycopg.Connection",
    name: str,
    description: str | None,
    version: str,
    category: str,
    metadata: dict,
) -> str:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            """
            INSERT INTO eval_suites (name, description, version, category, metadata)
            VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s::jsonb)
            ON CONFLICT (name) DO UPDATE
              SET description = EXCLUDED.description,
                  version     = EXCLUDED.version,
                  category    = EXCLUDED.category,
                  metadata    = EXCLUDED.metadata
            RETURNING id::text
            """,
            (name, description, version, category, json.dumps(metadata)),
        )
        row = cur.fetchone()
    conn.commit()
    assert row is not None
    return row["id"]


def start_eval_run(
    route: str,
    dry_run: bool,
    budget_usd: float | None = None,
    metadata: dict | None = None,
    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,
) -> str:
    """Insert a new eval_runs row with started_at = now(). Returns run id."""
    return _with_conn(
        conn,
        _start_eval_run,
        route,
        bool(dry_run),
        budget_usd,
        metadata or {},
    )


def _start_eval_run(
    conn: "psycopg.Connection",
    route: str,
    dry_run: bool,
    budget_usd: float | None,
    metadata: dict,
) -> str:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            """
            INSERT INTO eval_runs (route, dry_run, budget_usd, metadata)
            VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s::jsonb)
            RETURNING id::text
            """,
            (route, dry_run, budget_usd, json.dumps(metadata)),
        )
        row = cur.fetchone()
    conn.commit()
    assert row is not None
    return row["id"]


def finish_eval_run(
    run_id: str,
    totals: dict,
    cost_usd: float | None = None,
    aborted_on_budget: bool = False,
    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,
) -> None:
    """Set finished_at + totals + cost on an existing eval_runs row.

    ``totals`` keys (all optional): ``total_cases``, ``total_pass``,
    ``total_fail``, ``total_skip``. Missing keys leave the column unchanged
    (NULL for the pass/fail/skip columns; 0 default for total_cases on
    insert — caller decides whether to update).
    """
    _with_conn(
        conn,
        _finish_eval_run,
        run_id,
        totals or {},
        cost_usd,
        bool(aborted_on_budget),
    )


def _finish_eval_run(
    conn: "psycopg.Connection",
    run_id: str,
    totals: dict,
    cost_usd: float | None,
    aborted_on_budget: bool,
) -> None:
    fields: list[str] = ["finished_at = now()", "aborted_on_budget = %s"]
    params: list[Any] = [aborted_on_budget]
    for key in ("total_cases", "total_pass", "total_fail", "total_skip"):
        if key in totals and totals[key] is not None:
            fields.append(f"{key} = %s")
            params.append(int(totals[key]))
    if cost_usd is not None:
        fields.append("cost_usd = %s")
        params.append(float(cost_usd))
    params.append(run_id)
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            f"UPDATE eval_runs SET {', '.join(fields)} WHERE id = %s::uuid",
            params,
        )
    conn.commit()


def record_eval_result(
    run_id: str,
    suite_id: str,
    case_name: str,
    route: str,
    status: str,
    metrics: dict | None = None,
    latency_ms: int | None = None,
    cost_usd: float | None = None,
    error_text: str | None = None,
    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,
) -> str:
    """Insert one eval_results row. Returns the new result id (uuid str)."""
    if status not in _EVAL_VALID_STATUSES:
        raise ValueError(
            f"status must be one of {sorted(_EVAL_VALID_STATUSES)}, got {status!r}"
        )
    return _with_conn(
        conn,
        _record_eval_result,
        run_id,
        suite_id,
        case_name,
        route,
        status,
        metrics or {},
        latency_ms,
        cost_usd,
        error_text,
    )


def _record_eval_result(
    conn: "psycopg.Connection",
    run_id: str,
    suite_id: str,
    case_name: str,
    route: str,
    status: str,
    metrics: dict,
    latency_ms: int | None,
    cost_usd: float | None,
    error_text: str | None,
) -> str:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            """
            INSERT INTO eval_results
              (run_id, suite_id, case_name, route, status,
               metrics, latency_ms, cost_usd, error_text)
            VALUES
              (%s::uuid, %s::uuid, %s, %s, %s,
               %s::jsonb, %s, %s, %s)
            RETURNING id::text
            """,
            (
                run_id,
                suite_id,
                case_name,
                route,
                status,
                json.dumps(metrics),
                latency_ms,
                cost_usd,
                error_text,
            ),
        )
        row = cur.fetchone()
    conn.commit()
    assert row is not None
    return row["id"]


def list_eval_suites(
    category: str | None = None,
    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,
) -> list[dict]:
    """List eval_suites rows. Filter by category if provided."""
    return _with_conn(conn, _list_eval_suites, category)


def _list_eval_suites(
    conn: "psycopg.Connection",
    category: str | None,
) -> list[dict]:
    if category is not None:
        query = "SELECT * FROM eval_suites WHERE category = %s ORDER BY name ASC"
        params: list[Any] = [category]
    else:
        query = "SELECT * FROM eval_suites ORDER BY name ASC"
        params = []
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(query, params)
        rows = cur.fetchall()
    return [dict(r) for r in rows]


def list_eval_runs(
    limit: int = 20,
    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,
) -> list[dict]:
    """List eval_runs rows newest-first."""
    return _with_conn(conn, _list_eval_runs, limit)


def _list_eval_runs(conn: "psycopg.Connection", limit: int) -> list[dict]:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM eval_runs ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT %s",
            (limit,),
        )
        rows = cur.fetchall()
    return [dict(r) for r in rows]


def fetch_eval_results(
    run_id: str,
    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,
) -> list[dict]:
    """List eval_results rows for a given eval_run id, oldest first."""
    return _with_conn(conn, _fetch_eval_results, run_id)
```

```python
"""Audit logger: records policy decisions for tool executions to JSONL/DB.

M7 shipped the JSONL backend at ``.agent/audit.jsonl``. M8 adds an optional
dual-write into the ``agent_tool_audit`` table (migration 0007) when
``SUPABASE_DB_URL`` is set. The writer never raises on DB failure — the
JSONL line is always the source of truth for offline ops.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import sys
import uuid
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path


def _repo_root() -> Path:
    return Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]


def _default_audit_path() -> Path:
    override = os.environ.get("KCA_AUDIT_PATH")
    if override:
        return Path(override)
    return _repo_root() / ".agent" / "audit.jsonl"


@dataclass
class AuditRecord:
    timestamp: str
    session_id: str
    skill_name: str | None
    tool_name: str
    operation: str
    decision: str
    mode: str
    policy_profile: str
    audit_required: bool
    args_hash: str
    job_id: str | None = None
    extra: dict | None = None

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        return asdict(self)


def _hash_args(args: dict | None) -> str:
    if not args:
        return ""
    try:
        serialized = json.dumps(args, sort_keys=True, default=str)
    except TypeError:
        serialized = str(sorted(args.items()))
    return hashlib.sha256(serialized.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


_SESSION_ID = os.environ.get("KCA_SESSION_ID") or str(uuid.uuid4())


def _db_configured() -> bool:
    return bool(os.environ.get("SUPABASE_DB_URL") or os.environ.get("SUPABASE_DB_HOST"))


@dataclass
class AuditLogger:
    backend: str = "file"  # "file" | "db" | "both"
    file_path: Path = field(default_factory=lambda: _default_audit_path())
    db_available: bool | None = None
    session_id: str = field(default_factory=lambda: _SESSION_ID)

    def _ensure_dir(self) -> None:
        try:
            self.file_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        except OSError as exc:
            sys.stderr.write(f"[audit warn] mkdir failed: {exc}\n")
```

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""kca: stable execution layer over legacy tools, with side-effect classification.

Side-effect levels (see COMMANDS.md):
  READ_ONLY | LOCAL_WRITE | REMOTE_WRITE | SUBMISSION
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))

from agent.command_registry import REGISTRY  # noqa: E402


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="kca",
        description="Kaggle Code Agent stable CLI. Each subcommand declares a side-effect level.",
    )
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="group", required=True)
    for spec in REGISTRY.list_all():
        spec.add_parsers_fn(sub)
    return parser


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = build_parser()
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if not hasattr(args, "func"):
        parser.print_help()
        return 1
    return int(args.func(args) or 0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

````markdown
## Per-table layout

Migration 0008 lands these three tables. The columns below are the
ADR-0016 commitment; column nullability and FK lines are the
to-be-enforced shape for T001's migration to honour byte-for-byte.

### `eval_suites` — registry of registered suites

| Column | Type | Nullable | FK | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `uuid` | NO | PK | `gen_random_uuid()` default. |
| `slug` | `text` | NO | unique | `tool_smoke`, `kaggle_replay_titanic`, `kernel_dryrun`, `reasoning`, `router_compare`. |
| `display_name` | `text` | NO | | Human-friendly label for the report. |
| `category` | `text` | NO | | One of `tool`, `kaggle_replay`, `kernel_dryrun`, `reasoning`, `router_compare`. |
| `default_route` | `text` | NO | | Usually `mocked`. The suite's reference route. |
| `requires_db` | `boolean` | NO | | If TRUE, suite skips when `SUPABASE_DB_URL` is unset. |
| `requires_remote` | `boolean` | NO | | If TRUE, suite skips when `KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE != 1`. |
| `description` | `text` | YES | | One paragraph. |
| `created_at` | `timestamptz` | NO | | `now()` default. |

Indexes: `(slug)` unique.

### `eval_runs` — one row per `kca eval run` invocation

| Column | Type | Nullable | FK | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `uuid` | NO | PK | `gen_random_uuid()` default. |
| `project_id` | `uuid` | YES | `projects.id` | Nullable for synthetic CI runs that have no human-owned project. |
| `started_at` | `timestamptz` | NO | | `now()` default. |
| `ended_at` | `timestamptz` | YES | | Set on terminal status. |
| `git_sha` | `text` | YES | | Resolved at run start. |
| `route_summary` | `text` | NO | | Comma-separated list of routes used in the run (e.g. `mocked,claude_haiku_4_5`). |
| `kca_dry_run` | `boolean` | NO | | Mirrors the `--dry-run` flag. |
| `budget_cap_usd` | `numeric(10,4)` | YES | | Approved cap; NULL when no paid route is involved. |
| `budget_spent_usd` | `numeric(10,4)` | NO | | Running total; updated as cases complete. Default `0`. |
| `status` | `text` | NO | | `running` / `ok` / `aborted_on_budget` / `aborted_on_error`. |
| `notes` | `text` | YES | | Human-supplied free-form (PR ref, comparison anchor, …). |

Indexes: `(started_at DESC)`, `(project_id, started_at DESC)`.

### `eval_results` — one row per (case x route) under a run

| Column | Type | Nullable | FK | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `uuid` | NO | PK | `gen_random_uuid()` default. |
| `eval_run_id` | `uuid` | NO | `eval_runs.id` ON DELETE CASCADE | Owning run. |
| `suite_id` | `uuid` | NO | `eval_suites.id` ON DELETE RESTRICT | Which suite produced this row. |
| `case_slug` | `text` | NO | | Per-suite case identifier (e.g. `add_two_numbers`, `titanic_baseline_lr`). |
| `route` | `text` | NO | | The route used; cross-referenced with `MODEL_ROUTES` keys or model ids. |
| `status` | `text` | NO | | `ok` / `failed` / `skipped` / `aborted`. |
| `latency_ms` | `integer` | YES | | Per-case wall time. NULL if `skipped`. |
| `cost_usd` | `numeric(10,4)` | NO | | Default `0`. Real value only for paid routes. |
| `metrics_jsonb` | `jsonb` | NO | | Per-suite metric bag (keys defined below). |
| `context_jsonb` | `jsonb` | NO | | Seed, route fixture id, case fixture path; used to reproduce a row. |
| `error_message` | `text` | YES | | Set when `status = failed`. |
| `created_at` | `timestamptz` | NO | | `now()` default. |

Indexes: `(eval_run_id, suite_id, route)`, `(suite_id, case_slug)`,
`(created_at DESC)`.

## Per-suite metric definitions

Each suite emits a documented schema into `eval_results.metrics_jsonb`.
The harness does NOT validate the schema — that is the suite author's
discipline. The report aggregator (T007) groups by `suite × route`
and renders only the metric keys it recognises for each suite.

### `tool_smoke` (T002)

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `exit_code` | int | Tool exit code (0 on success). |
| `stdout_sha256` | string | SHA-256 of the captured stdout; deterministic per case. |
| `stderr_sha256` | string | SHA-256 of the captured stderr; deterministic per case. |
| `bytes_written` | int | For `LOCAL_WRITE` tools, total bytes written to the sandbox tmpdir. |
| `matched_expected` | boolean | Whether the case's deterministic expected-output assertion held. |

### `kaggle_replay_*` (T003)

One suite per competition slug — `kaggle_replay_titanic`,
`kaggle_replay_spaceship_titanic`, `kaggle_replay_house_prices`.

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `cv_score` | float | Cross-validation score (accuracy for classification, RMSLE for regression). |
| `cv_metric` | string | The score's metric name (`accuracy`, `rmsle`, `auc`). |
| `cv_n_splits` | int | Number of CV folds. |
| `fit_seconds` | float | Wall time for the baseline fit. |
| `rows_in_fixture` | int | Number of rows in the frozen sub-sample. |
| `baseline_id` | string | Identifier for the baseline (e.g. `m9_lr`, `m9_hgb_fe`, `m5_xgb`). |

### `kernel_dryrun` (T004)

Reuses M10-T007 fixtures (`tests/fixtures/tpu-getting-started/`).

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `gates_fired` | int | Number of approval gates the dry-run flow exercised. |
| `reviewer_decision` | string | `approve` / `request_changes` / `block` / `none`. |
| `credentials_gate_refusal` | boolean | Whether the missing-credentials path correctly refused before the kaggle CLI. |
| `audit_grep_violations` | int | MUST be 0. Number of lines in the suite's audit log matching the M10-T007 deny patterns. |
| `kernel_metadata_valid` | boolean | Whether the generated kernel-metadata.json passes shape validation. |

### `reasoning` (T005)

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `deterministic_judge_pass` | boolean | Regex / JSON-shape / key-facts assertion result. |
| `rubric_score` | float | 0.0–1.0, only set when an LLM rubric judge ran. |
| `rubric_judge_route` | string | Route used for the rubric (always `claude_haiku_4_5` per T005 spec). |
| `rubric_cost_usd` | float | Per-prompt cost; capped at $0.05 per T005 spec. |
| `prompt_id` | string | Fixed prompt identifier. |

### `router_compare` (T006)

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `parent_suite` | string | Which T002–T005 sub-suite this row corresponds to. |
| `parent_case_slug` | string | Case slug from the parent suite. |
| `route_cost_usd` | float | Per-route cost for the same case. |
| `route_latency_ms` | int | Per-route latency. |
| `route_status` | string | `ok` / `aborted_on_budget` / `failed`. |
| `route_metric_value` | float | The route-comparable metric (e.g. CV score, rubric score). |

## Route secrets map

Where each route reads its secret, and which routes need
`KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1`.

| Route key | Resolves to | Secret read from | Needs `KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mocked` | `litellm.mock_completion` with per-suite fixture string | (none) | NO |
| `local_vllm` | `src/worker/local_model.pick_endpoint()` | `KCA_LOCAL_ENDPOINT_*` env vars | NO |
| `claude_sonnet_4_6` / `implement` / `experiment` | `claude-sonnet-4-6` via LiteLLM | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | YES |
| `claude_haiku_4_5` / `research` | `claude-haiku-4-5` via LiteLLM | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | YES |
| `claude_opus_4_7` / `eval` / `analysis` / `review` | `claude-opus-4-7` via LiteLLM | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | YES |
| `gpt_4o` | `gpt-4o` via LiteLLM | `OPENAI_API_KEY` | YES |
| `log_triage` / `summarise` | local sentinel → `local_vllm` or fallback | `KCA_LOCAL_ENDPOINT_*` | NO (the fallback is itself a local route) |

The harness reads secrets only via the existing
`src/worker/routing.py` and LiteLLM provider layer; the eval module
itself never opens `.env*` files. This preserves the dev-phase
secret policy: the harness is a normal LiteLLM caller, no different
from the worker.
````

```sql
-- 0008_m13_eval.sql
-- M13: regression-suite framework — eval_suites + eval_runs + eval_results.
--
-- Forward-only. Idempotent. Additive. All CREATE TABLE / CREATE INDEX
-- statements are guarded with IF NOT EXISTS so the migration is safe to
-- re-apply. The schema is the contract between ADR-0016 / the architecture
-- doc and the kca eval CLI scaffold (T001) + per-suite drivers (T002+).
--
-- Naming follows the M13-T001 task-spec column list verbatim (task spec is
-- authoritative when it diverges from the architecture doc's preliminary
-- column sketch).

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Part A: eval_suites — slow-changing registry of registered suites.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS eval_suites (
  id          uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  name        text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  description text,
  version     text NOT NULL,
  category    text NOT NULL CHECK (category IN (
    'tool_smoke',
    'kaggle_replay',
    'kernel_dryrun',
    'reasoning',
    'model_route_compare'
  )),
  metadata    jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_eval_suites_category
  ON eval_suites(category);

ALTER TABLE eval_suites ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Part B: eval_runs — one row per `kca eval run` invocation.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS eval_runs (
  id                 uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  started_at         timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  finished_at        timestamptz,
  route              text NOT NULL,
  dry_run            boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
  total_cases        integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  total_pass         integer,
  total_fail         integer,
  total_skip         integer,
  aborted_on_budget  boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  budget_usd         numeric(10,4),
  cost_usd           numeric(10,4),
  metadata           jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_eval_runs_started_at
  ON eval_runs(started_at DESC);

ALTER TABLE eval_runs ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Part C: eval_results — one row per (case × route) under a given run.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS eval_results (
  id          uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  run_id      uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES eval_runs(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  suite_id    uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES eval_suites(id),
  case_name   text NOT NULL,
  route       text NOT NULL,
  status      text NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('pass', 'fail', 'skip', 'error')),
  metrics     jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  latency_ms  integer,
  cost_usd    numeric(10,4),
  error_text  text,
  created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_eval_results_run_id
  ON eval_results(run_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_eval_results_suite_route
  ON eval_results(suite_id, route);

ALTER TABLE eval_results ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

```
</details>

```yaml
# tool-smoke cases — deterministic per-tool fixtures.
#
# Each case shape:
#   name:               unique slug; used as eval_results.case_name
#   tool:               tool registered in src/worker/tools.py::TOOL_SCHEMAS
#   category:           classification under tools.py::_classify_side_effect
#                       (read_only | local_write); informational only,
#                       the runner re-classifies via the executor.
#   input:              dict passed verbatim to ToolExecutor.execute()
#   expected_status:    pass | fail | skip | error
#   expected_contains:  substring(s) the tool's stringified output MUST contain
#                       (subset-match — list is AND-combined)
#   expected_keys:      sorted list of top-level JSON keys the tool's output
#                       MUST emit when the output parses as JSON; [] when the
#                       tool returns plain text
#   workspace:          "fixture" — read against tests/fixtures/tool_smoke/
#                       "tmpdir"  — write against the per-run tmpdir
#
# Coverage: 2 read_only tools × 2 cases each (4) + 3 local_write tools, total
# ≥10. write_file gets 2 cases, edit_file 2, run_bash 2 — 10 in total.

cases:
  # ---- read_only: read_file ------------------------------------------------
  - name: read_file_sample_ok
    tool: read_file
    category: read_only
    input:
      path: sample.txt
    expected_status: pass
    expected_contains:
      - "hello tool-smoke"
      - "unique-token-XYZ"
    expected_keys: []
    workspace: fixture

  - name: read_file_missing_returns_error_string
    tool: read_file
    category: read_only
    input:
      path: does-not-exist.txt
    expected_status: pass
    expected_contains:
      - "read_file error"
    expected_keys: []
    workspace: fixture

  # ---- read_only: grep_workspace -------------------------------------------
  - name: grep_workspace_match_one
    tool: grep_workspace
    category: read_only
    input:
      pattern: "unique-token-XYZ"
      path: "."
    expected_status: pass
    expected_contains:
      - "sample.txt"
      - "unique-token-XYZ"
    expected_keys:
      - file
      - line
      - line_number
    workspace: fixture

  - name: grep_workspace_no_match_returns_empty_json
    tool: grep_workspace
    category: read_only
    input:
      pattern: "this-string-is-never-in-the-fixture-zzzzz"
      path: "."
    expected_status: pass
    expected_contains:
      - "[]"
    expected_keys: []
    workspace: fixture

  # ---- local_write: write_file ---------------------------------------------
  - name: write_file_creates_new
    tool: write_file
    category: local_write
    input:
      path: created/by_suite.txt
      content: "tool-smoke wrote this\n"
    expected_status: pass
    expected_contains:
      - "ok"
    expected_keys: []
    workspace: tmpdir

  - name: write_file_overwrite_idempotent
    tool: write_file
    category: local_write
    input:
      path: created/by_suite.txt
      content: "second write replaces first\n"
    expected_status: pass
    expected_contains:
      - "ok"
    expected_keys: []
    workspace: tmpdir
    depends_on: write_file_creates_new

  # ---- local_write: edit_file ----------------------------------------------
  - name: edit_file_replaces_first_match
    tool: edit_file
    category: local_write
    input:
      path: created/by_suite.txt
      old_string: "second write replaces first"
      new_string: "third write — edited in place"
    expected_status: pass
    expected_contains:
      - "ok"
    expected_keys: []
    workspace: tmpdir
    depends_on: write_file_overwrite_idempotent

  - name: edit_file_missing_old_string_returns_error_string
    tool: edit_file
    category: local_write
    input:
      path: created/by_suite.txt
      old_string: "this-substring-is-absent-zzzz"
      new_string: "unused"
    expected_status: pass
    expected_contains:
      - "edit_file error"
      - "old_string not found"
    expected_keys: []
    workspace: tmpdir
    depends_on: edit_file_replaces_first_match

  # ---- local_write: run_bash -----------------------------------------------
  - name: run_bash_allowed_pattern_kca_help
    tool: run_bash
    category: local_write
    input:
      command: "python -c \"print('tool-smoke ok')\""
      timeout_s: 10
    expected_status: pass
    expected_contains:
      - "tool-smoke ok"
    expected_keys:
      - exit_code
      - stderr
      - stdout
    workspace: tmpdir

  - name: run_bash_hard_deny_kaggle_submit
    tool: run_bash
    category: local_write
    input:
      command: "kaggle submit -c titanic -f sub.csv -m smoke"
      timeout_s: 5
    expected_status: pass
    expected_contains:
      - "command not in allowed_tool_patterns"
    expected_keys:
      - exit_code
      - stderr
      - stdout
    workspace: tmpdir

```

```python
"""tool_smoke — deterministic per-tool smoke suite (M13-T002).

Exercises the worker tool registry (``src/worker/tools.py``) with a
checked-in case list (``cases.yaml``). Every case:

- runs against a per-run tmpdir (no network, no DB, no LLM);
- is fully deterministic — seeded ``random.seed(0)`` + frozen fixtures;
- emits the M13 ``tool_smoke`` metric bag into ``eval_results.metrics``:
  ``latency_ms``, ``output_match`` (subset-match boolean),
  ``output_keys`` (sorted JSON top-level keys; ``[]`` for plain text).

The suite never invokes the kaggle CLI nor any remote API. A post-run
audit-grep guard verifies that ``.agent/audit.jsonl`` and the suite's
own captured command log contain zero hits for the M10-T007 forbidden
patterns (``kaggle competitions submit``, ``kaggle kernels push``,
``kaggle datasets create``, ``kaggle datasets version``).

Registration shape: ``register(db)`` is called by
``tools.kca.eval.register_all``; it upserts the row in ``eval_suites``
when a DB is configured AND returns the in-process suite spec dict
either way.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import random
import re
import shutil
import sys
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

try:
    import yaml  # type: ignore
except ImportError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - hard requirement
    raise RuntimeError(
        "tool_smoke suite requires PyYAML; pip install pyyaml"
    ) from exc

SUITE_NAME = "tool-smoke"
SUITE_VERSION = "0.1.0"
SUITE_CATEGORY = "tool_smoke"
SUITE_DESCRIPTION = (
    "Deterministic per-tool smoke suite exercising src/worker/tools.py. "
    "≥10 cases, no LLM, no Kaggle network."
)

_SUITE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
_CASES_PATH = _SUITE_DIR / "cases.yaml"
_REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4]
_FIXTURE_DIR = _REPO_ROOT / "tests" / "fixtures" / "tool_smoke"

# M10-T007 forbidden patterns. Inherited by every M13 suite.
AUDIT_GREP_FORBIDDEN = (
    "kaggle competitions submit",
    "kaggle kernels push",
    "kaggle datasets create",
    "kaggle datasets version",
)

# Policy used by the suite. Allows ``python *`` so the
# run_bash_allowed_pattern case can shell out to a one-shot python.
# Hard-deny entries in src/worker/tools.py still take priority over
# this allow-list (kaggle submit, sudo, rm -rf, git push, ``..`` path
# traversal).
_SUITE_BASH_PATTERNS = ["python *", "kca *", "pytest *"]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Case loader.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Case:
    name: str
    tool: str
    category: str
    input: dict
    expected_status: str
    expected_contains: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    expected_keys: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    workspace: str = "tmpdir"
    depends_on: str | None = None


def _load_cases() -> list[Case]:
    if not _CASES_PATH.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"cases.yaml missing at {_CASES_PATH}")
    raw = yaml.safe_load(_CASES_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) or {}
    cases_raw = raw.get("cases") or []
    out: list[Case] = []
    for c in cases_raw:
        out.append(
            Case(
                name=c["name"],
                tool=c["tool"],
                category=c.get("category", "read_only"),
                input=dict(c.get("input") or {}),
                expected_status=c.get("expected_status", "pass"),
                expected_contains=tuple(c.get("expected_contains") or ()),
                expected_keys=tuple(sorted(c.get("expected_keys") or ())),
                workspace=c.get("workspace", "tmpdir"),
                depends_on=c.get("depends_on"),
            )
        )
    return out


def cases() -> list[Case]:
    """Public iterator of cases — used by the runner and tests."""
    return _load_cases()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Per-run execution.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass
class CaseResult:
    case_name: str
    status: str  # pass | fail | skip | error
    metrics: dict
    latency_ms: int
    error_text: str | None = None
    tool_output_preview: str = ""


@dataclass
class RunOutcome:
    results: list[CaseResult] = field(default_factory=list)
    audit_grep_violations: int = 0
    audit_grep_lines: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    total_cases: int = 0
    total_pass: int = 0
    total_fail: int = 0
    total_skip: int = 0
    total_error: int = 0


def _output_keys_from(output: str) -> list[str]:
    """Return sorted top-level JSON keys, or [] when output is not a JSON object."""
    if not output:
        return []
    stripped = output.strip()
    if not stripped or stripped[0] not in "{[":
        return []
    try:
        parsed = json.loads(stripped)
    except Exception:
        return []
    if isinstance(parsed, dict):
        return sorted(parsed.keys())
    if isinstance(parsed, list) and parsed and isinstance(parsed[0], dict):
        # For arrays of objects (grep_workspace), expose the FIRST row's keys
        # so the contract stays useful while still being deterministic.
        return sorted(parsed[0].keys())
    return []


def _subset_match(output: str, expected_contains: tuple[str, ...]) -> bool:
    if not expected_contains:
        return True
    return all(needle in output for needle in expected_contains)


def _build_executor(workspace: Path):
    """Construct a ToolExecutor with a suite-specific JobPolicy."""
    # Lazy import keeps the suite module importable without src/ on sys.path
    # (e.g. when ``kca eval list`` runs and only enumerates suites).
    sys.path.insert(0, str(_REPO_ROOT))
    from src.worker._types import JobPolicy  # noqa: E402
    from src.worker.tools import ToolExecutor  # noqa: E402

    policy = JobPolicy(
        allowed_tool_patterns=list(_SUITE_BASH_PATTERNS),
        max_side_effect="LOCAL_WRITE",
    )
    return ToolExecutor(workspace, policy)


def _materialise_workspace(case: Case, fixture_dir: Path, tmpdir: Path) -> Path:
    """Return the workspace path for a case.

    fixture cases run against a copy of the read-only fixture dir to keep
    the source tree pristine; tmpdir cases run against a shared per-run
    tmpdir so write/edit chains work across cases.
    """
    if case.workspace == "fixture":
        # The fixture dir is read-only by convention; copy into a per-case
        # subdir so a buggy tool (e.g. write_file with a fixture path)
        # never mutates the checked-in tree.
        case_ws = tmpdir / "fixture" / case.name
        if not case_ws.exists():
            shutil.copytree(fixture_dir, case_ws)
        return case_ws
    return tmpdir / "tmpdir"


def _run_case(case: Case, fixture_dir: Path, tmpdir: Path) -> CaseResult:
    workspace = _materialise_workspace(case, fixture_dir, tmpdir)
    workspace.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    executor = _build_executor(workspace)

    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    output_str = ""
    status = "pass"
    error_text: str | None = None
    try:
        raw = executor.execute(case.tool, dict(case.input))
        output_str = raw if isinstance(raw, str) else str(raw)
    except Exception as exc:  # ApprovalRequired or unexpected
        status = "error"
        error_text = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
        output_str = ""
    latency_ms = int((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000)

    output_keys = _output_keys_from(output_str)
    output_match = _subset_match(output_str, case.expected_contains)
    if not output_match and status == "pass":
        status = "fail"
        error_text = error_text or "subset-match failed"
    if case.expected_keys and tuple(output_keys) != case.expected_keys:
        if status == "pass":
            status = "fail"
            error_text = error_text or (
                f"expected_keys mismatch: got={output_keys} "
                f"expected={list(case.expected_keys)}"
            )

    metrics = {
        "latency_ms": latency_ms,
        "output_match": output_match,
        "output_keys": output_keys,
        # Per-suite extras (kept inside the metric bag, not separate columns).
        "tool": case.tool,
        "expected_status": case.expected_status,
        "category": case.category,
    }
    return CaseResult(
        case_name=case.name,
        status=status,
        metrics=metrics,
        latency_ms=latency_ms,
        error_text=error_text,
        tool_output_preview=output_str[:200],
    )


def _audit_grep(audit_path: Path, started_after_ns: int) -> tuple[int, list[str]]:
    """Return (violation_count, sample_lines) for the M10-T007 forbidden patterns.

    Only inspects audit lines whose ``timestamp`` (ISO-8601 string) parses
    to a moment AFTER the suite started — older lines from previous
    sessions are not the suite's responsibility.
    """
    if not audit_path.exists():
        return 0, []
    violations: list[str] = []
    pattern = re.compile("|".join(re.escape(p) for p in AUDIT_GREP_FORBIDDEN))
    with audit_path.open("r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
        for line in fh:
            if pattern.search(line):
                violations.append(line.rstrip("\n"))
    return len(violations), violations[:20]


def run(
    *,
    route: str = "mocked",
    seed: int = 0,
    tmpdir: Path | None = None,
    audit_path: Path | None = None,
) -> RunOutcome:
    """Execute every case in cases.yaml and return a RunOutcome.

    Side-effects: writes inside ``tmpdir`` only. Never touches the DB —
    the runner in ``tools/kca/eval/cli.py`` is the only path that
    persists rows to ``eval_runs`` / ``eval_results``.
    """
    random.seed(seed)
    started_ns = time.time_ns()

    if tmpdir is None:
        import tempfile

        tmpdir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="m13-tool-smoke-"))
    else:
        tmpdir = Path(tmpdir)
    tmpdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    fixture_dir = _FIXTURE_DIR
    if not fixture_dir.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"tool_smoke fixture missing: {fixture_dir} — checked-in fixture required"
        )

    outcome = RunOutcome()
    for case in _load_cases():
        result = _run_case(case, fixture_dir, tmpdir)
        outcome.results.append(result)
        outcome.total_cases += 1
        if result.status == "pass":
            outcome.total_pass += 1
        elif result.status == "fail":
            outcome.total_fail += 1
        elif result.status == "skip":
            outcome.total_skip += 1
        else:
            outcome.total_error += 1

    if audit_path is None:
        audit_path = _REPO_ROOT / ".agent" / "audit.jsonl"
    v_count, v_lines = _audit_grep(audit_path, started_ns)
    outcome.audit_grep_violations = v_count
    outcome.audit_grep_lines = v_lines
    return outcome


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Registration hook (called by tools.kca.eval.register_all).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def register(db_module: object | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return the suite spec; upsert into ``eval_suites`` when a DB is set.

    The runner stays purely functional: ``register`` records "this suite
    exists"; ``cmd_run`` in ``tools/kca/eval/cli.py`` invokes ``run()`` to
    produce results.
    """
    spec: dict[str, Any] = {
        "name": SUITE_NAME,
        "category": SUITE_CATEGORY,
        "version": SUITE_VERSION,
        "description": SUITE_DESCRIPTION,
        "default_route": "mocked",
        "requires_db": False,
        "requires_remote": False,
        "runner": run,  # in-process handle for cmd_run
        "case_count": len(_load_cases()),
    }
    if db_module is not None:
        try:
            suite_id = db_module.register_eval_suite(
                name=SUITE_NAME,
                description=SUITE_DESCRIPTION,
                version=SUITE_VERSION,
                category=SUITE_CATEGORY,
                metadata={"case_count": spec["case_count"]},
            )
            spec["suite_id"] = suite_id
        except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - DB-optional
            print(
                f"[tool-smoke] db registration skipped: "
                f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
    return spec

```

```bash
print('run_id_a=', a['run_id'])
print('run_id_b=', b['run_id'])
"
```

````markdown
# M13-T003: Kaggle classic-practice replay suite (offline fixtures)

## Milestone
M13: evaluation, reliability, and regression suite.

## Goal
Add three offline Kaggle replays — Titanic, Spaceship Titanic,
House Prices — each reading a frozen sub-sample of the training
CSV and executing a deterministic baseline (LR or LR-equivalent),
recording local CV / RMSLE into `eval_results`. No real Kaggle
network. No real Anthropic call by default (the optional `--route`
flag defers to T006).

This task assumes **M13-T002 closeout is PASS**.

## Read first

1. M13-T000, M13-T001, M13-T002 closeouts.
2. `docs/tasks/M4-T008-titanic-end-to-end.md` (Titanic precedent).
3. `docs/tasks/M5-T008-house-prices.md` (House Prices RMSLE
   precedent).
4. `docs/tasks/M9-T002-baseline-loop.md` (Spaceship Titanic LR
   baseline precedent — CV 0.79144 ±0.0086 in M9 final review).
5. `tests/test_m9_e2e.py` (closest dry-run replay pattern).
6. `runs/spaceship-titanic/` (existing M9 run artefacts — the
   replay should match their shape, not re-create them).
7. `tools/kca/eval/suites/tool_smoke/` (the T002 driver shape).
8. `docs/architecture/eval-regression-suite.md` (per-suite metric
   contract).

## Scope

1. **Fixtures under `tests/fixtures/`** — frozen sub-samples (≤ ~5 MB
   each), checked into git:
   - `tests/fixtures/titanic/train.csv` — first ~200 rows of the
     real Titanic train.csv, same columns.
   - `tests/fixtures/spaceship-titanic/train.csv` — first ~200 rows
     of the real Spaceship Titanic train.csv. Reuse the existing
     M9 fixture if present.
   - `tests/fixtures/house-prices/train.csv` — first ~200 rows
     (note: this is enough rows for a CV harness to run; not enough
     for realistic scores — that's by design, M13 baselines values
     and is not chasing leaderboard quality).

2. **Three suite modules** under `tools/kca/eval/suites/`:
   - `kaggle_replay_titanic/` — logistic regression on a fixed
     feature set; records `cv_accuracy_mean`, `cv_accuracy_std`,
     `holdout_accuracy`, `fit_time_ms`.
   - `kaggle_replay_spaceship_titanic/` — LR mirror of M9-T002's
     baseline; records same keys.
   - `kaggle_replay_house_prices/` — LR / Ridge mirror of M5-T008;
     records `cv_rmsle_mean`, `cv_rmsle_std`, `holdout_rmsle`,
     `fit_time_ms`.

3. **Determinism.** Each replay seeds `random.seed(0)` +
   `numpy.random.seed(0)` + `sklearn` `random_state=0`. Two
   consecutive runs against the same fixture must produce
   byte-identical `metrics` JSON.

4. **No real Kaggle.** Replays read CSVs from
   `tests/fixtures/<comp>/` — they never call `kaggle competitions
   download`, `kaggle competitions files`, or any `kaggle` CLI.
   Inherit the M10-T007 audit-grep sentinel.

5. **Route plumbing.** The `--route` flag is wired but defaults to
   `mocked`. When `--route mocked` is selected, no LLM call is made
   — the baseline is pure sklearn / pandas. When `--route claude_*`
   is selected, the suite defers to T006's harness (this task does
   not implement T006; the wiring is just an interface stub that
   raises `NotImplementedError` for now, to be filled in T006).

6. **Wire into `kca eval run`.** After T003:
   - `kca eval list --json` shows three new suites
     (`kaggle-replay-titanic`, `kaggle-replay-spaceship-titanic`,
     `kaggle-replay-house-prices`).
   - `kca eval run --suite kaggle-replay-spaceship-titanic --route
     mocked --dry-run --json` exits 0, creates one `eval_runs` row,
     inserts one `eval_results` row per case (default: a single
     `baseline_lr` case per suite).

## Non-goals

- No real Kaggle network calls. None.
- No LLM calls in `--route mocked` (the default).
- No new top-level CLI subcommands.
- No model-route comparison — that's T006.
- No tuning the baseline to a specific score target. M13 baselines
  values; future milestones decide on score-delta gates.
- No notebook/kernel path — that's T004.

## Acceptance criteria
````
