````markdown
# M13 — Loop Prompts

_Evaluation, reliability, and regression suite — measures whether the
platform improves over time._
_For sequential, partly autonomous execution on Arch Linux._
_Prerequisite: M10 exit confirmed (notebook-submission path validated;
see `docs/m10-final-review.md`). M11 (CTF) and M12 (Devpost) are NOT
prerequisites — their eval cases are deferred to follow-ups._
_Shared rules: every Loop Prompt below MUST follow
`docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` (sequencing, no real Kaggle /
Anthropic outside designated paths, DB DSN + sandbox bypass,
per-milestone worktree by default, secret denylist, Discovery / Debate
Gate on `arch:` tasks)._

---

## M13 at a glance

M13 is the first **internal regression milestone** — it does not chase
a leaderboard or ship a user-visible feature. Its job is to make every
later platform change measurable. After M13, an arbitrary code change
on `main` can be evaluated against a fixed set of suites (tool-smoke,
Kaggle replay, notebook/kernel dry-run, reasoning, model-route
comparison) and produce a metrics snapshot that future PRs can be
graded against.

This is also the first milestone whose entry task (`M13-T000`) is
tagged `arch:` and therefore triggers the **Discovery / Debate Gate**
(M9.4): `legacy-archaeologist` (skippable — greenfield), then
`requirements-skeptic`, then `design-red-team`. ADR-0016 must cite all
three transcripts under `docs/evidence/m13/T000/discovery/` before any
implementation begins.

M13 is **not** a leaderboard-chasing milestone and **not** an
LLM-quality milestone. Pass/fail is structural: did the suite run,
did it record the expected metrics, did the report writer produce a
diffable snapshot. The metric *values* are baselined here, not
gated.

Direct entry into M13 is blocked until **all** are true:

- M10 is merged on `main` (`docs/m10-final-review.md` exists and
  reports PASS). The notebook/kernel fixtures from M10-T007 are the
  seed for `M13-T004`.
- M9 dry-run leak (issue #11) remains CLOSED on `main` — the eval
  harness inherits the same secrets posture; if #11 reopens, halt T008.
- Local Supabase container is running; M0–M10 migrations are applied;
  the existing `competitions` / `experiment_runs` / `submissions` /
  `agent_reviews` / `agent_tool_audit` rows from M9 / M10 are
  reachable. M13's new tables sit alongside them.

### What's in scope

| Capability | Owned by | M13 touches |
|---|---|---|
| Regression-suite framework + metrics schema | `docs/adr/0016-eval-regression-suite.md` + `docs/architecture/eval-regression-suite.md` | T000 |
| `eval_suites` / `eval_runs` / `eval_results` tables | `supabase/migrations/0008_m13_eval.sql` + `tools/kca/db.py` | T001 |
| `kca eval` CLI surface (`list`, `run`, `show`, `report`) | `tools/kca/eval.py` + `tools/kca/kca.py` registration | T001 — scaffold; T002–T007 — fill |
| Tool-smoke suite (deterministic, no LLM) | `tools/kca/eval/suites/tool_smoke/` + fixtures | T002 |
| Kaggle classic-practice replay (Titanic / Spaceship Titanic / House Prices) | `tools/kca/eval/suites/kaggle_replay/` + fixtures | T003 |
| Notebook/kernel dry-run regression | `tools/kca/eval/suites/kernel_dryrun/` (reuses M10 fixtures) | T004 |
| Reasoning-heavy benchmark | `tools/kca/eval/suites/reasoning/` + 5–10 fixed prompts + deterministic + rubric judges | T005 |
| Model-route comparison harness | `src/worker/routing.py` reuse + `tools/kca/eval/router.py` + cost budget | T006 |
| Metrics aggregator + Markdown / JSON report | `tools/kca/eval/report.py` + `kca eval report` | T007 |
| CI nightly cron + smoke / e2e tests | `.github/workflows/eval.yml` + `tests/test_m13_smoke.py` + `tests/test_m13_e2e.py` | T008 |
| Final review | `milestone-final-review` skill + `worktree-milestone-pr` skill | T009 |

### What's NOT in scope

- **CTF/lab eval cases.** Deferred to M13.1 (or whatever sub-milestone
  M11 produces). M11 has not landed; its solver-script / writeup
  artefacts are not yet stable enough to baseline against.
- **Hackathon / Devpost eval cases.** Deferred to M13.2 — see M12.
- **Real Kaggle network calls.** None. The whole point of replay is
  that the suites run offline against checked-in fixtures. T006's
  model-route comparison may call real LLM APIs under explicit budget
  cap and `--route` flag; Kaggle remains offline in every suite.
- **Production Supabase.** Local only.
- **New leaderboard chases.** M13 does not push a new Kaggle
  submission, kernel, dataset, or model. M9-T004 and M10-T004 are the
  only "real Kaggle write" rows in the system; M13 reads them but
  does not extend them.
- **Pass/fail thresholds on LLM quality.** M13 baselines values; future
  milestones (M14+) decide whether to gate PRs on score-deltas.
- **New top-level CLI subcommands beyond `kca eval`.** Internal
  helpers and per-suite drivers may live under `tools/kca/eval/`, but
  the CLI surface stays at one new top-level subcommand.

DB / sandbox details: see `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` §3 — the
local `supabase-db` container (`postgresql://postgres:s3cr3t@172.21.0.4:5432/postgres`)
needs `dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true`. T006's optional live-LLM
route also needs sandbox bypass; default is the local-vllm route or
`--dry-run` (mocked LLM via `litellm.mock_completion`).

## GitHub issue / label workflow for M13

Each M13 task is filed as a GitHub issue using the `feature-work.yml`
form (or `test-gap.yml` for T008), labelled per task type. A
canonical M13 proposal issue is filed at planning close and is the
target of `decision:confirmed` for the milestone.

| Task | Issue labels at file time | Labels added by triage | Labels at merge |
|---|---|---|---|
| M13-T000 | `arch:`, `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:eval`, `area:docs`, `decision:needed` | `decision:confirmed` + `ai:ready` after Discovery / Debate Gate transcripts attached | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M13-T001 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:supabase`, `area:eval`, `area:cli` | `ai:ready` (after AC + owner) | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M13-T002 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:eval`, `area:worker` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M13-T003 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:eval`, `area:kaggle` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M13-T004 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:eval`, `area:kaggle`, `area:testing` | `ai:ready` after M10-T007 fixture confirmed present | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M13-T005 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:eval`, `area:worker` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M13-T006 | `type:feature`, `ai:blocked`, `policy:approval-required`, `area:eval`, `area:routing`, `decision:needed` | `decision:confirmed` + `ai:ready` only after live-LLM budget cap confirmed on the M13 proposal issue | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M13-T007 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:eval`, `area:docs` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M13-T008 | `type:test-gap`, `ai:triage`, `area:testing`, `area:ci`, `area:eval` | `ai:ready` only after issue #11 confirmed CLOSED | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M13-T009 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:release`, `area:docs` | `ai:ready` after T000–T008 closed | `ai:implementing` → close |

T000 and T006 are the only tasks that start with `decision:needed`.
T000 because it's `arch:` and the Discovery / Debate Gate verdict
is part of the decision record. T006 because it is the only Loop
Prompt that may make non-mocked, paid LLM calls and needs an
explicit budget cap recorded on the proposal issue.

T008 is gated on issue #11 being CLOSED — same posture as M10-T007.

The PR for each task uses `.github/pull_request_template.md`. T006's
PR is the ONLY M13 PR that may check the "External LLM call" box,
and must link the budget-cap comment from the proposal issue.

## Rollback / stop criteria

Stop the milestone — do **not** advance to the next Loop Prompt —
if any of these is true:

- T006 exceeds the approved live-LLM budget cap. The harness should
  abort cleanly; if it does not, the leak is a P0 bug.
- Any test in the validation suite regresses from green to red.
- The DSN, credentials, or `.env*` are accidentally printed in any
  log, audit row, eval report, or PR. Stop and rotate the credential.
- Any suite mistakenly calls real Kaggle or real-LLM endpoints when
  it should not. The audit-grep sentinel from M10-T007 must apply
  to every M13 suite: 0 lines for `kaggle competitions submit`,
  `kaggle kernels push`, `kaggle datasets create`, `kaggle datasets
  version` reach the kaggle CLI from any test or eval process.
- Issue #11 (dotenv leak) is reopened mid-milestone. Halt T008 work
  until #11 is green again.
- The Discovery / Debate Gate at T000 does not surface a load-bearing
  unknown (eval framework lock-in, schema decision, route comparison
  shape). Pause, request a human review of the three transcripts,
  do not advance to T001.

If M13 needs a new architectural decision mid-flight (e.g.
"reasoning benchmark needs its own DB table", "model-route harness
needs a new run-artefact shape"), pause and update ADR-0016 in a
new revision; do not advance to the next Loop Prompt with hidden
schema drift.
````

````markdown
# M13-T004: Notebook / kernel dry-run regression suite

## Milestone
M13: evaluation, reliability, and regression suite.

## Goal
Add an offline regression suite that exercises the M10 notebook /
kernel-push path under M10-T007's dry-run + audit-grep posture, as
a record-producing eval (not just a pytest). Reuses the existing
M10-T007 fixture (`tests/fixtures/tpu-getting-started/`) — does
NOT add a parallel fixture.

Cases covered: kg-nb round-trip, reviewer-gate firing, decision-API
approval round-trip, `kca kaggle push` credentials-gate refusal.
Metric: count of gates fired + the audit-grep sentinel result.
No real Kaggle, no real Anthropic, no real kernel push.

This task assumes **M13-T002 closeout is PASS** AND **M10-T007 is
merged on `main`** (the fixture and the gating code must already
exist).

## Read first

1. M13-T000, M13-T001, M13-T002 closeouts.
2. M10-T002, M10-T004, M10-T007 closeouts (the path being replayed).
3. `tests/test_m10_e2e.py` — the closest pattern; reuse the
   credentials-gate refusal block almost verbatim.
4. `tools/kca/kg.py::cmd_push` — the gate this suite asserts on.
5. `src/worker/reviewer.py` — the reviewer-gate stub the suite
   triggers.
6. `tests/fixtures/tpu-getting-started/` — DO NOT add a parallel
   fixture.
7. `tools/kca/eval/suites/tool_smoke/` (T002 driver shape).

## Scope

1. **Suite module** `tools/kca/eval/suites/kernel_dryrun/`:
   - Registers as `kernel-dryrun` v0.1.0, category
     `kernel_dryrun`.
   - Four cases, one per assertion (see scope step 2).
   - Reuses `tests/fixtures/tpu-getting-started/` (≤ ~5 MB; 2-class
     stub from M10-T007).

2. **Four cases.** Each emits one `eval_results` row:
   - `kg_nb_roundtrip` — convert the fixture notebook to
     percent-format `.py` and back; assert cell sequence and
     output equivalence (modulo execution timestamps). Metric:
     `cells_equal=True/False`, `latency_ms`.
   - `reviewer_gate_fires` — drive a stub worker that reaches
     `kernel_push`; assert exactly one `agent_reviews` row + one
     `human_decisions` row land with `target_op="kernel_push"`.
     Metric: `gates_fired=1`, `rows_created=2`, `latency_ms`.
   - `decision_api_approve_roundtrip` — POST approve to the
     decision_api (or `kca decisions approve`); assert state flip.
     Skipped cleanly if `SUPABASE_DB_URL` is unset (`status="skip"`).
     Metric: `approved=True`, `latency_ms`.
   - `credentials_gate_refusal` — subprocess invocation of
     `kca kaggle push --competition tpu-getting-started --notebook
     /dev/null --message "m13-eval dry-run — must refuse"` under
     a scrubbed env (`KCA_SKIP_DOTENV=1`, `HOME=tmpdir`); assert
     `payload["ok"]==False` AND `payload["error"]` contains
     `KAGGLE_USERNAME` or `KAGGLE_KEY`. Metric:
     `refused=True`, `payload_keys=[...]`, `latency_ms`.

3. **Audit-grep regression sentinel.** After the suite runs,
   assert `.agent/audit/tool-events.jsonl` (or equivalent) has 0
   lines whose command starts with `kaggle kernels push` or
   `kca kaggle push` for this suite's process — same guard as
   M10-T007, but recorded as a metric in the
   `credentials_gate_refusal` case (`audit_grep_clean=True`).

4. **No real Kaggle.** Inherit the M10-T007 stance: the test
   process must NEVER reach the real kaggle CLI. The suite asserts
   this is the case.

5. **Wire into `kca eval run`.** After T004:
   - `kca eval list --json` shows `kernel-dryrun` as a registered
     suite.
   - `kca eval run --suite kernel-dryrun --route mocked --dry-run
     --json` exits 0, creates one `eval_runs` row, inserts 4
     `eval_results` rows (with one expected `skip` if
     `SUPABASE_DB_URL` is unset).

## Non-goals

- No real Kaggle calls. None.
- No real `kaggle kernels push` — that is exactly the leak this
  suite guards against.
- No new fixtures — reuse M10-T007's.
- No extension of `tools/kca/kg.py::cmd_push`. If the gating code
  needs fixing, file a separate issue and pause this task.
- No LLM calls — `--route mocked` only.

## Acceptance criteria

- `tools/kca/eval/suites/kernel_dryrun/` registers as
  `kernel-dryrun`; `kca eval list` shows it.
- All four cases produce `eval_results` rows on a clean run; the
  `decision_api_approve_roundtrip` case may report `status="skip"`
  cleanly without `SUPABASE_DB_URL`.
- `credentials_gate_refusal` case has `refused=True` AND
  `audit_grep_clean=True`.
- Audit-grep guard PASSes: 0 lines for `kaggle kernels push` /
  `kca kaggle push` from the suite's subprocesses.
- Two consecutive runs produce identical `metrics` per case
  (modulo `latency_ms`).
- `ruff check .` + `ruff format --check .` clean.
- `pytest tests/ services/decision_api/tests` — 0 regressions vs
  T003 baseline.

## Permissions

- `git add` / `git commit` deferred to milestone closeout.
- LOCAL_WRITE Supabase — ALLOWED.
- No real Kaggle calls.
- No real LLM calls.

## Closeout format

```
M13-T004 closeout
  Suite: tools/kca/eval/suites/kernel_dryrun/ (registered as `kernel-dryrun` v0.1.0)
  Cases: 4 (kg_nb_roundtrip, reviewer_gate_fires, decision_api_approve_roundtrip, credentials_gate_refusal)
  Fixture reuse: tests/fixtures/tpu-getting-started/ (no parallel fixture added)

  eval_results rows: 4 (pass / skip / fail / error counts)
  credentials_gate_refusal: refused=True, audit_grep_clean=True
  Audit-grep guard: 0 lines matching forbidden Kaggle CLI commands
  Determinism check: 2 consecutive runs — same metrics per case: YES
  pytest: <X> passed / <Y> skipped (0 regressions)
  ruff check + ruff format --check: clean
  Acceptance: PASS
  Next: M13-T005 (reasoning-heavy benchmark)
```

## Related issues

- M13 proposal issue.
- #11 (dotenv leak) — should still be CLOSED at run time. If
  reopened, halt and surface.

## Stop condition

Stop after 80 turns. HALT and ask if:
- The audit-grep sentinel FAILs at any point — that is exactly
  the regression this suite is designed to catch. Investigate
  which subprocess reached the kaggle CLI and file as a P0.
- `tests/fixtures/tpu-getting-started/` is missing or empty.
  M10-T007 must have landed first; if it has not, this task is
  blocked.
- Two runs produce divergent metrics in a way that suggests
  hidden state (often: leftover audit log lines from a previous
  run; ensure the tmpdir is fresh).
````

```python
"""tool_smoke — deterministic per-tool smoke suite (M13-T002).

Exercises the worker tool registry (``src/worker/tools.py``) with a
checked-in case list (``cases.yaml``). Every case:

- runs against a per-run tmpdir (no network, no DB, no LLM);
- is fully deterministic — seeded ``random.seed(0)`` + frozen fixtures;
- emits the M13 ``tool_smoke`` metric bag into ``eval_results.metrics``:
  ``latency_ms``, ``output_match`` (subset-match boolean),
  ``output_keys`` (sorted JSON top-level keys; ``[]`` for plain text).

The suite never invokes the kaggle CLI nor any remote API. A post-run
audit-grep guard verifies that ``.agent/audit.jsonl`` and the suite's
own captured command log contain zero hits for the M10-T007 forbidden
patterns (``kaggle competitions submit``, ``kaggle kernels push``,
``kaggle datasets create``, ``kaggle datasets version``).

Registration shape: ``register(db)`` is called by
``tools.kca.eval.register_all``; it upserts the row in ``eval_suites``
when a DB is configured AND returns the in-process suite spec dict
either way.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import random
import re
import shutil
import sys
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

try:
    import yaml  # type: ignore
except ImportError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - hard requirement
    raise RuntimeError("tool_smoke suite requires PyYAML; pip install pyyaml") from exc

SUITE_NAME = "tool-smoke"
SUITE_VERSION = "0.1.0"
SUITE_CATEGORY = "tool_smoke"
SUITE_DESCRIPTION = (
    "Deterministic per-tool smoke suite exercising src/worker/tools.py. "
    "≥10 cases, no LLM, no Kaggle network."
)

_SUITE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
_CASES_PATH = _SUITE_DIR / "cases.yaml"
_REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[5]
_FIXTURE_DIR = _REPO_ROOT / "tests" / "fixtures" / "tool_smoke"

# M10-T007 forbidden patterns. Inherited by every M13 suite.
AUDIT_GREP_FORBIDDEN = (
    "kaggle competitions submit",
    "kaggle kernels push",
    "kaggle datasets create",
    "kaggle datasets version",
)

# Policy used by the suite. Allows ``python *`` so the
# run_bash_allowed_pattern case can shell out to a one-shot python.
# Hard-deny entries in src/worker/tools.py still take priority over
# this allow-list (kaggle submit, sudo, rm -rf, git push, ``..`` path
# traversal).
_SUITE_BASH_PATTERNS = ["python *", "kca *", "pytest *"]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Case loader.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Case:
    name: str
    tool: str
    category: str
    input: dict
    expected_status: str
    expected_contains: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    expected_keys: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    workspace: str = "tmpdir"
    depends_on: str | None = None


def _load_cases() -> list[Case]:
    if not _CASES_PATH.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"cases.yaml missing at {_CASES_PATH}")
    raw = yaml.safe_load(_CASES_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) or {}
    cases_raw = raw.get("cases") or []
    out: list[Case] = []
    for c in cases_raw:
        out.append(
            Case(
                name=c["name"],
                tool=c["tool"],
                category=c.get("category", "read_only"),
                input=dict(c.get("input") or {}),
                expected_status=c.get("expected_status", "pass"),
                expected_contains=tuple(c.get("expected_contains") or ()),
                expected_keys=tuple(sorted(c.get("expected_keys") or ())),
                workspace=c.get("workspace", "tmpdir"),
                depends_on=c.get("depends_on"),
            )
        )
    return out


def cases() -> list[Case]:
    """Public iterator of cases — used by the runner and tests."""
    return _load_cases()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Per-run execution.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass
class CaseResult:
    case_name: str
    status: str  # pass | fail | skip | error
    metrics: dict
    latency_ms: int
    error_text: str | None = None
    tool_output_preview: str = ""


@dataclass
class RunOutcome:
    results: list[CaseResult] = field(default_factory=list)
    audit_grep_violations: int = 0
    audit_grep_lines: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    total_cases: int = 0
    total_pass: int = 0
    total_fail: int = 0
    total_skip: int = 0
    total_error: int = 0


def _output_keys_from(output: str) -> list[str]:
    """Return sorted top-level JSON keys, or [] when output is not a JSON object."""
    if not output:
        return []
    stripped = output.strip()
    if not stripped or stripped[0] not in "{[":
        return []
    try:
        parsed = json.loads(stripped)
    except Exception:
        return []
    if isinstance(parsed, dict):
        return sorted(parsed.keys())
    if isinstance(parsed, list) and parsed and isinstance(parsed[0], dict):
        # For arrays of objects (grep_workspace), expose the FIRST row's keys
        # so the contract stays useful while still being deterministic.
        return sorted(parsed[0].keys())
    return []


def _subset_match(output: str, expected_contains: tuple[str, ...]) -> bool:
    if not expected_contains:
        return True
    return all(needle in output for needle in expected_contains)


def _build_executor(workspace: Path):
    """Construct a ToolExecutor with a suite-specific JobPolicy."""
    # Lazy import keeps the suite module importable without src/ on sys.path
    # (e.g. when ``kca eval list`` runs and only enumerates suites).
    sys.path.insert(0, str(_REPO_ROOT))
    from src.worker._types import JobPolicy  # noqa: E402
    from src.worker.tools import ToolExecutor  # noqa: E402

    policy = JobPolicy(
        allowed_tool_patterns=list(_SUITE_BASH_PATTERNS),
        max_side_effect="LOCAL_WRITE",
    )
    return ToolExecutor(workspace, policy)


def _materialise_workspace(case: Case, fixture_dir: Path, tmpdir: Path) -> Path:
    """Return the workspace path for a case.

    fixture cases run against a copy of the read-only fixture dir to keep
    the source tree pristine; tmpdir cases run against a shared per-run
    tmpdir so write/edit chains work across cases.
    """
    if case.workspace == "fixture":
        # The fixture dir is read-only by convention; copy into a per-case
        # subdir so a buggy tool (e.g. write_file with a fixture path)
        # never mutates the checked-in tree.
        case_ws = tmpdir / "fixture" / case.name
        if not case_ws.exists():
            shutil.copytree(fixture_dir, case_ws)
        return case_ws
    return tmpdir / "tmpdir"


def _run_case(case: Case, fixture_dir: Path, tmpdir: Path) -> CaseResult:
    workspace = _materialise_workspace(case, fixture_dir, tmpdir)
    workspace.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    executor = _build_executor(workspace)

    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    output_str = ""
    status = "pass"
    error_text: str | None = None
    try:
        raw = executor.execute(case.tool, dict(case.input))
        output_str = raw if isinstance(raw, str) else str(raw)
    except Exception as exc:  # ApprovalRequired or unexpected
        status = "error"
        error_text = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
        output_str = ""
    latency_ms = int((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000)

    output_keys = _output_keys_from(output_str)
    output_match = _subset_match(output_str, case.expected_contains)
    if not output_match and status == "pass":
        status = "fail"
        error_text = error_text or "subset-match failed"
    if case.expected_keys and tuple(output_keys) != case.expected_keys:
        if status == "pass":
            status = "fail"
            error_text = error_text or (
                f"expected_keys mismatch: got={output_keys} "
                f"expected={list(case.expected_keys)}"
            )

    metrics = {
        "latency_ms": latency_ms,
        "output_match": output_match,
        "output_keys": output_keys,
        # Per-suite extras (kept inside the metric bag, not separate columns).
        "tool": case.tool,
        "expected_status": case.expected_status,
        "category": case.category,
    }
    return CaseResult(
        case_name=case.name,
        status=status,
        metrics=metrics,
        latency_ms=latency_ms,
        error_text=error_text,
        tool_output_preview=output_str[:200],
    )


def _audit_grep(audit_path: Path, started_after_ns: int) -> tuple[int, list[str]]:
    """Return (violation_count, sample_lines) for the M10-T007 forbidden patterns.

    Only inspects audit lines whose ``timestamp`` (ISO-8601 string) parses
    to a moment AFTER the suite started — older lines from previous
    sessions are not the suite's responsibility.
    """
    if not audit_path.exists():
        return 0, []
    violations: list[str] = []
    pattern = re.compile("|".join(re.escape(p) for p in AUDIT_GREP_FORBIDDEN))
    with audit_path.open("r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
        for line in fh:
            if pattern.search(line):
                violations.append(line.rstrip("\n"))
    return len(violations), violations[:20]


def run(
    *,
    route: str = "mocked",
    seed: int = 0,
    tmpdir: Path | None = None,
    audit_path: Path | None = None,
) -> RunOutcome:
    """Execute every case in cases.yaml and return a RunOutcome.

    Side-effects: writes inside ``tmpdir`` only. Never touches the DB —
    the runner in ``tools/kca/eval/cli.py`` is the only path that
    persists rows to ``eval_runs`` / ``eval_results``.
    """
    random.seed(seed)
    started_ns = time.time_ns()

    if tmpdir is None:
        import tempfile

        tmpdir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="m13-tool-smoke-"))
    else:
        tmpdir = Path(tmpdir)
    tmpdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    fixture_dir = _FIXTURE_DIR
    if not fixture_dir.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"tool_smoke fixture missing: {fixture_dir} — checked-in fixture required"
        )

    outcome = RunOutcome()
    for case in _load_cases():
        result = _run_case(case, fixture_dir, tmpdir)
        outcome.results.append(result)
        outcome.total_cases += 1
        if result.status == "pass":
            outcome.total_pass += 1
        elif result.status == "fail":
            outcome.total_fail += 1
        elif result.status == "skip":
            outcome.total_skip += 1
        else:
            outcome.total_error += 1

    if audit_path is None:
        audit_path = _REPO_ROOT / ".agent" / "audit.jsonl"
    v_count, v_lines = _audit_grep(audit_path, started_ns)
    outcome.audit_grep_violations = v_count
    outcome.audit_grep_lines = v_lines
    return outcome


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Registration hook (called by tools.kca.eval.register_all).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def register(db_module: object | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return the suite spec; upsert into ``eval_suites`` when a DB is set.

    The runner stays purely functional: ``register`` records "this suite
    exists"; ``cmd_run`` in ``tools/kca/eval/cli.py`` invokes ``run()`` to
    produce results.
    """
    spec: dict[str, Any] = {
        "name": SUITE_NAME,
        "category": SUITE_CATEGORY,
        "version": SUITE_VERSION,
        "description": SUITE_DESCRIPTION,
        "default_route": "mocked",
        "requires_db": False,
        "requires_remote": False,
        "runner": run,  # in-process handle for cmd_run
        "case_count": len(_load_cases()),
    }
    if db_module is not None:
        try:
            suite_id = db_module.register_eval_suite(
                name=SUITE_NAME,
                description=SUITE_DESCRIPTION,
                version=SUITE_VERSION,
                category=SUITE_CATEGORY,
                metadata={"case_count": spec["case_count"]},
            )
            spec["suite_id"] = suite_id
        except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - DB-optional
            print(
                f"[tool-smoke] db registration skipped: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
    return spec
```

```python
"""``kca eval`` subcommand implementation (M13-T001 scaffold).

Four verbs:

- ``kca eval list`` — list suites registered via ``register_all()``.
- ``kca eval run`` — run one or more suites. Until T002+ land their
  per-suite drivers, every invocation refuses with
  ``{"ok": false, "error": "NO_SUITES_REGISTERED"}``.
- ``kca eval show <run_id>`` — print roll-up rows for one ``eval_runs``
  id. Returns ``{"ok": false, "error": "NOT_FOUND"}`` on miss.
- ``kca eval report <run_id>`` — defers to T007's aggregator;
  refuses with ``REPORT_AGGREGATOR_NOT_YET_IMPLEMENTED`` until then.

The scaffold writes nothing to the DB unless ``run`` actually dispatches
suites (which it cannot do until T002+). It is therefore safe to invoke
in any environment, including CI without a DB.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import importlib
import json
import os
import pkgutil
import sys
from typing import Any

from _types import EXIT_OK, EXIT_RUNTIME, SideEffect


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Suite registry (in-process; populated by register_all()).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Each entry is the dict the suite module's register(db) function returned.
# Minimum keys (per ADR-0016): "name", "category", "version".
_REGISTRY: list[dict[str, Any]] = []


def _emit(payload: dict, side_effect: SideEffect = SideEffect.READ_ONLY) -> None:
    out = {"side_effect": side_effect.value, **payload}
    print(json.dumps(out, ensure_ascii=False))


def _maybe_db_module() -> object | None:
    """Resolve the kca db module if a DSN is configured; else None.

    The eval CLI is DB-optional: ``list`` / ``run --dry-run`` against the
    in-process registry work without a DB; ``show`` / ``run`` that
    persists rows need ``SUPABASE_DB_URL``.
    """
    if not os.environ.get("SUPABASE_DB_URL"):
        return None
    try:
        import db as db_mod  # local import; lives at tools/kca/db.py
    except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
        return None
    return db_mod


def register_all(db_module: object | None = None) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Discover and register every suite under ``tools/kca/eval/suites/``.

    Each suite module is expected to expose a ``register(db)`` callable
    returning a dict with at least ``name`` / ``category`` / ``version``.
    Suites that raise on import are skipped with a stderr warning so a
    single broken suite does not break the whole CLI.

    T001 ships this hook with zero suites; T002+ populate the suites
    directory.
    """
    _REGISTRY.clear()
    # Re-import via __package__ so this works under both `python -m
    # tools.kca.kca` (where the parent is `tools.kca.eval`) and a flat
    # sys.path layout where the parent is just `eval`.
    parent = __package__ or "tools.kca.eval"
    suites_pkg = importlib.import_module(f"{parent}.suites")

    for mod_info in pkgutil.iter_modules(suites_pkg.__path__):
        if mod_info.name.startswith("_"):
            continue
        full_name = f"{suites_pkg.__name__}.{mod_info.name}"
        try:
            mod = importlib.import_module(full_name)
        except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
            print(
                f"[kca eval] suite '{mod_info.name}' import failed: {exc}",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            continue
        register_fn = getattr(mod, "register", None)
        if register_fn is None:
            print(
                f"[kca eval] suite '{mod_info.name}' missing register(db); skipped",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            continue
        try:
            spec = register_fn(db_module)
        except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
            print(
                f"[kca eval] suite '{mod_info.name}' register() raised: {exc}",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            continue
        if not isinstance(spec, dict):
            print(
                f"[kca eval] suite '{mod_info.name}' register() returned "
                f"{type(spec).__name__}; expected dict",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            continue
        _REGISTRY.append(spec)
    return list(_REGISTRY)


def _ensure_registered(db_module: object | None = None) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Lazy re-registration — populates _REGISTRY on first verb call."""
    if not _REGISTRY:
        # Prefer the caller-supplied module; fall back to env-discovered.
        register_all(db_module if db_module is not None else _maybe_db_module())
    return _REGISTRY


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Verb implementations.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def cmd_list(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    suites = _ensure_registered()
    payload = {
        "ok": True,
        "suites": [
            {
                "name": s.get("name"),
                "category": s.get("category"),
                "version": s.get("version"),
                "description": s.get("description"),
            }
            for s in suites
        ],
        "count": len(suites),
    }
    if getattr(args, "json", False):
        _emit(payload)
    else:
        if not suites:
            print("(no suites registered)")
        else:
            for s in suites:
                print(f"{s.get('name'):<32} {s.get('category'):<20} {s.get('version')}")
        # Always emit a JSON line at the end so callers can pipe.
        _emit(payload)
    return EXIT_OK


def cmd_run(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    db_mod = _maybe_db_module()
    suites = _ensure_registered(db_mod)
    if not suites:
        _emit({"ok": False, "error": "NO_SUITES_REGISTERED"})
        return EXIT_RUNTIME

    # Resolve target suites.
    if getattr(args, "all", False):
        targets = list(suites)
    else:
        wanted = [s.strip() for s in getattr(args, "suite", []) if s and s.strip()]
        if not wanted:
            _emit({"ok": False, "error": "SUITE_REQUIRED"})
            return EXIT_RUNTIME
        by_name = {s.get("name"): s for s in suites}
        targets = []
        unknown: list[str] = []
        for w in wanted:
            if w in by_name:
                targets.append(by_name[w])
            else:
                unknown.append(w)
        if unknown:
            _emit(
                {
                    "ok": False,
                    "error": "UNKNOWN_SUITE",
                    "unknown": unknown,
                    "available": sorted(by_name.keys()),
                }
            )
            return EXIT_RUNTIME

    route = getattr(args, "route", None) or "mocked"
    dry_run = bool(getattr(args, "dry_run", False))
    budget = getattr(args, "budget", None)

    # The eval module itself only authorises mocked / local routes; any
    # remote route requires KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1 AND a non-null budget.
    if route not in {"mocked", "local_vllm"}:
        if os.environ.get("KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE") != "1":
            _emit({"ok": False, "error": "REMOTE_ROUTE_BLOCKED", "route": route})
            return EXIT_RUNTIME
        if budget is None:
            _emit({"ok": False, "error": "BUDGET_REQUIRED_FOR_REMOTE", "route": route})
            return EXIT_RUNTIME

    # Persist the eval_runs row when a DB is configured. ``--dry-run``
    # mirrors into ``eval_runs.dry_run`` per the schema; the row STILL
    # lands so the run is auditable. The dry-run flag is the data
    # consumer's signal to discount the metrics, not a "skip the insert"
    # toggle.
    run_id: str | None = None
    if db_mod is not None:
        try:
            run_id = db_mod.start_eval_run(
                route=route,
                dry_run=dry_run,
                budget_usd=budget,
                metadata={
                    "suite_names": [s.get("name") for s in targets],
                    "trigger": "kca-eval-run",
                },
            )
        except Exception as exc:
            _emit(
                {
                    "ok": False,
                    "error": "DB_ERROR",
                    "phase": "start_eval_run",
                    "error_type": type(exc).__name__,
                    "message": str(exc),
                }
            )
            return EXIT_RUNTIME

    suite_summaries: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    totals = {"total_cases": 0, "total_pass": 0, "total_fail": 0, "total_skip": 0}
    total_error = 0
    audit_violations_total = 0

    for spec in targets:
        runner = spec.get("runner")
        suite_name = spec.get("name") or "<unknown>"
        suite_id = spec.get("suite_id")
        if not callable(runner):
            # Spec registered (DB row exists) but no in-process runner —
            # legitimate during scaffold tests where a future suite is
            # registered without an implementation yet.
            suite_summaries.append(
                {
                    "name": suite_name,
                    "status": "skipped",
                    "reason": "NO_RUNNER",
                }
            )
            continue

        try:
            outcome = runner(route=route)
        except Exception as exc:
            suite_summaries.append(
                {
                    "name": suite_name,
                    "status": "errored",
                    "error_type": type(exc).__name__,
                    "message": str(exc),
                }
            )
            total_error += 1
            continue

        # Persist per-case results.
        cases_persisted = 0
        for r in outcome.results:
            if db_mod is not None and run_id is not None and suite_id is not None:
                try:
                    db_mod.record_eval_result(
                        run_id=run_id,
                        suite_id=suite_id,
                        case_name=r.case_name,
                        route=route,
                        status=r.status,
                        metrics=r.metrics,
                        latency_ms=r.latency_ms,
                        cost_usd=0.0,
                        error_text=r.error_text,
                    )
                    cases_persisted += 1
                except Exception as exc:
                    # Surface the DB error in the summary; do not abort
                    # remaining cases so the suite still reports.
                    suite_summaries.append(
                        {
                            "name": suite_name,
                            "case": r.case_name,
                            "status": "db_error",
                            "error_type": type(exc).__name__,
                            "message": str(exc),
                        }
                    )

        totals["total_cases"] += outcome.total_cases
        totals["total_pass"] += outcome.total_pass
        totals["total_fail"] += outcome.total_fail
        totals["total_skip"] += outcome.total_skip
        total_error += outcome.total_error
        audit_violations_total += outcome.audit_grep_violations

        suite_summaries.append(
            {
                "name": suite_name,
                "case_count": outcome.total_cases,
                "pass": outcome.total_pass,
                "fail": outcome.total_fail,
                "skip": outcome.total_skip,
                "error": outcome.total_error,
                "audit_grep_violations": outcome.audit_grep_violations,
                "audit_grep_sample": outcome.audit_grep_lines,
                "results": [
                    {
                        "case_name": r.case_name,
                        "status": r.status,
                        "latency_ms": r.latency_ms,
                        "metrics": r.metrics,
                        "error_text": r.error_text,
                    }
                    for r in outcome.results
                ],
                "rows_persisted": cases_persisted,
            }
        )

    if db_mod is not None and run_id is not None:
        try:
            db_mod.finish_eval_run(
                run_id=run_id,
                totals=totals,
                cost_usd=0.0,
                aborted_on_budget=False,
            )
        except Exception as exc:
            _emit(
                {
                    "ok": False,
                    "error": "DB_ERROR",
                    "phase": "finish_eval_run",
                    "run_id": run_id,
                    "error_type": type(exc).__name__,
                    "message": str(exc),
                }
            )
            return EXIT_RUNTIME

    payload = {
        "ok": True,
        "run_id": run_id,
        "route": route,
        "dry_run": dry_run,
        "totals": {**totals, "total_error": total_error},
        "audit_grep_violations": audit_violations_total,
        "suites": suite_summaries,
    }
    _emit(payload, SideEffect.LOCAL_WRITE)
    return EXIT_OK


def cmd_show(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    run_id = (getattr(args, "run_id", None) or "").strip()
    if not run_id:
        _emit({"ok": False, "error": "RUN_ID_REQUIRED"})
        return EXIT_RUNTIME
    # DB optional: if SUPABASE_DB_URL is unset we cannot resolve the run,
    # so surface NOT_FOUND consistently with a missing row.
    if not os.environ.get("SUPABASE_DB_URL"):
        _emit({"ok": False, "error": "NOT_FOUND", "reason": "DB_NOT_CONFIGURED"})
        return EXIT_RUNTIME
    import db as db_mod  # local import; module is at tools/kca/db.py

    try:
        rows = db_mod.fetch_eval_results(run_id)
    except Exception as exc:
        _emit(
            {
                "ok": False,
                "error": "DB_ERROR",
                "error_type": type(exc).__name__,
                "message": str(exc),
            }
        )
        return EXIT_RUNTIME
    if not rows:
        _emit({"ok": False, "error": "NOT_FOUND", "run_id": run_id})
        return EXIT_RUNTIME
    payload = {
        "ok": True,
        "run_id": run_id,
        "count": len(rows),
        "results": [_json_safe(r) for r in rows],
    }
    _emit(payload, SideEffect.READ_ONLY)
    return EXIT_OK


def cmd_report(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    # T007 owns the report aggregator. T001 is a thin shim.
    _emit({"ok": False, "error": "REPORT_AGGREGATOR_NOT_YET_IMPLEMENTED"})
    return EXIT_RUNTIME


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Argparse wiring.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def add_parsers(sub: argparse._SubParsersAction) -> None:
    ev = sub.add_parser(
        "eval",
        help="Evaluation regression-suite harness (M13).",
        description=(
            "M13 regression-suite framework. Four verbs: list, run, show, "
            "report. T001 scaffolds the surface; T002+ land per-suite "
            "drivers."
        ),
    )
    ev_sub = ev.add_subparsers(dest="eval_cmd", required=True)

    # list ------------------------------------------------------------------
    p_list = ev_sub.add_parser("list", help="List registered eval suites.")
    p_list.add_argument(
        "--category",
        help="Filter by suite category (tool_smoke / kaggle_replay / ...).",
    )
    p_list.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    p_list.set_defaults(func=cmd_list)

    # run -------------------------------------------------------------------
    p_run = ev_sub.add_parser(
        "run",
        help="Run one or more suites. Refuses if no suites are registered.",
    )
    p_run.add_argument(
        "--suite",
        action="append",
        default=[],
        help="Suite name to run; repeat for multiple.",
    )
    p_run.add_argument(
        "--all",
        action="store_true",
        help="Run every registered suite.",
    )
    p_run.add_argument(
        "--route",
        default="mocked",
        help="Route key (mocked / local_vllm / claude_* / gpt_*). Default: mocked.",
    )
    p_run.add_argument(
        "--dry-run",
        action="store_true",
        help="Walk through the suite without persisting eval_results rows.",
    )
    p_run.add_argument(
        "--budget",
        type=float,
        default=None,
        help="Hard cost cap in USD; required for any non-mocked / non-local route.",
    )
    p_run.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    p_run.set_defaults(func=cmd_run)

    # show ------------------------------------------------------------------
    p_show = ev_sub.add_parser(
        "show",
        help="Print eval_results rows for a given run id.",
    )
    p_show.add_argument("run_id", help="UUID of the eval_runs row.")
    p_show.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    p_show.set_defaults(func=cmd_show)

    # report ----------------------------------------------------------------
    p_report = ev_sub.add_parser(
        "report",
        help="Roll up eval_results into JSON + Markdown (T007).",
    )
    p_report.add_argument("run_id", help="UUID of the eval_runs row.")
    grp = p_report.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    grp.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    grp.add_argument("--md", action="store_true")
    p_report.add_argument("--out", help="Output path (default: stdout).")
    p_report.set_defaults(func=cmd_report)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers.

def _json_safe(d: dict) -> dict:
    """Coerce psycopg row values to JSON-serialisable types."""
    out: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for k, v in d.items():
        if hasattr(v, "isoformat"):  # datetime / date / time
            out[k] = v.isoformat()
        elif hasattr(v, "hex") and not isinstance(v, (bytes, bytearray, str)):
            # UUID
            out[k] = str(v)
        else:
            try:
                json.dumps(v)
                out[k] = v
            except TypeError:
                out[k] = str(v)
    return out
```

```python
def _sha256_file(p: Path) -> str:
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with p.open("rb") as f:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
            h.update(chunk)
    return h.hexdigest()


def _walk_files(root: Path) -> list[Path]:
    out: list[Path] = []
    for child in sorted(root.rglob("*")):
        if child.is_file() and child.name != "manifest.json":
            out.append(child)
    return out


def cmd_download(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    se = SideEffect.LOCAL_WRITE
    competition = args.competition
    path_str = args.path or str(Path.cwd() / "data" / competition)
    path = Path(path_str)
    path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    manifest_path = path / "manifest.json"

    existing: dict = {"files": []}
    if manifest_path.exists():
        try:
            existing = json.loads(manifest_path.read_text())
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            existing = {"files": []}

    skipped = 0
    if args.resume and existing.get("files"):
        # Walk existing manifest; if file on disk matches sha256, skip its
        # re-download by removing it from a "to download" list. Since the
        # kaggle CLI fetches the whole bundle, we cannot truly skip per-file
        # — but we record how many files matched so the caller knows the
        # resume comparison ran. The actual download is still invoked unless
        # every file matched.
        all_matched = True
        for entry in existing.get("files", []):
            target = path / entry["name"]
            if target.exists() and _sha256_file(target) == entry.get("sha256"):
                skipped += 1
            else:
                all_matched = False
        if all_matched and skipped > 0:
            # Nothing left to fetch; just refresh manifest and return.
            return _refresh_manifest_and_emit(
                competition=competition,
                path=path,
                manifest_path=manifest_path,
                skipped=skipped,
                rc=0,
                stdout="",
                stderr="",
                ran_kaggle=False,
                side_effect=se,
            )

    # Run kaggle CLI; if it isn't installed or creds missing, surface a
    # graceful error and still build/refresh the manifest from whatever is
    # already on disk (useful for tests and --resume scenarios).
    rc = 0
    stdout = ""
    stderr = ""
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run(
            ["kaggle", "competitions", "download", "-c", competition, "-p", str(path)],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
        )
        rc = proc.returncode
        stdout = proc.stdout or ""
        stderr = proc.stderr or ""
    except FileNotFoundError as e:
        rc = 127
        stderr = f"kaggle CLI not found: {e}"

    return _refresh_manifest_and_emit(
        competition=competition,
        path=path,
        manifest_path=manifest_path,
        skipped=skipped,
        rc=rc,
        stdout=stdout,
        stderr=stderr,
        ran_kaggle=True,
        side_effect=se,
    )


def _refresh_manifest_and_emit(
    *,
    competition: str,
    path: Path,
    manifest_path: Path,
    skipped: int,
    rc: int,
    stdout: str,
    stderr: str,
    ran_kaggle: bool,
    side_effect: SideEffect,
```

```python
def _check_approval_gate(operation: str, policy: dict) -> None:
    """Raise ApprovalRequired if `policy` (or defaults) gates `operation`.

    KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1 remains an emergency CI override.
    """
    gates = (policy or {}).get("approval_gates", {})
    requires = gates.get(operation, OPERATION_DEFAULTS.get(operation, True))
    if requires and not os.environ.get(_GATE_ENV):
        raise ApprovalRequired(operation, policy or {})


def _gate(side_effect: SideEffect, command_name: str) -> tuple[bool, str | None]:
    if side_effect in (SideEffect.READ_ONLY, SideEffect.LOCAL_WRITE):
        return True, None
    if os.environ.get(_GATE_ENV) == "1":
        warn(f"REMOTE OPERATION: kaggle {command_name} — {_GATE_ENV} is set")
        return True, None
    return False, f"remote operation requires {_GATE_ENV}=1 and human approval"


def _record_approval(command_name: str, options: dict) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
    """Insert a pending human_decisions row. Returns (approval_id, warning).

    Best-effort: DB failures never block the refusal path. Caller emits the
    blocked envelope regardless.
    """
    args_summary = ", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in options.items() if v is not None)
    prompt = f"Approve Kaggle {command_name} ({args_summary or 'no args'})"
    try:
        approval_id = db.insert_approval_request(
            decision_type=f"kaggle.{command_name}",
            prompt=prompt,
            options=options,
        )
        return approval_id, None
    except Exception as e:
        return None, f"approval recording failed: {type(e).__name__}: {e}"
```

```python
def insert_approval_request(
    decision_type: str,
    prompt: str,
    options: dict | list | None = None,
    session_id: str | None = None,
    project_id: str | None = None,
    requested_by: str | None = "kca",
    job_id: str | None = None,
    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,
) -> str:
    """Insert a pending human_decisions row. Return its id (uuid str)."""
    project_id = project_id or DEFAULT_PROJECT_ID
    options = options or []
    return _with_conn(
        conn,
        _insert_approval_request,
        decision_type,
        prompt,
        options,
        session_id,
        project_id,
        requested_by,
        job_id,
    )


def _insert_approval_request(
    conn: "psycopg.Connection",
    decision_type: str,
    prompt: str,
    options: dict | list,
    session_id: str | None,
    project_id: str,
    requested_by: str | None,
    job_id: str | None,
) -> str:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            """
            insert into human_decisions
              (project_id, session_id, decision_type, prompt, options,
               requested_by, job_id)
            values (%s::uuid, %s::uuid, %s, %s, %s::jsonb, %s, %s::uuid)
            returning id::text
            """,
            (
                project_id,
                session_id,
                decision_type,
                prompt,
                json.dumps(options),
                requested_by,
                job_id,
            ),
        )
        row = cur.fetchone()
    conn.commit()
    assert row is not None
    return row["id"]


def get_decision(
    decision_id: str,
    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,
) -> dict:
    """Fetch one human_decisions row. Raises KeyError if not found."""
    return _with_conn(conn, _get_decision, decision_id)


def _get_decision(conn: "psycopg.Connection", decision_id: str) -> dict:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("SELECT * FROM human_decisions WHERE id = %s::uuid", (decision_id,))
        row = cur.fetchone()
    if row is None:
        raise KeyError(f"decision not found: {decision_id}")
```

```python
"""FastAPI action service for the M8 Decision Gate UI.

The browser never holds a service-role Supabase key. It posts to
``/decision/<id>/approve|reject|ask-improve``; this service re-uses the
existing ``tools/kca/decisions.py`` functions and ``tools/kca/db.py`` writes
so the M7 permission policy stays authoritative.

Auth: a shared token in ``KCA_DECISION_API_TOKEN``. Requests must include the
matching ``X-Decision-Api-Token`` header. Multi-user auth lands in M9+.

Testing: pass a ``decisions_module`` override (e.g. via dependency injection)
to swap in a mocked DB layer.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hmac
import os
from typing import Callable, Optional

from fastapi import FastAPI, Header, HTTPException
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


TOKEN_ENV = "KCA_DECISION_API_TOKEN"


class ApproveBody(BaseModel):
    reason: Optional[str] = Field(default=None, max_length=2000)


class RejectBody(BaseModel):
    reason: str = Field(..., min_length=8, max_length=2000)


class AskImproveBody(BaseModel):
    feedback: str = Field(..., min_length=1, max_length=4000)
    metric_target: Optional[str] = None


def _check_token(provided: Optional[str]) -> None:
    expected = os.environ.get(TOKEN_ENV, "")
    if not expected:
        # If the server has no token configured, accept any (local dev only).
        return
    if not provided or not hmac.compare_digest(provided, expected):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="invalid token")


def make_app(
    decisions_module: Optional[object] = None,
    audit_logger: Optional[Callable] = None,
) -> FastAPI:
    """Construct the FastAPI app.

    ``decisions_module`` exposes ``get_decision``, ``resolve_decision``, and
    ``append_job_event``. Tests pass a fake module to avoid touching Supabase.
    """
    app = FastAPI(title="kca decision_api", version="0.1.0")

    def _resolve_db():
        if decisions_module is not None:
            return decisions_module
        import sys
        from pathlib import Path

        sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "tools" / "kca"))
        import db as _db  # type: ignore

        return _db

    def _audit(*, decision: str, decision_id: str, reason: Optional[str]) -> None:
        if audit_logger is not None:
            audit_logger(
                decision=decision, decision_id=decision_id, reason=reason or ""
            )
            return
        try:
            from tools.kca.agent.audit import log_policy_decision  # type: ignore

            log_policy_decision(
                tool="decision_api",
                operation=f"decision_{decision}",
                decision="allow",
                policy_profile="default",
                args={"decision_id": decision_id, "reason_len": len(reason or "")},
            )
        except Exception:
            pass

    def _get_pending(decision_id: str):
        _db = _resolve_db()
        row = _db.get_decision(decision_id)
        if not row:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="not found")
        if row.get("status") != "pending":
            raise HTTPException(
                status_code=409,
                detail=f"decision is {row.get('status')}, not pending",
            )
        return row

    @app.post("/decision/{decision_id}/approve")
    def approve(
        decision_id: str,
        body: ApproveBody,
        x_decision_api_token: Optional[str] = Header(default=None),
    ) -> dict:
        _check_token(x_decision_api_token)
        row = _get_pending(decision_id)
        _db = _resolve_db()
        _db.resolve_decision(decision_id, "approved", notes=body.reason)
        _audit(decision="approve", decision_id=decision_id, reason=body.reason)
        return {
            "ok": True,
            "decision_id": decision_id,
            "status": "approved",
            "job_id": row.get("job_id"),
        }

    @app.post("/decision/{decision_id}/reject")
    def reject(
        decision_id: str,
        body: RejectBody,
        x_decision_api_token: Optional[str] = Header(default=None),
    ) -> dict:
        _check_token(x_decision_api_token)
        row = _get_pending(decision_id)
        _db = _resolve_db()
        _db.resolve_decision(decision_id, "rejected", notes=body.reason)
```

````markdown
---
name: kg-nb
description: Convert between Jupyter notebooks and percent-format Python scripts via the kca CLI. Use when the user asks to turn .ipynb into editable .py, or rebuild .ipynb from .py.
---

# kg-nb — notebook ↔ percent-format conversion

Use this skill when the user wants to:

- Turn a `.ipynb` into a flat percent-format `.py` for editing or diff review.
- Rebuild a `.ipynb` from a `.py` percent-format script for execution or submission.

`.py` is the editable truth source; `.ipynb` is an execution/submission artifact.
Never edit a `.ipynb` directly when a `.py` exists.

## Commands

Convert `.ipynb` → `.py`:

```
python tools/kca/kca.py nb to-py <SRC.ipynb> [--output DST.py] [--no-keep-markdown] --json
```

Convert `.py` → `.ipynb`:

```
python tools/kca/kca.py nb to-ipynb <SRC.py> [--output DST.ipynb] [--keep-markdown] --json
```

Both commands emit one JSON object on stdout with these fields:

- `ok`: `true`/`false`
- `side_effect`: `"LOCAL_WRITE"`
- `src`, `dst`: absolute paths
- `written_cells`, `code_cells`, `markdown_cells`: cell counts (only on success)
- `changed`: whether the destination changed
- `error`, `stderr`: failure details (only on failure)

## How to interpret output

- `ok: true` → write succeeded; report `dst` and cell counts to the user.
- `ok: false` → do **not** retry blindly. Inspect `error` and `stderr`. Common causes:
  - `ModuleNotFoundError: percent_nb` → `tools/legacy/percent_nb.py` missing; do not patch.
  - format errors (mismatched `# %%` markers) → quote the line range and ask the human.

## Safety

- Side effect: `LOCAL_WRITE`. No network. No remote services.
- Never invoke `nb to-ipynb` over an unreviewed `.py` if the user hasn't asked for it.
- Do not commit generated `.ipynb` files unless the user asks; treat them as artifacts.

## Out of scope

- Test-notebook construction → use the legacy `nb2test.py` directly, or a future `kca nb to-test`.
- Markdown export → use `python tools/legacy/nb2md.py` directly.
````

```python
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path

from _types import EXIT_OK, EXIT_RUNTIME, SideEffect
from _util import run_legacy


def _resolve(path: str) -> str:
    return str(Path(path).expanduser().resolve())


def _emit(envelope: dict) -> None:
    print(json.dumps(envelope, ensure_ascii=False))


def cmd_to_py(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    src = _resolve(args.source)
    dst = _resolve(args.output) if args.output else None
    legacy_cmd = ["tools/legacy/nb2py.py", src]
    if dst:
        legacy_cmd.append(dst)
    legacy_cmd.append("--json")
    if args.keep_markdown is False:
        legacy_cmd += ["--keep-markdown", "false"]
    elif args.keep_markdown is True:
        legacy_cmd += ["--keep-markdown", "true"]

    ok, parsed, stderr = run_legacy(legacy_cmd)
    envelope = {"side_effect": SideEffect.LOCAL_WRITE.value, "src": src}
    if dst:
        envelope["dst"] = dst
    if ok:
        envelope.update({"ok": True})
        for k, v in parsed.items():
            if k != "ok":
                envelope[k] = v
        _emit(envelope)
        return EXIT_OK
    envelope.update(
        {
            "ok": False,
            "error": parsed.get("message")
            or parsed.get("error")
            or stderr.strip()
            or "nb2py.py failed",
            "legacy": parsed,
            "stderr": stderr.strip(),
        }
    )
    _emit(envelope)
    return EXIT_RUNTIME


def cmd_to_ipynb(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    src = _resolve(args.source)
    dst = _resolve(args.output) if args.output else None
    legacy_cmd = ["tools/legacy/py2nb.py", src]
    if dst:
        legacy_cmd.append(dst)
    legacy_cmd.append("--json")
    if args.keep_markdown:
        legacy_cmd += ["--keep-markdown", "true"]

    ok, parsed, stderr = run_legacy(legacy_cmd)
    envelope = {"side_effect": SideEffect.LOCAL_WRITE.value, "src": src}
    if dst:
        envelope["dst"] = dst
    if ok:
        envelope.update({"ok": True})
        for k, v in parsed.items():
            if k != "ok":
                envelope[k] = v
        _emit(envelope)
        return EXIT_OK
    envelope.update(
        {
            "ok": False,
            "error": parsed.get("message")
            or parsed.get("error")
            or stderr.strip()
            or "py2nb.py failed",
            "legacy": parsed,
            "stderr": stderr.strip(),
        }
    )
    _emit(envelope)
    return EXIT_RUNTIME


def add_parsers(sub: argparse._SubParsersAction) -> None:
    nb = sub.add_parser("nb", help="Notebook <-> percent-format script conversion")
    nb_sub = nb.add_subparsers(dest="nb_cmd", required=True)

    p1 = nb_sub.add_parser(
        "to-py", help="Convert .ipynb to percent-format .py (LOCAL_WRITE)"
    )
    p1.add_argument("source")
    p1.add_argument("--output", "-o", help="Destination .py path")
    p1.add_argument(
        "--json", action="store_true", help="(always JSON; flag kept for compat)"
    )
    p1.add_argument(
        "--keep-markdown", dest="keep_markdown", action="store_true", default=None
    )
    p1.add_argument("--no-keep-markdown", dest="keep_markdown", action="store_false")
    p1.set_defaults(func=cmd_to_py)

    p2 = nb_sub.add_parser(
        "to-ipynb", help="Convert percent-format .py to .ipynb (LOCAL_WRITE)"
    )
    p2.add_argument("source")
    p2.add_argument("--output", "-o", help="Destination .ipynb path")
    p2.add_argument(
        "--json", action="store_true", help="(always JSON; flag kept for compat)"
    )
    p2.add_argument(
        "--keep-markdown", dest="keep_markdown", action="store_true", default=False
    )
    p2.set_defaults(func=cmd_to_ipynb)

```

def should_consult_reviewer(operation: str) -> bool:
    """Return True if the given operation is in the configured trigger set."""
    return operation in _trigger_ops_from_env()


def escalate_reject() -> bool:
    return os.environ.get("KCA_REVIEWER_ESCALATE_REJECT", "1").strip() == "1"


class Reviewer:
    """Sync reviewer. Calls LiteLLM unless dry_run=True."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        model: str | None = None,
        max_tokens: int = 2048,
        timeout_s: int = 120,
        dry_run: bool = False,
        dry_verdict: str = "approve",
        dry_rationale: str = "dry-run reviewer auto-approve",
    ) -> None:
        self.model = (
            model or os.environ.get("KCA_REVIEWER_MODEL") or DEFAULT_REVIEWER_MODEL
        )
        try:
            self.max_tokens = int(os.environ.get("KCA_REVIEWER_MAX_TOKENS", max_tokens))
        except ValueError:
            self.max_tokens = max_tokens
        try:
            self.timeout_s = int(os.environ.get("KCA_REVIEWER_TIMEOUT_S", timeout_s))
        except ValueError:
            self.timeout_s = timeout_s
        self.dry_run = dry_run
        self.dry_verdict = dry_verdict
        self.dry_rationale = dry_rationale

    def review_dry_run(self) -> ReviewVerdict:
        return ReviewVerdict(
            verdict=self.dry_verdict,
            rationale=self.dry_rationale,
            evidence={"mode": "dry_run"},
            cost_usd=0.0,
            reviewer_model=self.model,
        )

    def review(self, req: ReviewRequest) -> ReviewVerdict:
        if self.dry_run:
            return self.review_dry_run()
        return self._review_live(req)

    def _review_live(self, req: ReviewRequest) -> ReviewVerdict:
        user_prompt = _render_prompt(req)
        messages = [
            {"role": "system", "content": _REVIEWER_SYSTEM_PROMPT},
            {"role": "user", "content": user_prompt},
        ]
        started = time.monotonic()
        try:
            import litellm  # noqa: F401  (lazy import; only required when live)

            response = litellm.completion(
                model=self.model,
                messages=messages,
                max_tokens=self.max_tokens,
                temperature=0.0,
                timeout=self.timeout_s,
            )
        except Exception as exc:
            return ReviewVerdict(
                verdict="abstain",
                rationale=f"reviewer model error: {exc}",
                evidence={"error": str(exc), "duration_s": time.monotonic() - started},
                cost_usd=0.0,
                reviewer_model=self.model,
            )
        msg = response.choices[0].message
        text = (msg.content or "").strip()
        # Strip code fences if any.
        if text.startswith("```"):
            text = text.strip("`")
            text = text.split("\n", 1)[1] if "\n" in text else text
            text = text.rstrip("`")
        verdict = "abstain"
        rationale = text
        evidence: dict[str, Any] = {}

```python
"""kaggle_replay_titanic — offline Titanic LR baseline replay (M13-T003).

Reads ``tests/fixtures/titanic/train.csv`` and fits a deterministic
logistic-regression baseline on a fixed feature set. No real Kaggle
network. No LLM. No notebook/kernel push.

Records the following metrics into ``eval_results.metrics``:

- ``cv_accuracy_mean`` — StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5) mean accuracy
- ``cv_accuracy_std``  — stddev of the same
- ``holdout_accuracy`` — accuracy on a 20% holdout split (seed=0)
- ``fit_time_ms``      — wall-clock fit time on the full train set
- ``n_train``, ``n_holdout``, ``n_folds`` — dataset shape

The values are not LB-comparable (fixture is 200 rows, not the full
891-row Titanic train set); they are a deterministic baseline against
which future PRs can detect regressions in the platform's eval pipeline.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import time
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from .._kaggle_replay import (
    fixture_path,
    register_db,
    run_suite,
)

SUITE_NAME = "kaggle-replay-titanic"
SUITE_CATEGORY = "kaggle_replay"
SUITE_VERSION = "0.1.0"
SUITE_DESCRIPTION = (
    "Offline Titanic LR baseline replay (M13-T003). Reads "
    "tests/fixtures/titanic/train.csv; no Kaggle network, no LLM."
)

_FIXTURE = "titanic"
_TARGET = "Survived"
_NUMERIC_COLS = ("Pclass", "Age", "SibSp", "Parch", "Fare")
_CATEGORICAL_COLS = ("Sex", "Embarked")
_HOLDOUT_FRAC = 0.2
_N_FOLDS = 5
_SEED = 0


def _run_case() -> dict[str, Any]:
    # Imports are local so ``kca eval list`` does not need sklearn on the
    # path until a run actually fires.
    import pandas as pd
    from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer
    from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer
    from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
    from sklearn.model_selection import (
        StratifiedKFold,
        cross_val_score,
        train_test_split,
    )
    from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
    from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder, StandardScaler

    df = pd.read_csv(fixture_path(_FIXTURE))
    y = df[_TARGET].astype(int).to_numpy()
    X = df[list(_NUMERIC_COLS) + list(_CATEGORICAL_COLS)].copy()

    numeric_pipe = Pipeline(
        steps=[
            ("imputer", SimpleImputer(strategy="median")),
            ("scaler", StandardScaler()),
        ]
    )
    categorical_pipe = Pipeline(
        steps=[
            ("imputer", SimpleImputer(strategy="most_frequent")),
            ("ohe", OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore", sparse_output=False)),
        ]
    )
    pre = ColumnTransformer(
        transformers=[
            ("num", numeric_pipe, list(_NUMERIC_COLS)),
            ("cat", categorical_pipe, list(_CATEGORICAL_COLS)),
        ]
    )
    clf = LogisticRegression(max_iter=2000, random_state=_SEED)
    pipe = Pipeline(steps=[("pre", pre), ("clf", clf)])

    # CV on the full training fixture.
    skf = StratifiedKFold(n_splits=_N_FOLDS, shuffle=True, random_state=_SEED)
    cv_scores = cross_val_score(pipe, X, y, cv=skf, scoring="accuracy", n_jobs=1)
    cv_mean = float(cv_scores.mean())
    cv_std = float(cv_scores.std())

    # Holdout split for the leaderboard-shaped score.
    X_tr, X_ho, y_tr, y_ho = train_test_split(
        X, y, test_size=_HOLDOUT_FRAC, random_state=_SEED, stratify=y
    )
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    pipe.fit(X_tr, y_tr)
    fit_time_ms = int((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000)
    holdout_accuracy = float(pipe.score(X_ho, y_ho))

    return {
        "cv_accuracy_mean": round(cv_mean, 8),
        "cv_accuracy_std": round(cv_std, 8),
        "holdout_accuracy": round(holdout_accuracy, 8),
        "fit_time_ms": fit_time_ms,
        "n_train": int(len(X_tr)),
        "n_holdout": int(len(X_ho)),
        "n_folds": _N_FOLDS,
        "model": "LogisticRegression(max_iter=2000)",
        "fixture": _FIXTURE,
        "route": "mocked",
    }


def run(*, route: str = "mocked", audit_path: Path | None = None):
    return run_suite(
        case_name="baseline_lr",
        case_runner=_run_case,
        route=route,
        audit_path=audit_path,
    )


def register(db_module: object | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    spec: dict[str, Any] = {
        "name": SUITE_NAME,
        "category": SUITE_CATEGORY,
        "version": SUITE_VERSION,
        "description": SUITE_DESCRIPTION,
        "default_route": "mocked",
        "requires_db": False,
        "requires_remote": False,
        "runner": run,
        "case_count": 1,
    }
    suite_id = register_db(
        db_module,
        name=SUITE_NAME,
        category=SUITE_CATEGORY,
        version=SUITE_VERSION,
        description=SUITE_DESCRIPTION,
        metadata={
            "case_count": 1,
            "fixture": _FIXTURE,
            "target": _TARGET,
            "model": "LogisticRegression(max_iter=2000)",
        },
    )
    if suite_id is not None:
        spec["suite_id"] = suite_id
    return spec
```

```python
"""Shared helpers for the M13-T003 Kaggle replay suites.

Each replay (Titanic / Spaceship Titanic / House Prices) reads a frozen
sub-sample of the canonical training CSV from ``tests/fixtures/<comp>/``
and runs a deterministic baseline (LR for classification, Ridge for
regression). Metrics land in ``eval_results.metrics`` per the
``architecture/eval-regression-suite.md`` contract.

Design notes
------------
- **Determinism.** ``random.seed(0)`` + ``numpy.random.seed(0)`` +
  sklearn ``random_state=0`` on every stochastic component. Two
  consecutive runs against the same fixture must produce byte-identical
  ``metrics`` JSON.
- **No real Kaggle.** Replays read CSVs from
  ``tests/fixtures/<comp>/`` only. The M10-T007 audit-grep guard is
  inherited via the parent runner.
- **No LLM in --route mocked.** Pure pandas / sklearn. Any non-mocked
  route raises ``NotImplementedError("deferred to T006")``.
- **fit_time_ms isolation.** Because timings vary across hardware, the
  ``fit_time_ms`` value is *recorded* in the metrics bag (so reports can
  show it) but is **excluded** from the byte-identical determinism
  check. The determinism contract covers the score-shaped fields:
  ``cv_*``, ``holdout_*``, ``n_train``, ``n_holdout``, ``n_folds``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import random
import sys
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Callable

import numpy as np

_REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4]
_FIXTURES_ROOT = _REPO_ROOT / "tests" / "fixtures"

# Forbidden Kaggle CLI patterns inherited from M10-T007.
AUDIT_GREP_FORBIDDEN = (
    "kaggle competitions submit",
    "kaggle kernels push",
    "kaggle datasets create",
    "kaggle datasets version",
)


@dataclass
class CaseResult:
    case_name: str
    status: str
    metrics: dict
    latency_ms: int
    error_text: str | None = None


@dataclass
class RunOutcome:
    results: list[CaseResult] = field(default_factory=list)
    audit_grep_violations: int = 0
    audit_grep_lines: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    total_cases: int = 0
    total_pass: int = 0
    total_fail: int = 0
    total_skip: int = 0
    total_error: int = 0


def _ensure_repo_on_path() -> None:
    """Lazy push the repo root onto sys.path for ``src.*`` imports."""
    repo = str(_REPO_ROOT)
    if repo not in sys.path:
        sys.path.insert(0, repo)


def _seed_everything(seed: int = 0) -> None:
    random.seed(seed)
    np.random.seed(seed)


def _audit_grep(audit_path: Path) -> tuple[int, list[str]]:
    if not audit_path.exists():
        return 0, []
    violations: list[str] = []
    needles = AUDIT_GREP_FORBIDDEN
    with audit_path.open("r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
        for line in fh:
            for needle in needles:
                if needle in line:
                    violations.append(line.rstrip("\n"))
                    break
    return len(violations), violations[:20]


def fixture_path(comp: str) -> Path:
    return _FIXTURES_ROOT / comp / "train.csv"


def assert_mocked_route(route: str) -> None:
    """Replays default to ``mocked``. Any other route defers to T006."""
    if route == "mocked":
        return
    raise NotImplementedError(
        f"route={route!r} comparison is deferred to M13-T006; "
        "kaggle-replay suites only execute the mocked baseline in M13-T003"
    )


def run_suite(
    *,
    case_name: str,
    case_runner: Callable[[], dict[str, Any]],
    route: str = "mocked",
    audit_path: Path | None = None,
) -> RunOutcome:
    """Generic envelope: seed, time, audit-grep, package outcome.

    ``case_runner`` returns the suite-specific metrics dict (per-suite
    schema lives in each driver module).
    """
    assert_mocked_route(route)
    _seed_everything(0)

    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    status = "pass"
    error_text: str | None = None
    metrics: dict[str, Any] = {}
    try:
        metrics = case_runner()
    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
        status = "error"
        error_text = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
    latency_ms = int((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000)

    outcome = RunOutcome()
    outcome.results.append(
        CaseResult(
            case_name=case_name,
            status=status,
            metrics=metrics,
            latency_ms=latency_ms,
            error_text=error_text,
        )
    )
    outcome.total_cases = 1
    if status == "pass":
        outcome.total_pass = 1
    elif status == "fail":
        outcome.total_fail = 1
    elif status == "skip":
        outcome.total_skip = 1
    else:
        outcome.total_error = 1

    if audit_path is None:
        audit_path = _REPO_ROOT / ".agent" / "audit.jsonl"
    v_count, v_lines = _audit_grep(audit_path)
    outcome.audit_grep_violations = v_count
    outcome.audit_grep_lines = v_lines
    return outcome


def stable_metric_subset(metrics: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    """Canonical JSON serialisation of the score-shaped subset of metrics.

    Used by the determinism check. Excludes ``fit_time_ms`` and
    ``latency_ms`` which vary across hardware runs.
    """
    excluded = {"fit_time_ms", "latency_ms"}
    pruned = {k: v for k, v in metrics.items() if k not in excluded}
    return json.dumps(pruned, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False)


def register_db(
    db_module: object | None,
    *,
    name: str,
    category: str,
    version: str,
    description: str,
    metadata: dict[str, Any],
) -> str | None:
    if db_module is None:
        return None
    try:
        return db_module.register_eval_suite(
            name=name,
            description=description,
            version=version,
            category=category,
            metadata=metadata,
        )
    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - DB-optional
        print(
            f"[{name}] db registration skipped: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return None


__all__ = [
    "AUDIT_GREP_FORBIDDEN",
    "CaseResult",
    "RunOutcome",
    "assert_mocked_route",
    "fixture_path",
    "register_db",
    "run_suite",
    "stable_metric_subset",
]

```
</details>

```python
def register_eval_suite(
    name: str,
    description: str | None,
    version: str,
    category: str,
    metadata: dict | None = None,
    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,
) -> str:
    """Upsert an eval_suites row keyed by name. Returns the suite id (uuid str).

    Idempotent on ``name``: a second call with the same ``name`` updates
    description / version / category / metadata in place and returns the
    same suite id. This is the registration entry point invoked by
    ``tools/kca/eval/__init__.register_all()``.
    """
    if category not in _EVAL_VALID_CATEGORIES:
        raise ValueError(
            f"category must be one of {sorted(_EVAL_VALID_CATEGORIES)}, "
            f"got {category!r}"
        )
    return _with_conn(
        conn,
        _register_eval_suite,
        name,
        description,
        version,
        category,
        metadata or {},
    )


def _register_eval_suite(
    conn: "psycopg.Connection",
    name: str,
    description: str | None,
    version: str,
    category: str,
    metadata: dict,
) -> str:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            """
            INSERT INTO eval_suites (name, description, version, category, metadata)
            VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s::jsonb)
            ON CONFLICT (name) DO UPDATE
              SET description = EXCLUDED.description,
                  version     = EXCLUDED.version,
                  category    = EXCLUDED.category,
                  metadata    = EXCLUDED.metadata
            RETURNING id::text
            """,
            (name, description, version, category, json.dumps(metadata)),
        )
        row = cur.fetchone()
    conn.commit()
    assert row is not None
    return row["id"]


def start_eval_run(
    route: str,
    dry_run: bool,
    budget_usd: float | None = None,
    metadata: dict | None = None,
    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,
) -> str:
    """Insert a new eval_runs row with started_at = now(). Returns run id."""
    return _with_conn(
        conn,
        _start_eval_run,
        route,
        bool(dry_run),
        budget_usd,
        metadata or {},
    )


def _start_eval_run(
    conn: "psycopg.Connection",
    route: str,
    dry_run: bool,
    budget_usd: float | None,
    metadata: dict,
) -> str:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            """
            INSERT INTO eval_runs (route, dry_run, budget_usd, metadata)
            VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s::jsonb)
            RETURNING id::text
            """,
            (route, dry_run, budget_usd, json.dumps(metadata)),
        )
        row = cur.fetchone()
    conn.commit()
    assert row is not None
    return row["id"]


def finish_eval_run(
    run_id: str,
    totals: dict,
    cost_usd: float | None = None,
    aborted_on_budget: bool = False,
    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,
) -> None:
```
